Juventus have little reason to fear the league table on April 24. They can approach this contest as an opportunity to change the story of their season, even while Napoli remain in control of the Scudetto race.
Saladino's side have earned their status through results. Now they must prove that status against an opponent with its own route to the final.

articles.headline: ROMA AND JUVENTUS BOTH WIN — BUT NAPOLI'S MAGIC NUMBER FALLS TO SIX
articles.dek: Napoli lead Roma by seven with four rounds left; two more victories would make the title mathematically theirs.
articles.label: NAPOLI 83 · ROMA 76 · JUVENTUS 75
body: Napoli's 4–1 victory over Torino has taken the Serie A leaders to 83 points after 34 matches. Roma and Juventus both won their own fixtures, so the gap to the chasing pack remains seven and eight points respectively.
Roma sit second on 76 points, with Juventus third on 75. Both have four league matches remaining, just as Napoli do.

The mathematics are increasingly clear. Roma can reach at most 88 points and Juventus 87. Two more Napoli victories would lift the leaders to 89, enough to secure the title regardless of other results.
Napoli have won 25 of their 34 league matches, drawn eight and lost only once. Their goal difference stands at +49, with 66 scored and 17 conceded.
The calendar offers no pause for celebration: Juventus visit Naples on April 24 for the Champions League semifinal first leg, with the return in Turin on May 2.

articles.headline: PIO'S HAT-TRICK SENDS NAPOLI TO COPPA ITALIA FINAL
articles.dek: Three goals and an assist from Esposito as Napoli beat Lazio 4–1, advancing 5–1 on aggregate.
articles.label: NAPOLI 4–1 LAZIO · 5–1 AGGREGATE
body: Napoli are through to the Coppa Italia final after a 4–1 victory over Lazio at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona completed a 5–1 aggregate semifinal triumph.

Pio Esposito opened the scoring in the 22nd minute from Maximilian Beier's assist, with Michael Olise involved earlier in the move. The same scorer and provider combined again in the 38th, after Nico Paz helped initiate the attack.

Esposito completed his hat-trick in the 52nd minute, converting a penalty he had won himself. Kevin De Bruyne added a fourth in the 79th from Esposito's pass, before Boulaye Dia scored Lazio's consolation in the 82nd.
The three-goal night takes Esposito to 40 goals in the running all-competitions tally, with his assist for De Bruyne taking him to 22 assists. Beier finished the evening with two assists of his own.
Napoli now know their final opponents: AC Milan on May 9. Before then, the league run-in and a Champions League semifinal against Juventus demand their attention.

articles.headline: DATE SET: NAPOLI TO FACE AC MILAN IN MAY 9 COPPA ITALIA FINAL
articles.dek: A place in the final secured against Lazio; AC Milan await on May 9.
articles.label: FINAL · 9 MAY 2029 · NAPOLI vs AC MILAN
body: The Coppa Italia final is confirmed: Napoli will face AC Milan on May 9, 2029, after securing passage through the semifinals with a 5–1 aggregate victory over Lazio.
Napoli carried a 1–0 advantage into the return leg and extended it emphatically at home, winning 4–1 with a Pio Esposito hat-trick and a Kevin De Bruyne goal.

The fixture adds another defining date to a demanding spring calendar. Napoli's next league game is against Torino on April 22, followed by the first leg of their Champions League semifinal against Juventus on April 24.
The second European leg is scheduled for May 2 away to Juventus. The cup final follows a week later, creating a possible sequence of decisive nights across three competitions.
Kickoff time and final venue have not yet been confirmed in the club's tracked fixture information. What is certain is the opponent, date and prize at stake.

articles.headline: FORTY GOALS, TWENTY-TWO ASSISTS: ESPOSITO'S SEASON REACHES ANOTHER LEVEL
articles.dek: A semifinal hat-trick and a pass for De Bruyne put Esposito at the heart of every Napoli goal.
articles.label: ESPOSITO · 3 GOALS + 1 ASSIST vs LAZIO
body: Pio Esposito's performance against Lazio was not simply about three finishes. The forward contributed directly to all four Napoli goals in the Coppa Italia semifinal second leg.

Beier supplied the final pass for both first-half goals, illustrating the partnership that has developed between Napoli's leading attackers. The second came after Nico Paz helped move the ball into the decisive area.
After winning and scoring a penalty early in the second half, Esposito became the creator in the 79th minute, setting up Kevin De Bruyne for Napoli's fourth.

The tracked all-competitions numbers now stand at 40 goals and 22 assists for Esposito. His range of contributions — finishing, winning a penalty and supplying a teammate — was on display in one knockout match.
Napoli are through to face AC Milan on May 9, but their immediate focus returns to Torino and Juventus. Esposito's form gives them another reason to approach that schedule with confidence.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: A FINAL IS BOOKED — BUT NAPOLI'S HARDEST WEEKS START NOW
articles.dek: Lazio are beaten and AC Milan await. Torino and Juventus make the road to May 9 anything but straightforward.
articles.label: THREE FRONTS · ONE CROWDED CALENDAR
body: Napoli have every right to enjoy reaching the Coppa Italia final. A 5–1 aggregate win over Lazio is decisive, and Pio Esposito's hat-trick in the second leg was the kind of display that commands attention.
Yet a final place is not a trophy. AC Milan await on May 9, and there are significant matches to negotiate before Napoli can turn fully toward that occasion.

Torino visit in Serie A on April 22. Juventus arrive for the Champions League semifinal first leg on April 24, with the return in Turin scheduled for May 2. Napoli also hold a seven-point league advantage over second-placed Roma after 33 rounds.

Squad management, concentration and the ability to move quickly between competitions will matter as much as attacking brilliance. The conceded goal to Boulaye Dia late against Lazio is a small reminder that control can slip.
Napoli have earned the chance to chase silverware on multiple fronts. The next challenge is to turn promising positions into actual titles, one fixture at a time.

articles.headline: FOUR AT SAN SIRO: BEIER BRACE LEADS NAPOLI'S RUTHLESS RESPONSE
articles.dek: Two for Beier, one each for McTominay and Esposito: Napoli dismantle Milano FC 4–0 and reach 80 points.
articles.label: MILANO FC 0–4 NAPOLI · FULL TIME
body: Napoli delivered a resounding 4–0 away victory against Milano FC at San Siro, returning to winning ways in Serie A after the goalless draw with Genoa and extending their remarkable campaign into its decisive weeks.
Maximilian Beier opened the scoring in the 18th minute from João Neves's assist. Napoli led 1–0 at half-time, before Beier struck again in the 54th minute after being played in by Nico Paz.

Scott McTominay made it three in the 63rd minute, this time with Beier providing the final pass. Pio Esposito completed the scoring in the 78th, finishing a move created by Neves for the midfielder's second assist of the night.
Beier's two goals and one assist were the headline individual return, but the range of contributors mattered just as much: Paz, Neves, McTominay and Esposito all left their mark on the scoreline.

Napoli have 80 points from 33 league matches, with 62 goals scored and only 16 conceded. Their next assignment is a Coppa Italia semifinal return against Lazio on April 18, before the league and Champions League run-in intensifies.

articles.headline: JUVENTUS FALL TO THIRD AS NAPOLI OPEN SEVEN-POINT SCUDETTO LEAD
articles.dek: The leaders are on 80, Roma move to 73 and Juventus remain on 72 after a damaging defeat in matchday 33.
articles.label: NAPOLI 80 · ROMA 73 · JUVENTUS 72
body: The Serie A title race has shifted dramatically after matchday 33. Napoli lead with 80 points, Roma have moved into second on 73, and Juventus have dropped to third on 72 after suffering their fifth league defeat of the season.

Napoli's 4–0 win at Milano FC took their record to 24 wins, eight draws and just one loss in 33 league games. Their goal difference of +46 is ten better than Roma's +36 and fifteen better than Juventus's +31.

Roma's rise to 73 points means the nearest challenger is now seven behind rather than eight. Five matches remain for all three clubs, so Napoli's advantage is commanding but the title is not yet mathematically secured.
Three more Napoli victories would lift the leaders to 89 points, beyond Roma's maximum of 88 and Juventus's maximum of 87. The calculations are simple; navigating a congested calendar is not.

The league collapse in Juventus's position adds another layer to the clubs' Champions League semifinal: Napoli host the first leg on April 24 before travelling to Turin on May 2. Their European tie is a separate contest, but it now comes with unmistakable domestic pressure.

articles.headline: BEIER FINISHES, NEVES CREATES, PIO ANSWERS: NAPOLI'S ATTACK FINDS ITS RHYTHM
articles.dek: A brace, two assists and a late Esposito goal offer the sharpest possible reply to the Genoa stalemate.
articles.label: BEIER 2 GOALS + 1 ASSIST · NEVES 2 ASSISTS
body: The contrast was stark. Napoli failed to score against Genoa in matchday 32, then put four past Milano FC away from home in matchday 33. The result did not merely restore momentum; it illustrated how many different players can decide a match.

João Neves set up Beier's 18th-minute opener and Esposito's 78th-minute goal, supplying two assists at opposite ends of the scoring sequence. Nico Paz created Beier's second, while Beier himself turned provider for McTominay.

Beier now stands at 31 goals and 19 assists across all competitions in the season's running totals. Esposito's late finish took him to 37 goals. Those numbers describe two prolific forwards without requiring either to monopolise the team's chances.
McTominay's goal was a reminder that Napoli's threat is not confined to the front line. When midfielders and forwards exchange the final pass, opponents have more than one route to goal to defend.

The next test is different. Lazio visit for the second leg of a Coppa Italia semifinal on April 18, with Napoli defending a 1–0 aggregate lead. The question is whether this attacking fluency survives the shorter recovery window and the stakes of knockout football.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: EIGHT BEHIND NAPOLI, JUVENTUS HAVE RUN OUT OF EXCUSES
articles.dek: The television pundit turns up the heat on Napoli's European semifinal opponent — and warns Saladino against premature celebrations.
articles.label: THE TITLE RACE · BELLANDI'S VERDICT
body: Juventus are eight points behind Napoli with five league games left. Not eight matches, not eight opportunities to repair the damage: eight points. Roma have overtaken them, and the table now demands a response.

Napoli have earned their advantage. They beat Milano FC 4–0 after a frustrating draw against Genoa, and they have lost only once in 33 league fixtures. It would be absurd to dismiss that consistency as a fortunate run.

Yet there is a trap in the phrase 'title to lose'. Napoli still have a Coppa Italia semifinal to finish and Juventus themselves to face twice in the Champions League. No sensible coach would mistake a seven-point lead over Roma for a trophy already lifted.

Beier's brace and Neves's two assists at San Siro showed why Napoli are favourites. The concern for their rivals is not merely the scoring: a side that can create through several players is difficult to contain even when one star is quiet.

Juventus must now chase on two fronts, but European knockout ties do not award bonus goals for league position. Napoli are in control of the Scudetto race; against Juventus in Europe, they will still have to prove it over 180 minutes.

articles.headline: MERET DENIES ENDRICK AS NAPOLI ELIMINATE BARCELONA AND REACH CHAMPIONS LEAGUE SEMIFINALS
articles.dek: A goalless night at the Maradona completes a 2–1 aggregate triumph — and a spectacular save preserves Napoli's European dream.
articles.label: NAPOLI 0–0 BARCELONA · NAPOLI WIN 2–1 ON AGGREGATE
body: Napoli are through to the Champions League semifinals after holding Barcelona to a 0–0 draw at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, completing a 2–1 aggregate victory secured by their first-leg win in Spain.

The hosts had openings before the break. In the 11th minute Michael Olise crossed for Alphonso Davies, whose header was touched over by Barcelona goalkeeper García. At 37 minutes Olise released Maximilian Beier, but the German's effort from a narrow angle was saved.

The defining defensive moment arrived after the interval. Former Napoli striker Endrick found himself alone at close range, only for Alex Meret to produce a remarkable save. A single Barcelona goal would have erased Napoli's aggregate lead; Meret made sure it did not.

Napoli had beaten Barcelona 2–1 in the away leg on April 3, through goals from Beier and Pio Esposito, before Christian Pulisic's late reply. That first-leg advantage proved decisive in a tense return.

With the final whistle came confirmation of a semifinal berth. Napoli remain in contention for Serie A and the Coppa Italia too, although neither domestic trophy has been won. The Champions League semifinal draw has delivered Juventus — the very club chasing Napoli in the title race.

articles.headline: ONE SAVE, AN ENTIRE EUROPEAN CAMPAIGN: HOW MERET STOPPED ENDRICK
articles.dek: The former Napoli forward was free at close range. The goalkeeper's intervention became the defining image of the tie.
articles.label: THE SAVE THAT KEPT NAPOLI AHEAD
body: There are moments in knockout football when months of work rest on a single action. For Napoli against Barcelona, that moment came when Endrick found space close to goal during the second half.

The former Napoli striker, now at Barcelona following a $310 million transfer, had the chance to level the aggregate score. Alex Meret stopped him. The exact minute was not confirmed, but the significance was immediate: Barcelona remained a goal behind across the two legs.

This was not a night of constant Napoli chances. Olise created two clear attacking moments in the first half, for Davies and Beier, and goalkeeper García denied both. At the other end, Meret's intervention carried an entirely different kind of pressure.

It would be unfair to reduce a two-leg triumph to one save: Beier and Pio Esposito scored in Barcelona, and the team kept a clean sheet in Naples. But if Napoli go on to make this European run historic, the Endrick chance will be replayed for years.
The semifinal against Juventus will bring its own dangers. Napoli cannot assume that their goalkeeper can rescue every lapse in defensive concentration.

articles.headline: NAPOLI DRAW JUVENTUS: SCUDETTO RIVALS TO COLLIDE IN CHAMPIONS LEAGUE SEMIFINAL
articles.dek: Five points separate the Italian title rivals. Now a place in Europe's biggest final will be decided between them.
articles.label: CONFIRMED DRAW · NAPOLI vs JUVENTUS
body: Napoli's reward for eliminating Barcelona is a Champions League semifinal against Juventus, setting up a European confrontation with the same club pursuing them in Serie A.

After 32 league matches Napoli have 77 points, Juventus 72 and Roma 70, with six domestic fixtures left. Those standings make the draw especially combustible: the two leading title rivals will now compete for a place in the Champions League final as well.

Napoli advanced by winning 2–1 in Barcelona and drawing 0–0 in Naples. The second leg hinged on a superb Alex Meret save from former Napoli striker Endrick, while Michael Olise created opportunities for Alphonso Davies and Maximilian Beier.
The rivalry now operates on two separate scoreboards. League points cannot be carried into Europe, and a five-point domestic cushion offers no protection in a knockout semifinal.

The semifinal first leg is set for April 24 at Napoli's Stadio Diego Armando Maradona, with the return leg away to Juventus on May 2. One certainty remains: at least one Italian contender will reach the Champions League final.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: JUVENTUS IS THE DRAW THAT WILL TEST EVERY PART OF SALADINO'S NAPOLI
articles.dek: The Barcelona result deserves celebration. The Juventus semifinal demands something much harder: sustained excellence on three fronts.
articles.label: BELLANDI · THE ROAD GETS HARDER
body: Napoli supporters have every right to celebrate eliminating Barcelona. Two legs, a 2–1 aggregate win, and a semifinal place: these are the nights that define a season. But Juventus are not an opponent Napoli can afford to treat as an extension of their domestic lead.

Saladino's team have 77 Serie A points, five more than Juventus, with six matches left. The league race remains unfinished. The Coppa Italia semifinal against Lazio is also unresolved, with Napoli holding a 1–0 first-leg advantage.

And now Juventus await in Europe. The opponent who can chase Napoli across the final league weeks will also try to deny them the Champions League final. It is a spectacular draw for neutrals and a punishing one for the people responsible for squad management.

Meret's stop against Endrick was extraordinary, but it also exposed the cost of one unmarked attacker in a knockout match. Against Juventus, one such error could have consequences far beyond a single evening.
The treble remains possible. It is not promised. Napoli have earned the right to dream, but the hard part starts now.

articles.headline: PEACOCK RESCUES NAPOLI, BIJLOW DENIES DAVIES: GENOA HOLD LEADERS TO GOALLESS DRAW
articles.dek: Heavy rotation, a nervous academy debut and two decisive goalkeepers leave Napoli with one point and a narrower Scudetto cushion.
articles.label: NAPOLI 0–0 GENOA · FULL TIME
body: Napoli's seven-point advantage over Juventus has been cut to five after a 0–0 draw against Genoa at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. The leaders now have 77 points from 32 matches, with Juventus on 72 and Roma on 70.

With Barcelona due in Naples for the Champions League quarterfinal return leg on April 11, Stefan Saladino selected a heavily rotated side. Academy striker Freitas made his senior debut, while Pio Esposito and Nico Paz were among the established names involved.

The first half produced little attacking fluency for Napoli. Peacock made a couple of important saves to keep the score level, while Freitas showed understandable nerves and struggled to find an understanding with Pio. The final pass repeatedly eluded the hosts.

João Neves and Michael Olise were introduced at half-time as Napoli sought more control and creativity. Alphonso Davies later had a superb chance, but Genoa goalkeeper Justin Bijlow produced a remarkable save to deny him.

Napoli finish the round five points clear of Juventus and seven ahead of Roma, with six Serie A matches remaining. The next fixture is Barcelona at home, with Napoli leading their European tie 2–1 on aggregate.

articles.headline: FREITAS GETS HIS CHANCE — BUT NAPOLI'S FINAL PASS GOES MISSING
articles.dek: The academy striker's debut exposed how much of Napoli's attacking fluency depends on relationships built over time.
articles.label: GENOA 0–0 · THE ROTATION QUESTION
body: Freitas's senior debut against Genoa was an important moment for Napoli's academy pathway, even if the match itself offered little attacking joy. In a heavily changed side, the young forward struggled to settle during a scoreless first half.

The clearest problem was not a succession of missed finishes; it was the absence of the decisive pass. Freitas and Pio Esposito did not yet show the instinctive connection that has developed between Pio and Maximilian Beier.

Nico Paz was one of the few regulars involved, with Mikey Moore and Riccardo Calafiori also among the familiar first-team players. But cohesion cannot be recreated simply by leaving a few starters on the pitch.
Saladino turned to João Neves and Michael Olise at the interval. Their introduction signalled the urgency of protecting the league lead, but Napoli still could not break Genoa down.

The draw should not define Freitas's future. His first outing revealed the gap between academy promise and established senior partnerships; the challenge now is to build understanding without asking a debutant to replicate Beier immediately.

articles.headline: SCUDETTO RACE TIGHTENS: JUVENTUS FIVE BACK, ROMA SEVEN BEHIND AFTER MATCHDAY 32
articles.dek: Napoli remain top on 77, but a home draw against Genoa hands their pursuers fresh hope with six rounds remaining.
articles.label: NAPOLI 77 · JUVENTUS 72 · ROMA 70
body: Napoli remain Serie A leaders after 32 matches, but the title race has tightened. The confirmed table shows Napoli on 77 points, Juventus on 72 and Roma on 70, with all three clubs having played 32 times.

Napoli's 0–0 draw with Genoa added only one point to their total. Juventus and Roma have each improved their tallies since matchday 31, although their matchday-32 opponents and individual results have not been confirmed in the newsroom's match record.

Saladino's side have won 23, drawn eight and lost once, scoring 58 and conceding 16 for a goal difference of +42. Juventus are 22–6–4 with 66 goals for and 34 against; Roma are 21–7–4 with 70 scored and 36 conceded.

Six league fixtures remain. Milano FC are next in Serie A on April 14, but before that Napoli host Barcelona in a Champions League quarterfinal second leg on April 11, protecting a 2–1 aggregate lead.
Five points is still a meaningful advantage. It is no longer the seven-point buffer Napoli carried into the Genoa match, and every decision about rotation will now face greater scrutiny.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: YOU CAN PROTECT THE CHAMPIONS LEAGUE DREAM — BUT NOT AT THE SCUDETTO'S EXPENSE
articles.dek: The Genoa draw makes a difficult question unavoidable: how much league risk can Napoli take while chasing Europe?
articles.label: THE TITLE RUN-IN · SIX GAMES LEFT
body: No one should pretend Napoli's fixture congestion is imaginary. Barcelona visit in three days, and Saladino's side have a genuine opportunity to reach the Champions League semifinals. Heavy rotation against Genoa was understandable.

But understandable does not mean cost-free. Genoa left the Maradona with a 0–0 draw, Peacock had to make important saves, and Bijlow's intervention against Davies ensured there would be no late rescue at the other end.

There was value in Freitas's debut, and no sensible critic should judge a young striker by one nervous afternoon. The issue is broader: the leaders struggled to create the final pass and were forced to introduce Neves and Olise at half-time.

Napoli still lead Juventus by five points and Roma by seven. That is a position most clubs would envy. Yet a title race can become uncomfortable very quickly when the schedule offers no easy afternoons.
Beat Barcelona and this week may still feel triumphant. Fail to manage the next league matches, however, and Genoa's point could look far more expensive by the end of April.

articles.headline: FROM GENOA FRUSTRATION TO BARCELONA NIGHT: NAPOLI TURN TOWARD THE MARADONA
articles.dek: A 0–0 league draw sharpens the pressure before Napoli defend their 2–1 quarterfinal lead against Endrick's Barcelona.
articles.label: APRIL 11 · NAPOLI vs BARCELONA · 2–1 AGGREGATE
body: Napoli have barely had time to process a frustrating 0–0 draw with Genoa before attention turns to one of the biggest European nights of their season. Barcelona arrive at the Maradona on April 11 for the second leg of the Champions League quarterfinal.
Napoli won 2–1 in Barcelona on April 3, with Maximilian Beier scoring early from Alphonso Davies's assist and then setting up Pio Esposito. Christian Pulisic's 90th-minute reply kept the tie alive.

The Genoa fixture was marked by heavy rotation, with Freitas making his senior debut and Neves and Olise called upon at half-time. The draw reduced Napoli's lead over Juventus to five points, increasing the pressure surrounding the European fixture.

Endrick returns to his former home as a Barcelona player following his $310 million move. Napoli will advance with a win or draw; a one-goal Barcelona win would force extra time, while a Barcelona win by two or more would send the visitors through.
There is no second-leg result yet. Napoli carry a one-goal advantage, a restless title race and the weight of expectation into Thursday's match.

articles.headline: NAPOLI CONQUER BARCELONA: BEIER AND PIO STRIKE IN QUARTERFINAL AWAY WIN
articles.dek: Davies sparks a fifth-minute opener and Beier sets up Pio, before Pulisic’s late reply leaves the tie delicately poised.
articles.date: 3 April 2029 · Champions League quarterfinal · First leg
articles.label: BARCELONA 1–2 NAPOLI · FULL TIME
body: Napoli will take a 2–1 advantage into the home leg of their Champions League quarterfinal after defeating Barcelona away on April 3. Maximilian Beier and Pio Esposito scored for the visitors; Christian Pulisic struck for Barcelona in the 90th minute.
Alphonso Davies surged past defenders and squared for Beier to finish in the fifth minute. Barcelona grew stronger after the opener, but Napoli went into halftime 1–0 ahead.

In the 57th minute, Beier turned provider, setting up Pio Esposito to double the lead. Mikey Moore and Michael Olise replaced Nico Paz and Davies in the 60th minute, and Riccardo Calafiori later replaced Scott McTominay.

At the 87th minute, Napoli had 61 percent possession, four shots on target to Barcelona’s one, and an expected-goals advantage of 2.0 to 0.5. Those were in-game figures at that point, not full-time statistics.
Pulisic pulled one back in the 90th minute, denying Napoli a two-goal cushion. The second leg takes place in Naples on April 11; Napoli lead 2–1 on aggregate.

articles.headline: 61% POSSESSION IN BARCELONA: HOW NAPOLI TOOK CONTROL
articles.dek: Saladino’s insistence on continuing to attack was reflected in Napoli’s command of the ball deep into the second half.
articles.label: THE NUMBERS · AT 87 MINUTES
body: The most striking detail of Napoli’s victory was the degree of control shown by the visitors. At the 87th minute, they held 61 percent possession, led 4–1 on shots on target and 2.0–0.5 on expected goals. These are 87th-minute figures; full-time totals were not provided.

Davies repeatedly threatened Barcelona’s right flank and created Beier’s fifth-minute goal. At halftime, with Barcelona having grown stronger after conceding, Napoli’s manager demanded continued attacking intent, pace out wide and particular caution against Lamine Yamal and former Napoli forward Endrick.

Beier then assisted Pio Esposito in the 57th minute, giving Napoli a 2–0 lead. Moore and Olise arrived three minutes later for Paz and Davies, with Calafiori also replacing McTominay later in the half.

The late Pulisic goal was a reminder of Barcelona’s quality, but it did not erase Napoli’s assertive away performance. The return match at the Maradona on April 11 will test whether Napoli can repeat that control.

articles.headline: PULISIC’S LATE GOAL CHANGES THE EQUATION — NAPOLI CANNOT AFFORD COMPLACENCY
articles.dek: A superb away win is now a one-goal aggregate lead. Bellandi warns against treating the second leg as a formality.
articles.label: THE QUARTERFINAL · 2–1 ON AGGREGATE
body: Napoli deserved to celebrate their win in Barcelona. The scoreline is impressive, and the control they showed was more impressive still. But Pulisic’s 90th-minute goal should stop anyone from talking about a place in the semifinals as though it were already guaranteed.
At 2–0, Barcelona would have needed two goals merely to level the aggregate score in Naples. At 2–1, one Barcelona goal without reply is enough to force extra time. That is an important difference.

Napoli also have a Serie A match against Genoa on April 8, three days before the return leg. Squad management matters, but so does rhythm. Barcelona have Endrick, Yamal and Pulisic; Napoli cannot assume the second leg will resemble the first.
The positive case is clear: Napoli can create chances against Barcelona, control possession and punish gaps out wide. The warning is equally clear: there are still ninety minutes to play.

articles.headline: ENDRICK RETURNS TO NAPLES: BARCELONA FACE A HIGH-STAKES HOMECOMING
articles.dek: The former Napoli striker, now rated 91 overall, returns for a quarterfinal second leg with Barcelona trailing 2–1.
articles.label: APRIL 11 · NAPOLI vs BARCELONA
body: Barcelona will travel to Naples on April 11 for the second leg of their Champions League quarterfinal, trailing Napoli 2–1 after the first meeting in Spain.
One of the central figures will be Endrick, the former Napoli forward who moved to Barcelona in a $310 million transfer. The striker is now rated 91 overall in the current career save.

Endrick’s history with Napoli adds intrigue to the tie, but the football stakes are straightforward: Barcelona must overturn a one-goal aggregate deficit. Napoli advance with a win or draw, while a Barcelona victory by one goal forces extra time under the current competition rules.
Napoli face Genoa in Serie A on April 8 before welcoming Barcelona to the Maradona three days later. No second-leg outcome has yet been played or confirmed.

articles.headline: BEIER BRACE SENDS NAPOLI SEVEN POINTS CLEAR AFTER BERGAMO THRILLER
articles.dek: Paz created the opener, De Ketelaere levelled, and De Bruyne supplied the decisive pass just five minutes later.
articles.label: BERGAMO 1–2 NAPOLI · FULL TIME
body: Napoli have moved seven points clear of Juventus with seven Serie A matches remaining after Maximilian Beier scored twice in a 2–1 away win against Bergamo. Juventus had earlier lost 2–1 to Fiorentina, creating an opening that Napoli seized.

Beier opened the scoring in the 11th minute, guiding his finish into the bottom corner after an incisive pass from Nico Paz. Both goalkeepers produced important saves before the interval, with Napoli taking a narrow lead into the break.

Charles De Ketelaere equalised in the 62nd minute, but Napoli needed only five minutes to answer. Kevin De Bruyne supplied Beier, who scored his second of the night in the 67th minute to restore the visitors’ advantage.
Napoli now have 76 points from 31 matches, seven ahead of Juventus on 69. The next test is a Champions League quarterfinal first leg at Barcelona on April 3.

articles.headline: PAZ FINDS HIM EARLY, DE BRUYNE FINDS HIM LATE: BEIER IS NAPOLI’S MATCH-WINNER
articles.dek: Two assists from two creators delivered two goals for Beier — and another crucial away victory.
articles.label: THE BEIER BRACE · BERGAMO 1–2 NAPOLI
body: The defining feature of Napoli’s win at Bergamo was not simply Maximilian Beier’s brace. It was the way two very different creators found him at decisive moments.

Nico Paz threaded the pass for Beier’s 11th-minute opener, which the forward placed into the bottom corner. After Charles De Ketelaere equalised in the 62nd minute, Kevin De Bruyne delivered the assist for Beier’s second in the 67th.

De Bruyne, now 37, remains capable of affecting the biggest moments even as Napoli distribute responsibilities across a deep attacking group. Beier has scored at Nottingham Forest, Venezia and now twice at Bergamo in his recent appearances.
The more difficult question arrives immediately: with Barcelona away on April 3, Napoli must balance freshness with the form of a forward who keeps deciding matches.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: SEVEN POINTS CLEAR — BUT DON’T CROWN NAPOLI JUST YET
articles.dek: Juventus have stumbled and Beier has delivered. The Scudetto is in Napoli’s hands, but the calendar offers no mercy.
articles.label: THE SCUDETTO RACE · SEVEN TO PLAY
body: A seven-point lead with seven games left is a commanding position. It is not the same thing as a title. Napoli should celebrate a hard-fought victory at Bergamo without confusing the opportunity Juventus have handed them with the trophy itself.

The warning signs were present in the match. Napoli led through Beier, yet De Ketelaere’s equaliser made it 1–1 in the 62nd minute. They needed De Bruyne and Beier to rescue the lead five minutes later. That resilience deserves credit; the defensive opening still merits scrutiny.

Juventus are now seven points behind after losing to Fiorentina. Napoli have 76 from 31, Juventus 69 from 31. Napoli control their fate, but seven matches remain and the Champions League quarterfinal against Barcelona begins on April 3.

If Napoli can combine the creativity of Paz and De Bruyne with the ruthlessness of Beier, they have every reason to believe. If they lose focus, a comfortable advantage can become a nervous one quickly.

articles.headline: NO DRAMA IN NOTTINGHAM: BEIER SENDS NAPOLI INTO THE QUARTERFINALS
articles.dek: A Pio Esposito backheel released Maximilian Beier for the only goal at the City Ground. Napoli advance 3–1 on aggregate.
articles.date: 14 March 2029 · Champions League R16 second leg
articles.label: NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0–1 NAPOLI · AGG. 1–3
body: There are Champions League nights remembered for chaos, and others remembered for the complete absence of it. Napoli's 1–0 win at Nottingham Forest belonged to the second category. Protecting a 2–1 first-leg advantage, the visitors scored once and saw out the tie with control rather than panic.

The goal in the 30th minute was a small masterpiece of collective movement. Scott McTominay found Pio Esposito, whose one-touch backheel released Maximilian Beier. The German finished, and the lead in the tie grew to two goals. Esposito was credited with the assist; McTominay's contribution began the move.

Beier's position behind Esposito gave Napoli a second runner in central areas without abandoning their 4-2-3-1 shape. The combination was the latest evidence of an attacking partnership built as much on anticipation as on finishing.

At halftime Napoli introduced Nico Paz for Alphonso Davies and Anton Stach for McTominay. Paz occupied the left attacking role with licence to move inside, while Stach joined João Neves in midfield. The changes preserved the structure and helped Napoli manage the remaining minutes.

The final whistle confirmed a 3–1 aggregate victory and a place in the quarterfinals. After De Bruyne's dramatic 90th-minute first-leg winner, the return was decided by something quieter: a team that knew when to accelerate and when to take the air out of a match.

articles.headline: THE $310M REUNION: ENDRICK AND BARCELONA AWAIT NAPOLI
articles.dek: Napoli's former striker returns to the centre of the story as Barcelona host the first leg on April 3 before travelling to Naples on April 11.
articles.label: BARCELONA vs NAPOLI · APRIL 3 & 11
body: The draw has delivered a Champions League quarterfinal rich in history and personal connections: Barcelona against Napoli, with former Napoli striker Endrick on the opposite side.

Barcelona paid $310 million to sign Endrick. The figure made his departure a defining transfer in Napoli's recent history; now it gives the tie an unavoidable subplot. A player once surrounded by Napoli teammates will face many of those same footballers in Europe's most demanding knockout competition.

The first leg is scheduled in Barcelona on April 3. Napoli host the return on April 11. The two matches fall amid a demanding Serie A calendar, making the depth of both squads more than a talking point.

There is a temptation to frame this as a referendum on the sale. That would oversimplify matters. Napoli have remained competitive at the highest level, while Endrick's move placed him on a different path. The quarterfinal is not a transfer audit; it is a contest between two teams chasing a semifinal.

Bastoni and Buongiorno know Endrick's qualities from his time in Naples. Endrick knows their habits too. Familiarity runs in both directions, and neither side can rely on nostalgia once the whistle blows.
For supporters, the emotional contrast will be irresistible. For Napoli, the task is simpler and harder: overcome Barcelona over 180 minutes.

articles.headline: BARCELONA TWICE, MILANO AWAY AND LAZIO: APRIL WILL TEST NAPOLI'S DEPTH
articles.dek: A European quarterfinal, a Coppa semifinal and a Scudetto race converge in a demanding 26-day stretch.
articles.label: THE RUN-IN · MARCH–APRIL 2029
body: Napoli's new calendar makes one thing plain: there will be no isolated Champions League campaign. Barcelona away on April 3 and at home on April 11 sit between league fixtures against Genoa on April 8 and Milano away on April 14.

Before that sequence, Napoli host Venezia on March 18, then the international window interrupts club football. Italy face Iraq on March 21 and the United States on March 25, while Napoli resume league play away to Bergamo on March 31.

April 18 brings the second leg of the Coppa Italia semifinal against Lazio, with Napoli holding a 1–0 advantage from the first leg. Torino visit in Serie A on April 22, followed by another away league fixture on April 29.

The challenge is not simply fatigue. It is tactical continuity when combinations change from match to match. Napoli have shown they can alter one or two starting positions while preserving the collective structure. That approach will face its sternest test when matches arrive every three or four days.

The title race leaves little room for an accidental sacrifice. Napoli reached 70 points after 29 Serie A matches, four clear of Juventus. Every league fixture has weight, even when Barcelona dominate the headlines.
A deep squad can be a competitive advantage only if its members remain match-ready. In April, Napoli will discover just how much of that advantage is real.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: BARCELONA BOUGHT ENDRICK. THEY DIDN'T BUY THE REST OF NAPOLI.
articles.dek: The reunion writes its own headline, but Napoli's evolution since the $310 million sale deserves the real scrutiny.
articles.label: THE BELLANDI COLUMN · EUROPE
body: Of course it had to be Barcelona. Football has a weakness for dramatic symmetry, and few scripts are neater than a $310 million striker facing the club that sold him in a Champions League quarterfinal.

Endrick will command the cameras. That is inevitable, and it is deserved: transfers of that magnitude do not vanish from memory. But anyone who reduces this tie to a former player's revenge story has not been watching Napoli.

Pio Esposito and Maximilian Beier are not supporting actors in someone else's reunion. Their understanding has become one of Napoli's most potent attacking weapons. In Nottingham, Esposito's backheel supplied Beier for the winner. The goal was the opposite of an individual vanity project: three players, including Scott McTominay, connected almost instinctively.

There is a harder question for Barcelona. How do you contain a Napoli side that can change personnel without changing its identity? And there is an equally hard question for Napoli. Can that control survive against an opponent of Barcelona's quality, over two legs, with a league title race pressing from either side?
I will not pretend a transfer fee settles a football argument. It buys a player, not a result. The quarterfinal will be decided by the footballers on the pitch, not the numbers in an old transaction.
Barcelona bought Endrick. Napoli kept building. Now we find out what those two decisions look like when they meet.

articles.headline: DE BRUYNE AT NINETY: NAPOLI TAKE THE LEAD TO NOTTINGHAM
articles.dek: Murillo silenced Naples in the 79th minute. Kevin De Bruyne answered in the 90th. The Champions League tie is alive.
articles.date: 6 March 2029 · Champions League R16 first leg
articles.label: NAPOLI 2–1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
body: At 79 minutes the night seemed to have turned against Napoli. Murillo had found the equaliser from a Nottingham Forest corner, and a home advantage built carefully across the first half had vanished in an instant. Eleven minutes later, Kevin De Bruyne changed the entire conversation. Napoli 2, Nottingham Forest 1. The scoreboard did not tell the story of a comfortable victory. It told the story of a European tie that refused to stay still.

The opening breakthrough had come in the 36th minute. Pio Esposito was fouled inside the penalty area and took responsibility himself. The striker placed the penalty low into the bottom corner. In a knockout fixture where nerves and small margins govern everything, that was a decisive act of composure.

Forest's response did not come through an elaborate passage of open play. It came through a corner, with Murillo levelling in the 79th minute. The equaliser was a reminder that possession of an advantage is not the same as control of a tie. Napoli had to absorb the disappointment of seeing their first-leg lead disappear.

Then came the final minute of normal time. João Neves supplied De Bruyne, and the veteran finished to put Napoli ahead again. One pass, one finish, and a stadium that had spent the previous eleven minutes contemplating a draw suddenly had a winning moment to remember.

De Bruyne's goal is the image this match will leave behind, but Pio's penalty and Neves' assist belong in the same account. This was a victory built from contributions at different stages of the night, not a miracle performed by one man.

Napoli travel to Nottingham for the return leg on March 14 with a 2–1 aggregate lead. There is no away-goals rule. A one-goal advantage is valuable, but it is not protection against a difficult evening at the City Ground. For now, Naples can celebrate a dramatic first-leg win. Tomorrow, the question becomes how to defend it.

articles.headline: NEVES TO DE BRUYNE: THE PASS THAT CHANGED THE TIE
articles.dek: A corner exposed Napoli. One pass from João Neves restored the advantage. What must change in Nottingham?
articles.date: 6 March 2029 · Champions League R16 first leg
articles.label: NAPOLI 2–1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
body: The final combination was beautiful in its simplicity: João Neves found Kevin De Bruyne, and the Belgian scored in the 90th minute. But the tactical story of Napoli's 2–1 victory is not simply that a world-class player produced a world-class moment. It is that Napoli needed that moment after allowing Nottingham Forest back into the tie.

Pio Esposito's 36th-minute penalty had given Napoli the advantage. The foul that earned it and the conversion itself were both significant. In a two-legged contest, turning pressure into an actual goal changes what the opponent must do. Napoli reached the final stretch holding that advantage.

Murillo's 79th-minute equaliser came from a corner. That detail matters because a set piece can bypass the rhythms that have defined the preceding match. It asks different questions: organisation, concentration, first contact and reaction to second balls. Without the full sequence, individual blame would be guesswork. The collective warning is real.

Neves' late assist provided the other side of the argument. Rather than accepting the draw, Napoli found a decisive attacking connection. De Bruyne's finish transformed the mood and, more importantly, the aggregate score. The margin is one goal, not two; a 1–0 Forest victory in the return leg would level the tie.

The temptation is to describe this as proof that Napoli always find a way. That is a useful supporter sentiment, but a dangerous coaching assumption. Forest have already shown they can score from a dead-ball situation, and the second leg will bring a different setting and a different emotional balance.

Napoli's task in Nottingham is to protect the advantage without becoming prisoners of it. The opening penalty, the corner concession and the 90th-minute winner offer three lessons: seize the moments you earn, defend the moments you cannot dictate, and keep enough attacking ambition to punish an opponent that must chase.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: NEVER WRITE OFF THE OLD MASTER
articles.dek: Bellandi celebrates the old master, then asks why Napoli needed saving.
articles.date: 6 March 2029 · Champions League R16 first leg
articles.label: NAPOLI 2–1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
body: I have watched enough European football to know that the word 'comfortable' should be banned from every first-leg press room. Napoli were ahead. Then they were level. Then Kevin De Bruyne, apparently offended by the idea of a quiet evening, decided the final minute belonged to him.

Let us start with the man everyone will put on the front page. João Neves delivers the pass; De Bruyne finishes. Ninety minutes. A winner. That is the sort of scene that makes a veteran's reputation feel less like a historical achievement and more like an ongoing argument against the passage of time.

But the romantic ending cannot erase what happened eleven minutes earlier. Murillo scored from a corner in the 79th minute. If I were sitting in the Napoli analysis room, that sequence would be playing on repeat. Not because the sky is falling, but because Forest have been handed evidence of a route back into the contest.

Pio Esposito deserves his share of the praise too. Fouled in the area, he stepped up and scored the penalty in the 36th minute. A younger player carrying that responsibility in a Champions League knockout match is not a footnote. It is part of the reason Napoli had something to lose in the first place.

I can already hear the arguments. One group will say Napoli were saved by individual brilliance. Another will say good teams create the conditions for decisive players to decide matches. The truth can accommodate both. You can admire the winner and still ask uncomfortable questions about the equaliser.

And now Nottingham. The home crowd will not applaud Napoli's romantic storyline. Forest need one goal to erase the aggregate deficit. Napoli need to show that their response at 90 minutes was not just an emotional rescue but the beginning of a disciplined European performance. Enjoy the old master's masterpiece tonight. Then put the corner footage back on.

articles.headline: PIO BRACE SENDS NAPOLI SEVEN CLEAR OF ROMA
articles.dek: Pio and Beier traded goals in eleven minutes. A penalty flew over. Napoli finished three clear and four points ahead of Juventus.
articles.label: COMO 0–3 NAPOLI
body: Four minutes were enough to tell Como what sort of afternoon this would be. Pio Esposito opened the scoring in the seventh minute from Maximilian Beier's assist. In the eleventh, Esposito returned the favour and Beier made it 2–0. The two forwards had exchanged goals and assists before the match had properly settled.

Napoli arrived with a title race to manage and a Champions League return leg approaching. They left with a 3–0 victory, a clean sheet for Peacock and 70 points from 29 Serie A matches. It was a result that felt particularly emphatic after a sequence of narrow wins.

Como did have a moment that could have altered the afternoon. In the 24th minute Addai stepped up for a penalty. Peacock went the correct way, but the shot flew over the crossbar. It was a miss by the taker, not a save by the goalkeeper. At 2–0, that distinction did not change the relief felt by the visitors.

Napoli did not need to chase a third goal recklessly. The decisive extra margin arrived in the 70th minute, when Esposito found the top corner to complete his brace. His second goal gave the scoreline the authority that the opening exchanges had promised.

The league table sharpens the significance. Napoli have 70 points, Juventus 66 and Roma 63, all after 29 matches. Juventus are the nearest challengers at four points back. Roma are seven behind. Napoli's league record reads 21 wins, seven draws and one defeat, with 52 scored and only 14 conceded.

The title has not been won in Como. Nine league matches remain, and Juventus have no intention of conceding it. But this was an afternoon when Napoli did more than survive. They scored early, survived the penalty scare, and finished with the kind of clarity that sends a message to the chasing pack.

articles.headline: BEIER AND PIO: ELEVEN MINUTES THAT BROKE COMO
articles.dek: Two forwards, two exchanged assists, and a partnership making Napoli's attack increasingly difficult to contain.
articles.label: COMO 0–3 NAPOLI
body: The seventh and eleventh minutes offered a compact study in attacking chemistry. Maximilian Beier created the first goal for Pio Esposito; Pio created the second for Beier. It was not merely two names on a scoresheet. It was the same partnership changing roles in the space of four minutes.

That exchange matters because a forward line becomes harder to defend when its responsibilities are fluid. One attacker is the finisher in one move and the provider in the next. Opponents cannot build their entire plan around denying service to a single striker when the supposed supplier is equally capable of arriving to score.

Como's penalty in the 24th minute was the match's obvious hinge. Addai missed the target, sending the ball over while Peacock dived the correct way. A successful conversion would have reduced Napoli's advantage to one goal with most of the contest still to play. Instead, the visitors retained their two-goal cushion.

The 70th-minute third goal completed Pio's brace and turned a strong lead into a decisive scoreline. The finish into the top corner underlined the striker's confidence. His tracked all-competition total now stands at 34 goals and 19 assists; Beier has 24 goals and 17 assists. Those are the figures of a partnership contributing both finishing and creation.

Napoli's defensive record is equally relevant. Fourteen goals conceded in 29 league matches gives the attack a platform. A team with that level of defensive resistance does not need three goals every week, but the ability to score three can change the psychological terms of a title race.

The challenge is maintaining this balance while European football intrudes. Nottingham Forest await on March 14 with Napoli holding a narrow first-leg advantage. Como showed what happens when the forwards connect early; the next test will ask whether Napoli can reproduce enough of that attacking threat while protecting a Champions League lead.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: THREE GOALS, THREE POINTS, AND NO LATE PANIC
articles.dek: For once, Napoli spared their supporters the 90th-minute ordeal. Bellandi isn't getting used to it.
articles.label: COMO 0–3 NAPOLI
body: I have one request for Napoli. Just one. Can we occasionally win a football match without making the entire city check its blood pressure? At Como, the answer was apparently yes. Three goals, none conceded, and an afternoon that did not require Kevin De Bruyne to rescue everybody in the 90th minute.

Seven minutes: Beier to Pio. Eleven minutes: Pio to Beier. I love that little exchange because it is football's most persuasive answer to the argument about which striker is more important. One creates, one finishes, then they swap. Both get their moment. Everybody else gets a headache.

There was, of course, an obligatory scare. Addai had a penalty in the 24th minute and sent it over. Peacock dived correctly, but I will not award him a save he did not make. Let us enjoy the clean sheet without rewriting the laws of physics.

Then Pio scored again in the 70th minute, into the top corner, because apparently a goal and an assist were insufficient for his afternoon's work. Thirty-four goals and nineteen assists across competitions: at some point, even the loudest doubters must either reconsider their position or begin inventing increasingly absurd criteria.

Now look at the standings. Seventy points for Napoli, sixty-six for Juventus, sixty-three for Roma. The temptation is to treat four points as a protective wall. It is not. With nine matches remaining, a single bad week can change the mood of an entire city. The Scudetto race is still alive.

But today deserves a little joy. Napoli were clinical early, survived the penalty, and finished the job. That is what title contenders should do to opponents when the chance appears. Next comes Nottingham, where a one-goal aggregate lead will demand a different sort of nerve. For once, though, I am not writing this column with trembling hands.

articles.headline: OLISE BREAKS PARMA RESISTANCE AS NAPOLI TAKE THREE MORE POINTS
articles.dek: A 51st-minute goal, made by Nico Paz, delivers a 1–0 away win. Napoli generate 3.1 expected goals but cannot add to their lead.
articles.label: PARMA 0–1 NAPOLI · SERIE A
body: Parma 0, Napoli 1. Michael Olise scored the only goal in the 51st minute, assisted by Nico Paz, to take Napoli to 67 points from 28 Serie A matches.

The visitors fashioned numerous opportunities in a goalless first half, then finally found a breakthrough six minutes after the restart. Paz supplied Olise, whose finish gave Napoli the lead they would retain until full-time.

The numbers describe a match that could have been far more comfortable. Napoli recorded 11 shots to Parma's three, with five efforts on target to the home side's one. Expected goals finished at 3.1 for Napoli and 1.1 for Parma. The score remained 1–0.
It is a familiar theme after Napoli's 1–0 Coppa Italia semifinal first-leg victory over Lazio. The side is creating opportunities but not finding a second goal to ease the pressure.

Napoli's league record now stands at 20 wins, seven draws and one defeat, with 49 goals scored and 14 conceded. After 28 matches, Roma and Juventus are level on 63 points, four behind Napoli. Atalanta have 55, Inter 51 and AC Milan 45. Ten league matches remain. The result also extends the team's sequence of clean sheets across the Lazio and Parma matches.
Next comes Nottingham Forest in Naples on March 6 for the first leg of the Champions League round of 16. Napoli enter that tie with momentum, and a clear challenge in front of goal.

articles.headline: 3.1 EXPECTED GOALS. ONE FINISH. THE WARNING BEFORE NOTTINGHAM FOREST
articles.dek: Napoli's chance creation is healthy, but consecutive 1–0 victories expose the risk of leaving opponents in contention.
articles.label: TACTICAL NOTEBOOK · FOREST NEXT
body: There is a difference between failing to create chances and failing to convert them. Napoli's 1–0 victory at Parma belongs firmly in the second category.

The league leaders registered 3.1 expected goals from 11 attempts, five on target. Parma managed three shots, one on target, and 1.1 expected goals. Michael Olise's 51st-minute goal, created by Nico Paz, was the only finish that counted.

Expected goals are not a guarantee of three goals, nor does one match establish a permanent finishing problem. But a two-goal gap between chance quality and actual output is notable, especially after Napoli also won their Coppa Italia first leg against Lazio by a single goal despite repeated dangerous openings.

The positive reading is that the attacking structure continues to work. Paz, frustrated by Motta and the post against Lazio, provided the decisive pass in Parma. Olise supplied the finish. Napoli also preserved another clean sheet.

The concern is what a narrow lead permits. An opponent need not dominate to equalise, and Nottingham Forest's two-legged Champions League tie introduces another layer: chances left unfinished in Naples could matter enormously in the return match.

The solution is not frantic shooting or abandoning the patterns that produce chances. It is better execution in the box, composure after the first goal, and the discipline to keep creating rather than settling for a fragile advantage.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: I LOVE THREE POINTS. I WOULD ALSO LOVE A SECOND GOAL.
articles.dek: Napoli keep winning 1–0, and the Champions League is next. The results are excellent; the finishing is testing everyone's nerves.
articles.label: BELLANDI · THE NARROW-WIN CLUB
body: Another 1–0. Another clean sheet. Another three points. Another afternoon spent wondering how a team with this much attacking quality has made winning look so unnecessarily stressful.

Let me be clear: I will take a win at Parma every single time. Michael Olise scored, Nico Paz assisted, and Napoli now have 67 points from 28 league games. That is what title-winning teams are supposed to do.

But 3.1 expected goals for one actual goal? Eleven shots against three? Five on target against one? We have been watching enough chances to win comfortably and getting scorelines that keep the opposition interested until the end.
The same thing happened against Lazio in the cup. Motta was excellent that night, Paz hit the post, and Napoli still won. I appreciate the resilience. I also appreciate being able to breathe.
Now comes Nottingham Forest. The Champions League knockout rounds do not care how beautifully you constructed the chance you missed. They care about the score when the whistle goes.
So celebrate Olise. Applaud Paz. Give the defence its flowers. Then spend the next training session reminding everyone where the corners of the goal are.
Three points secured. Napoli lead Roma and Juventus by four points, with both challengers on 63 after 28 matches. European finishing examination next.

articles.headline: PIO STRIKES EARLY, MOTTA REFUSES TO YIELD: NAPOLI TAKE A SLENDER LEAD OVER LAZIO
articles.dek: Esposito's ninth-minute finish from De Bruyne's pass settles the first leg, but the goalkeeper and the woodwork keep the semifinal alive.
articles.date: 2028–29 · Coppa Italia · Semifinal first leg · Full-time
articles.label: NAPOLI 1–0 LAZIO · FIRST LEG
body: Napoli will carry a 1–0 lead into the second leg of their Coppa Italia semifinal against Lazio. The result is a victory, a clean sheet and a reminder that knockout football can turn on a single moment even when the chances keep coming.

The decisive moment arrived in the ninth minute. Kevin De Bruyne supplied Pio Esposito, who finished to give a heavily rotated Napoli side the lead. It was Esposito's 31st tracked club goal of the season, and De Bruyne's contribution came before fatigue eventually became a consideration.

The Belgian almost scored himself when Esposito returned the favour, centring for a first-time effort. Lazio goalkeeper Motta stretched to keep it out. De Bruyne then released Nico Paz for another opening, only for Motta to intervene again.
Paz struck the post in the 53rd minute and was denied on two further dangerous occasions. Esposito also found Motta in his way. Napoli could not turn their chances into a second goal.
Manager Stefan Saladino introduced Alphonso Davies, Scott McTominay and Michael Olise in a triple substitution as Napoli looked to maintain their threat. The score did not change.
There was one last reminder of the tie's fragility: goalkeeper Peacock made an important save at the final whistle to protect the clean sheet.
Napoli have the advantage. Lazio have only a one-goal deficit. That distinction will matter when the teams meet again.

articles.headline: AFTER SVILAR, MOTTA: WHY NAPOLI'S CHANCES AREN'T BECOMING GOALS
articles.dek: Nico Paz hit the post and was denied repeatedly. Napoli's attacking combinations were there; the cushion was not.
articles.date: 2028–29 · Coppa Italia · Semifinal first leg · Analysis
articles.label: TACTICAL NOTEBOOK · THE GOALKEEPER WALL
body: One match after Mile Svilar made five saves in Napoli's 1–1 league draw with Roma, another goalkeeper shaped the story. Lazio's Motta was repeatedly called upon in a Coppa Italia semifinal first leg that Napoli won 1–0.

The early goal showed the range of Napoli's attacking relationships: De Bruyne assisted Esposito in the ninth minute, then Esposito created a first-time opportunity for De Bruyne that Motta stopped at full stretch.

Nico Paz became the clearest illustration of Napoli's frustration. De Bruyne found him for a chance that Motta saved before halftime. In the 53rd minute Paz hit the post; later he was stopped twice more from dangerous positions.

Esposito, already on the scoresheet, also had an effort denied. It would be too easy to treat the narrow margin as proof that the attacking plan failed. Napoli reached dangerous areas through different players and combinations. The finishing outcome simply did not match the opportunities.

There is no verified shot-total or expected-goals figure from this match, so a numerical claim about dominance would be guesswork. The documented sequence is enough to establish that Motta had an exceptional evening.
The tactical question for the return leg is not whether Napoli can create chances. It is whether they can make their advantage count before Lazio find a moment of their own.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: A WIN FOR THE ROTATED ELEVEN. AND A SAVE WE CANNOT FORGET.
articles.dek: Pio got the goal, the substitutes brought pedigree, and Peacock ensured the first-leg advantage survived the final whistle.
articles.date: 2028–29 · Coppa Italia · Semifinal first leg · Opinion
articles.label: BELLANDI · CUP NIGHT VERDICT
body: Let me start with the good news: Napoli won. A rotated side took a semifinal first leg 1–0, Pio Esposito scored again, and the team will go into the return match ahead.

Now the part that makes my blood pressure rise: how did this finish only 1–0? Motta denied De Bruyne at full stretch, frustrated Paz repeatedly, and stopped Pio as well. Paz even hit the post. After Svilar's performance against Roma, I am ready to file a formal complaint against Italian goalkeepers.

There was a lesson in the team selection. Esposito led the line, De Bruyne provided the early assist, and Napoli still had the resources to introduce Alphonso Davies, Scott McTominay and Michael Olise together. Rotation did not mean surrendering ambition.
But the name I want to remember is Peacock. His save at the whistle preserved the clean sheet. In a two-legged semifinal, that intervention could become as valuable as the ninth-minute goal.
I will celebrate a cup victory. I will not pretend a one-goal lead is safe, because it isn't. Lazio are still in this tie and Napoli must finish the job in the second leg.
For now, credit the rotated starters, credit the goalkeeper, and give Motta the evening off next time. Please.

articles.headline: SIX SHOTS ON TARGET. FIVE SVILAR SAVES. NAPOLI AND ROMA SHARE THE POINTS.
articles.dek: Pisilli scored with Roma's only effort on target; Beier's 71st-minute equaliser, supplied by Pio Esposito, rescued a 1–1 draw.
articles.label: NAPOLI 1–1 ROMA · TITLE RACE
body: Napoli 1, Roma 1. A result that preserves the four-point separation at the top of Serie A, and one that will leave the home side wondering how six shots on target produced only one goal.

Roma struck first in the 33rd minute through Niccolò Pisilli, whose finish was a legitimate piece of quality rather than a defensive gift. It was also Roma's only shot on target of the entire match. One effort, one goal: an unforgiving equation for Napoli.

The hosts had four shots on target by halftime. Mile Svilar had already made major interventions, including two against Pio Esposito before the 18th minute, and Napoli entered the break 1–0 down despite the weight of their chances.

Napoli finally found the breakthrough in the 71st minute. Pio supplied Maximilian Beier, who beat Svilar to level the contest. There would be no winner. Svilar finished with five saves from Napoli's six shots on target.

For the title race, the draw is less dramatic than the match itself. Napoli move to 64 points from 27 matches, Roma to 60. Napoli's league record becomes 19 wins, seven draws and one defeat, with 48 goals scored and 14 conceded.

Svilar had already tormented Napoli in the Supercoppa final, which Roma won on penalties after a goalless draw. Once again he became the defining figure. Napoli can take encouragement from the chances created, but not from the result they yielded.
The league lead survives. The opportunity to make it seven points does not.

articles.headline: SVILAR, AGAIN: THE GOALKEEPER WHO KEEPS GETTING BETWEEN NAPOLI AND ROMA
articles.dek: Five saves in Naples and a familiar name from the Supercoppa. How much of this draw belongs to the man in goal?
articles.label: GOALKEEPER FOCUS · FIVE SAVES
body: There is a particular kind of frustration that comes from creating the chances and still failing to win. Napoli know it well after a 1–1 draw with Roma in which Mile Svilar stopped five of six efforts on target.

The goalkeeper's evening began early. By the 18th minute he had already denied Pio Esposito twice, while an opening created by Alphonso Davies also ended with Svilar intervening. Napoli managed four shots on target before the interval, yet Roma led.

The scoreline can tempt a lazy verdict about poor finishing. That would miss the distinction between a wasteful attempt and a goalkeeper producing an exceptional save. Without shot-by-shot quality data, the precise balance cannot be measured. The evidence from the match, however, includes several outstanding interventions.

This was not Svilar's first starring role against Napoli. In January's Supercoppa final, Roma survived a goalless match and prevailed 4–3 on penalties, with Svilar saving Pio's spot kick. Different competition, same obstacle.
Beier eventually beat him in the 71st minute, with Pio turning provider. The goal spared Napoli a defeat that would have reduced their league advantage over Roma to a single point.
Five saves are not five trophies, and a draw does not make Roma favourites. But across two high-stakes encounters, Svilar has made himself impossible to ignore.

articles.headline: BELLANDI: I WANTED SEVEN POINTS. I'LL TAKE FOUR. I WON'T PRETEND I'M HAPPY.
articles.dek: A lead protected, a chance missed, and one infuriating goalkeeper. The title race remains in Napoli's hands.
articles.label: BELLANDI · AFTER THE WHISTLE
body: I had seven points in my head. I'll admit it. Roma had just lost 4–2 to Palermo, Napoli were at home, and I spent the week imagining a league table with enough daylight to breathe.

Then Pisilli scored. Again. Thirty-three minutes in, Roma had found the net with the only shot they would put on target all evening. You can admire the finish and still want to throw the television out the window.
And Svilar. Oh, Svilar. Five saves. Five. I am beginning to think his contract includes a special clause requiring him to become a superhero whenever Napoli are involved.

I won't call the team hopeless after six shots on target. I won't call our defence a disaster because Roma converted one well-taken chance. Football is sometimes crueler than the post-match arguments allow.

Beier's equaliser in the 71st minute, created by Pio, mattered enormously. Without it, the lead over Roma shrinks to one. With it, Napoli sit on 64 points, Roma on 60, and there are eleven league matches to go.
So no, I am not celebrating a draw at home. But neither am I pretending this was a collapse. Four points clear is a position to defend, not a reason to panic.
Now beat Lazio in the cup. And if somebody sees Svilar in the tunnel, please ask him to take a holiday.

articles.headline: THE MATCH THAT COULD BREAK THE TITLE RACE: HOW NAPOLI BEAT ROMA — AND THE MAN WHO MUST STEP UP
articles.dek: Four points clear, Roma at the Maradona, and a seven-point lead within reach. Pio may supply the goals, but João Neves could decide whether Napoli control the night.
articles.label: BIG MATCH PREVIEW · NAPOLI vs ROMA
body: Four points. That is all that separates Napoli and Roma before the biggest league meeting of Stefan Saladino's season so far. After 26 matches, Napoli lead with 63 points, Roma follow on 59, and Juventus remain close enough to matter on 57. A home win would extend Napoli's advantage over Roma to seven points; defeat would reduce it to one. This is not a coronation. It is an opportunity to take command.

The emotional temptation is to read too much into Roma's 4–2 home defeat to Palermo. Napoli's own 2–0 win over Empoli, sealed by two Pio Esposito goals and eight Peacock saves, was earned rather than gifted. But Roma's 57 league goals are ten more than Napoli's 47. The visitors have the attacking capacity to punish a team that confuses momentum with control.
THE PLAN: ATTACK ROMA'S FULLBACKS WITHOUT EXPOSING OUR OWN

Napoli's left side offers a clear route forward. Alphonso Davies, used high on the wing, can stretch the pitch; Marc Cucurella's supporting runs and quick combinations can force Roma's right flank into uncomfortable decisions. The instruction is not simply to attack relentlessly. When Cucurella advances, the midfield must be positioned to stop the counterattack before Roma can exploit the space he leaves.
PIO AND BEIER: GIVE ROMA TWO PROBLEMS, NOT ONE

Esposito arrives with 30 tracked goals and 17 assists across competitions. Maximilian Beier has 22 goals and 16 assists. Their partnership is more dangerous than either player's individual totals: Beier can drag defenders away from the central lane, combine early, and create the second movement that frees Pio. Roma cannot be allowed to defend against a stationary striker. Napoli must vary which forward drops, which runs behind, and where the first pass goes.
THE WARNING: ROMA'S MIDFIELD CAN CHANGE A MATCH

In the Coppa Italia meeting, Roma's Manu Koné scored the equaliser before Pio ultimately settled a 2–1 Napoli victory in extra time. That history matters. Napoli's centre-backs, Alessandro Bastoni and Alessandro Buongiorno, have anchored a league defence that has conceded just 13 goals in 26 games, but even an elite pairing can be pulled apart if runners arrive untracked between midfield and defence. Napoli must defend the central channels together, not ask the back line to solve every transition alone.
THE X-FACTOR: JOÃO NEVES

The obvious headline choice is Pio. The decisive tactical choice is João Neves. Against a Roma side capable of scoring in bursts, Napoli need someone who can turn frantic exchanges into deliberate possessions. Neves must offer Bastoni and Buongiorno a reliable first pass, resist pressure without inviting turnovers, and recognise when to release Davies quickly rather than recycle the ball. Above all, he must cover the space behind Napoli's advancing left side.

That is why Neves is the X-factor rather than another goalscorer. If he dominates the spaces between the two penalty areas, Pio and Beier will have opportunities to hurt Roma without Napoli becoming vulnerable every time an attack breaks down. If Roma's midfield runners escape him, the match risks becoming the kind of end-to-end contest their scoring record suggests they would welcome.
WHAT NAPOLI MUST DO

Start with composure rather than the emotion of the occasion. Use Davies and Cucurella to stretch Roma's defensive shape; keep Pio and Beier moving on different lines; let Neves control the rhythm and guard against counters; deny Koné easy progression through the middle. When Napoli lose the ball, the nearest midfielders must react immediately, allowing Bastoni and Buongiorno to hold their positions rather than defend open grass.
THE VERDICT

Roma's defeat to Palermo has created an opening, not removed the danger. Napoli have the tighter defence, the home advantage and a four-point lead. Roma have the higher league goal total and every incentive to take risks. If Saladino's side keep their balance, they can make the Maradona the place where the title race bends decisively toward Naples. The forwards may write the headline. João Neves may determine whether it gets written at all.

articles.headline: FOUR POINTS. ONE SHOWDOWN. ROMA COME TO NAPLES WITH THEIR TITLE HOPES ON THE LINE
articles.dek: Napoli lead Roma 63–59 after 26 matches. Following a 4–2 defeat to Palermo, the visitors face the league leaders next.
body: The timing could scarcely be more dramatic. Roma arrive in Naples as the nearest challengers in the Scudetto race, four points behind Stefan Saladino's side with twelve league fixtures remaining.

Only one matchday ago, Napoli held a single-point advantage. Napoli then beat Empoli 2–0 through two Pio Esposito goals, while Roma suffered a startling 4–2 home defeat to Palermo. Juventus won their match to reach 57 points, six behind the leaders.

The table after 26 matches tells the story: Napoli have 63 points, Roma 59 and Juventus 57. Napoli have conceded only 13 league goals, compared with Roma's 26, though Roma have scored 57 to Napoli's 47.

A Napoli victory would open a seven-point lead over Roma. A Roma victory would cut the gap to one. A draw would maintain the four-point separation. With the title race this tight, every outcome carries weight.

Napoli have just advanced past Monaco 5–1 on aggregate in the Champions League, but the European celebrations must now be put aside. Roma are the immediate assignment. The match date and kickoff time have not yet been confirmed by the manager.
For Saladino, the question is whether his team can turn a welcome gift from Palermo into an advantage of its own making. For Roma, it is a chance to respond before the title race begins to slip away.
articles.label: NEXT MATCH · NAPOLI 63 · ROMA 59

articles.headline: FORGET PALERMO. ROMA ARE COMING, AND THIS IS OUR MOMENT.
articles.dek: The party was deserved. Now Napoli have to do the difficult part themselves.
body: I enjoyed every second of Roma conceding four to Palermo. I won't pretend otherwise. But the greatest danger now is believing their bad day will do our work for us.
Roma are still second. They have scored 57 league goals. They know a victory in Naples would bring them straight back within a point of the leaders.
We have a chance to make it seven. Seven! But no one earns that gap by looking at a newspaper headline.
Pio is scoring for fun, Peacock just gave us a clean sheet, and the squad has shown it can rotate without surrendering points. Now we need ninety minutes of the same hunger against our closest rival.
Celebrate Palermo once. Then forget Palermo. This is Napoli against Roma. This is where we prove it.
articles.label: NAPOLI vs ROMA · TITLE RACE

articles.headline: FOREST AWAIT: NAPOLI DRAW NOTTINGHAM FOREST IN CHAMPIONS LEAGUE LAST 16
articles.dek: Napoli's next European assignment is Nottingham Forest. The Round of 16 first leg is scheduled at home on March 6, with the return away on March 14.
body: Napoli's next European assignment is Nottingham Forest. The Round of 16 first leg is scheduled at home on March 6, with the return away on March 14.
The Italian champions progressed 5–1 on aggregate against Monaco, winning the opening away leg 4–0 before a 1–1 second-leg draw.
Pio Esposito scored four times across the two legs. His first-half hat-trick in the opening match set the tone; his equaliser in the return ended Monaco's brief revival.
After last season's Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, the stakes of another knockout campaign are clear. Forest will offer a fresh test, and the result is yet to be written.
articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · FOREST ROUND OF 16

articles.headline: MISSION ACCOMPLISHED: NAPOLI FINISH MONACO JOB AND REACH THE LAST 16
articles.dek: Bamba struck in the fifth minute to give Monaco early hope in the return leg. Napoli responded on the half-hour: João Neves found Maximilian Beier, whose pass gave Pio Esposito a tap-in.
body: Bamba struck in the fifth minute to give Monaco early hope in the return leg. Napoli responded on the half-hour: João Neves found Maximilian Beier, whose pass gave Pio Esposito a tap-in.
The match ended 1–1, completing a 5–1 aggregate win for Napoli. The first-leg 4–0 victory had done the heavy lifting, but the second leg still required discipline.
Pio's fourth goal of the tie brought his tracked season tally to 30. Beier registered his 16th tracked assist.
Napoli are through to the Champions League Round of 16, where Nottingham Forest await.
articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · FOREST ROUND OF 16

articles.headline: LAZIO ON FEBRUARY 27: NAPOLI'S CUP AMBITIONS FACE ANOTHER TEST
articles.dek: Napoli face Lazio in the Coppa Italia on February 27, manager Saladino has confirmed. The precise cup round and venue are not yet confirmed.
body: Napoli face Lazio in the Coppa Italia on February 27, manager Saladino has confirmed. The precise cup round and venue are not yet confirmed.
The match arrives after Napoli's Champions League qualification and before a demanding March that includes Nottingham Forest twice.
Rotation will be a serious consideration, but Napoli have already demonstrated the value of their squad depth in the league win over Empoli.
The result is still to come. The opportunity to pursue another domestic trophy remains alive.
articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · FOREST ROUND OF 16

articles.headline: MARCH'S FIXTURE GAUNTLET: FOREST TWICE, PARMA, COMO AND INTERNATIONAL DUTY
articles.dek: March 3 brings a league trip to Parma. On March 6 Napoli host Nottingham Forest in the Champions League Round of 16 first leg.
body: March 3 brings a league trip to Parma. On March 6 Napoli host Nottingham Forest in the Champions League Round of 16 first leg.
A league visit to Como follows on March 10, before Napoli travel to Forest for the second leg on March 14.
Another home league match is scheduled for March 18, although the opponent is Venezia, as confirmed by manager Saladino.
Italy then face Egypt on March 21 and the United States on March 25 in international friendlies, before Napoli travel to Bergamo Calcio on March 31.
This stretch will test the depth of Saladino's squad as much as the quality of his preferred eleven.
articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · FOREST ROUND OF 16

articles.headline: BRING ON FOREST. WE DIDN'T COME THIS FAR TO FEAR THE DRAW.
articles.dek: The road back toward a European final runs through Nottingham Forest. There is something fitting about another English opponent waiting for Napoli.
body: The road back toward a European final runs through Nottingham Forest. There is something fitting about another English opponent waiting for Napoli.
No supporter should pretend the draw guarantees anything. Knockout football punishes arrogance. But Napoli's four-goal demolition of Monaco away from home gives this team every reason to believe.
The Serie A race is tight, Lazio await in the cup and March looks exhausting. Those are the demands of competing at the highest level.
Respect Forest. Prepare properly. Then go out and play like Napoli.
articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · FOREST ROUND OF 16

articles.headline: PALERMO BLOW THE TITLE RACE OPEN: ROMA FALL 4–2 AS NAPOLI GO FOUR CLEAR
articles.dek: Roma 2–4 Palermo. Napoli 2–0 Empoli. Four points separate the leaders from their nearest challengers.
body: There are weekends that change the arithmetic of a title race. Then there are weekends that change its mood. Palermo's 4–2 victory over Roma has done both.

Napoli had already done their part, beating Empoli 2–0 with two Pio Esposito goals and an eight-save clean sheet from Peacock. Roma, who entered the round just one point behind, suffered their third league defeat of the campaign.
The standings after 26 matches now read Napoli 63, Roma 59 and Juventus 57. Twelve fixtures remain. Napoli's four-point advantage over Roma is real, but hardly decisive.

There is a particularly sharp twist in the fixture list: Napoli's next league opponent is Roma. The challengers have been handed a chance to respond immediately, while the leaders have an opportunity to turn a damaging weekend for their rivals into something even more significant.
No one at Napoli should confuse Palermo's victory with a trophy presentation. But after weeks of pressure, the league leaders have finally been given breathing room.
articles.label: NAPOLI 63 · ROMA 59 · JUVENTUS 57

articles.headline: PIO SCORES TWICE, PEACOCK STANDS TALL: NAPOLI'S ROTATION PASSES THE EMPOLI TEST
