articles.dek: Napoli 2–0 Empoli: Pio 38′ and 61′; Peacock finishes with eight saves and a clean sheet.
body: A rotated Napoli side secured a vital 2–0 victory over Empoli, though the final score should not disguise the work required at both ends of the pitch.
Pio Esposito opened the scoring in the 38th minute, reacting quickest when Maximilian Beier's attempt came back into play and converting the rebound. No assist has been confirmed for that goal.
The second arrived in the 61st minute. Anton Stach supplied Pio, who finished from a sharp angle with a shot that struck the post before going in.

At the other end, young goalkeeper Peacock recorded eight saves. Manager Saladino noted that not all were dangerous efforts, an important distinction, but his concentration and clean sheet were well earned.
The result takes Napoli to 63 points from 26 league matches. For a squad managing European commitments, the most encouraging detail may be that rotation did not cost them a result.
articles.label: NAPOLI 63 · ROMA 59 · JUVENTUS 57

articles.headline: EIGHT SAVES, ZERO GOALS CONCEDED: PEACOCK MAKES HIS CASE
articles.dek: Not every stop was spectacular. The reliability may matter more.
body: Goalkeepers are often judged by the one impossible save. Against Empoli, Peacock made a different kind of argument: eight stops, a clean sheet and ninety minutes of sustained concentration.
There is no evidence that all eight saves were high-difficulty chances. That is precisely why the performance deserves an honest assessment rather than exaggerated mythology.
A young goalkeeper trying to establish himself must deal with routine efforts as well as dangerous ones. He cannot choose when a shot arrives, or whether the next one will be the difficult one.
Peacock's outing will not settle the long-term selection debate on its own. It does, however, give Napoli another dependable performance to consider as their calendar grows more demanding.
Pio Esposito supplied the goals. Peacock ensured Empoli supplied none. Both contributions were essential to the three points.
articles.label: NAPOLI 63 · ROMA 59 · JUVENTUS 57

articles.headline: FOUR POINTS. ONE SHOWDOWN. ROMA'S TRIP TO NAPLES JUST GOT BIGGER
articles.dek: The next Serie A fixture pits the leaders against the side chasing them.
body: A week ago Napoli's advantage over Roma was a single point. Now it is four, with Roma next on the fixture list for the league leaders.

The contrast is stark: Napoli have conceded only 13 league goals in 26 matches, while Roma have conceded 26. Roma have scored 57, ten more than Napoli's 47, but their defensive record took another blow in the 4–2 loss to Palermo.
Juventus remain in contention on 57 points, six behind Napoli and two behind Roma. The Turin club cannot be written out of the equation, especially with twelve matches remaining.

For Roma, the upcoming meeting is an immediate opportunity to reduce the gap. For Napoli, it is a chance to make their advantage substantially more comfortable. A draw would preserve the four-point separation.
The danger for Saladino's side is obvious: the noise around Palermo's upset can become a distraction. Napoli's task is to prepare for Roma, not celebrate Roma's defeat for a week.
articles.label: NAPOLI 63 · ROMA 59 · JUVENTUS 57

articles.headline: SEND PALERMO A THANK-YOU CARD. THEN GET BACK TO WORK.
articles.dek: A supporter celebrates the unexpected gift without forgetting what is still at stake.
body: I admit it: I checked the Roma score twice. Then a third time. Four goals for Palermo? At Roma? In the middle of this title race?

And yet the part I keep coming back to is what Napoli did themselves. A rotated team, two goals from Pio and a goalkeeper who stopped everything that reached him. We earned our own three points before anyone else could do us a favour.
There is no Scudetto for being four points ahead in February. There is no medal for laughing at a rival's bad afternoon. And the fixture list has a wicked sense of humour, because Roma are next.

So yes, uncork the vino tonight. Thank Palermo. Enjoy the table. But tomorrow morning I want every player looking at the same thing: Roma, twelve games remaining, and a championship that still has to be won.
Forza Napoli. And, just this once, grazie Palermo.
articles.label: NAPOLI 63 · ROMA 59 · JUVENTUS 57

articles.headline: PIO'S FIRST-HALF HAT-TRICK DESTROYS MONACO AS NAPOLI WIN 4–0 AWAY
articles.dek: Monaco 0–4 Napoli: Pio scores three before the break; Beier adds a fourth.
body: Napoli delivered a stunning away performance in their Champions League knockout play-off, defeating Monaco 4–0.
Pio Esposito struck in the fifth minute from a Maximilian Beier assist. Scott McTominay then supplied Pio twice, in the 24th and 40th minutes, completing a first-half hat-trick.
The forwards reversed roles in the 68th minute when Pio set up Beier for Napoli's fourth.

The display was exceptional, though Pio's six-goal-contribution performance against Atalanta earlier in the season remains his bigger individual statistical feat: three goals and three assists in Napoli's 6–2 win.
The emphatic away score places Napoli in a commanding position in the play-off tie. Qualification itself should not be recorded until the remaining tie requirements are confirmed.
articles.label: NAPOLI 63 · ROMA 59 · JUVENTUS 57

articles.headline: EIGHT MINUTES THAT SAVED NAPOLI: PIO AND BEIER TURN BOLOGNA DEFEAT INTO VICTORY
articles.dek: Napoli 2–1 Bologna: Openda 57′, Pio 75′, Beier 83′.
body: Napoli looked destined to drop points for a second consecutive Serie A match. Instead, two goals in eight minutes turned a 1–0 deficit into a 2–1 victory over Bologna.
A scoreless first half gave way to Bologna's breakthrough in the 57th minute, when Openda put the visitors ahead. The assist has not been confirmed.
Napoli's answer came in the 75th minute. Maximilian Beier supplied Pio Esposito for the equaliser, restoring hope to a side whose lead over Roma had been reduced to a single point before kick-off.
Then the roles reversed. In the 83rd minute, Pio turned provider and Beier finished the comeback. The score held to full time.
The win takes Napoli to 60 points after 25 matches, with 18 wins, six draws and one defeat. But Roma and Juventus also won their respective league fixtures, leaving the title race as tight as ever.
The result was a steal in the best sense: not an easy afternoon, not a flawless performance, but a champion's refusal to surrender three points.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 60 · ROMA 59

articles.headline: NOBODY BLINKS: NAPOLI, ROMA AND JUVENTUS ALL WIN
articles.dek: Napoli 60, Roma 59, Juventus 54. Thirteen matches remain.
body: Napoli's comeback against Bologna might have looked like a decisive shift in the Scudetto race. The updated table tells a different story: the leading three all won.
Napoli lead with 60 points from 25 matches. Roma sit one point back on 59, while Juventus remain six behind the leaders on 54.
Roma have scored 55 league goals to Napoli's 45, and their +33 goal difference is one better than Napoli's +32. Napoli, meanwhile, have conceded just 13 goals compared with Roma's 22.
Juventus have 16 wins, six draws and three defeats, with 52 goals scored and 28 conceded. They have not allowed the leading pair to break completely free.
The specific opponents, scores and goalscorers in Roma's and Juventus's latest victories have not been confirmed. Their wins and updated league totals are clear from the standings.
Thirteen league matches remain. Napoli have preserved first place, but no contender has yielded ground.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 60 · ROMA 59

articles.headline: BEIER TO PIO. PIO TO BEIER. A TITLE RACE IN TWO PASSES
articles.dek: The forwards each score and assist in Napoli's 2–1 comeback.
body: With Napoli trailing Bologna, the connection between Pio Esposito and Maximilian Beier changed the match in a matter of minutes.
At 75 minutes, Beier created the equaliser for Pio. At 83, Pio returned the favour and Beier scored the winner.
The tracked season totals now stand at 24 goals and 16 assists for Pio, and 21 goals and 14 assists for Beier. Pio has scored in seven consecutive appearances.
Their influence extends beyond individual numbers. In the cup victory against Roma, Beier supplied both Pio goals. Against Bologna, each man both finished and created.
It would be too easy to describe the victory as proof that Napoli have solved every attacking problem. They were scoreless at halftime and behind by the 57th minute.
But when the champions needed two decisive actions, their most productive partnership supplied both.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 60 · ROMA 59

articles.headline: A WINNER'S INSTINCT, A WARNING SIGN: NAPOLI'S BOLOGNA ESCAPE
articles.dek: Napoli's defence concedes a 13th league goal; the attack rescues three points.
body: Napoli are first with 60 points and the best goals-against record among the top six: 13 conceded in 25 Serie A games.
That foundation did not prevent a difficult afternoon against Bologna. Openda broke the deadlock in the 57th minute, and Napoli needed late goals from Pio and Beier to win 2–1.
The outcome underlines two truths at once. Napoli can recover under pressure, and they cannot always count on a comeback to cover a deficit.
The league leaders have scored 45 goals, ten fewer than Roma's 55. Roma's goal difference is +33, narrowly ahead of Napoli's +32, despite conceding nine more goals.
Without verified shot maps, xG or substitution details for this match, a claim about which tactical adjustment turned the game would be speculation.
The next challenge is to combine Napoli's resilient defending with earlier attacking control. The table gives them first place; the performance offers work for the training ground.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 60 · ROMA 59

articles.headline: THAT WAS A STEAL. DON'T YOU DARE APOLOGISE FOR IT.
articles.dek: Bellandi celebrates the comeback but refuses to ignore Roma's one-point pursuit.
body: For seventy-four minutes, this looked like the kind of afternoon that loses championships. Napoli were behind, Roma were refusing to go away, and the champions were running out of time.
Then Pio Esposito scored in the 75th minute. Then Maximilian Beier scored in the 83rd. And suddenly the story was not a collapse but a comeback.
Call it a steal. I do. Not because Bologna were robbed by an official or because Napoli did not deserve their goals, but because the points looked lost until the very end.
Roma won too. Juventus won too. Napoli have 60 points, Roma 59 and Juventus 54. Nobody is blinking.
There is a warning in this match. Napoli cannot make a habit of falling behind and expecting two forwards to perform miracles.
But there is also something wonderfully defiant about a team that refuses to let its season be dictated by one bad hour.
Thirteen matches left. First place is ours. And after this afternoon, I would not dare write these champions off.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 60 · ROMA 59

articles.headline: NAPOLI HELD AGAIN: FIORENTINA DRAW CUTS TITLE LEAD TO ONE
articles.dek: Napoli remain first on 57 points, but Roma close to 56 after 24 rounds.
body: Napoli are still top of Serie A. After 24 matches, though, the defending champions' lead has shrunk to a single point.
A 0–0 draw with Fiorentina leaves Napoli on 57 points from 17 wins, six draws and one defeat. Roma have moved to 56 points after 24 games, with 17 wins, five draws and two defeats.

The scoreline is confirmed, but no shots, xG, individual performances or match date have been supplied for this Fiorentina meeting. It would be premature to attribute the stalemate to a particular player or tactical problem.
Napoli have conceded just 12 goals in 24 league games and still boast a +31 goal difference. They have scored 43, while Roma have scored 52 and conceded 22.
Fourteen matches remain. The table still belongs to Napoli, but the cushion is almost gone.
The question for the coming weeks is whether Napoli can turn defensive consistency into enough victories to keep their nearest challenger at arm's length.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 57 · ROMA 56

articles.headline: ONE POINT. FOURTEEN GAMES. THE SCUDETTO RACE HAS CHANGED
articles.dek: Roma's 56 points put them within touching distance of league leaders Napoli.
body: The headline is no longer Napoli's comfortable advantage. It is Napoli's survival at the summit.
With 24 matches played, Napoli lead Roma 57 points to 56. Juventus sit third with 51 points, six behind Napoli.
Roma have 17 victories, five draws and two losses, with 52 goals scored and 22 conceded. Napoli have 17 wins, six draws and one defeat, scoring 43 and conceding only 12.
The clubs offer contrasting statistical profiles. Roma have nine more goals scored; Napoli have conceded ten fewer. Napoli's goal difference is +31, Roma's +30.
No further head-to-head or fixture predictions are justified until the remaining schedule is confirmed. What is certain is that both clubs have fourteen league matches left.
Napoli retain first place. Roma have made it a genuine contest.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 57 · ROMA 56

articles.headline: TWELVE CONCEDED IN TWENTY-FOUR: NAPOLI'S DEFENCE STILL SETS THE STANDARD
articles.dek: The title lead is narrow, but Napoli's defensive numbers remain exceptional.
body: A scoreless draw is rarely greeted with celebration by a title contender. Yet Napoli's 0–0 with Fiorentina extends a remarkable defensive record.
Across 24 league matches, Napoli have conceded only 12 goals. That is half a goal per game, and ten fewer than second-placed Roma.
The other side of the ledger is less comfortable: Napoli have scored 43 league goals, nine fewer than Roma. Their 17 victories have been supported by a defence that has kept opponents at bay.
That combination has delivered 57 points and first place, but six draws have left the door open for Roma, who have 56.

Without shot data for the Fiorentina fixture, it is impossible to say whether the attack failed through chance creation, finishing or exceptional goalkeeping. The broader scoring gap is nevertheless worth examining.
The league is still in Napoli's hands. Protecting that advantage will require the defensive base to remain strong and the attack to turn more stalemates into wins.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 57 · ROMA 56

articles.headline: EVEN A RED-HOT ATTACK CAN GO QUIET: FIORENTINA STOP NAPOLI
articles.dek: The Pio–Beier combination carried the Roma cup tie, but Napoli draw a blank in Serie A.
body: In Rome, Pio Esposito scored twice from Maximilian Beier assists to send Napoli through in the cup. In the next confirmed league result, Fiorentina held Napoli to 0–0.
The contrast is striking, but it does not establish that either forward played poorly. No player-level match statistics have been supplied for the Fiorentina draw.
Esposito's tracked club totals stand at 23 goals and 15 assists, with Beier on 20 goals and 13 assists after the Roma cup win. Those figures remain unchanged pending confirmed scorer information.
Napoli's broader attack has scored 43 league goals in 24 matches, while Roma have scored 52. The need for more decisive attacking results is clear even without singling out individuals.
The title race has compressed to one point. The partnership that broke Roma's resistance may have a significant role in what comes next.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 57 · ROMA 56

articles.headline: FIRST PLACE IS NOT A COMFORT BLANKET
articles.dek: Bellandi sees a warning in another scoreless draw while Roma close within a point.
body: I keep hearing the same response: Napoli are still first. Yes, they are. On 57 points, one ahead of Roma.
But a title lead is not something you frame on the wall. It is something you defend every week. A 0–0 with Fiorentina has turned a three-point advantage into one.
Let us be fair: this defence is outstanding. Twelve goals conceded in 24 league games is a champion's foundation. It is also true that Roma have scored 52 league goals to Napoli's 43.
I will not pretend to know who missed what against Fiorentina. We have no confirmed shot or xG numbers for the match, and inventing blame would be lazy.
What I can say is that six draws are now on Napoli's record, and fourteen games remain. The margins have become painfully small.
I still believe Napoli can defend the Scudetto. But belief does not earn points. Wins do.
Celebrate first place if you wish. Then remember that Roma are just one result away from changing the entire mood.
articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 57 · ROMA 56

articles.headline: PIO BREAKS ROMA: NAPOLI ADVANCE AFTER EXTRA TIME
articles.dek: Roma 1–2 Napoli AET. Pio Esposito scores twice, both assisted by Beier.
body: Napoli have their revenge for the Supercoppa final. Away in Rome, they beat Roma 2–1 after extra time and advance in the domestic cup.
Pio Esposito was denied by Mile Svilar in the 11th minute before finishing a Maximilian Beier pass in the 29th. Roma levelled through Manu Koné in the 51st minute.
Svilar was outstanding, making six close-range saves according to the manager, including stops against Pio, Beier and Nico Paz. Napoli created 4.9 xG to Roma's 1.8 and registered ten shots on target.
The winner arrived in the 95th minute: Beier found Pio again, and this time Napoli's advantage held until the end of extra time.
The manager believed Napoli could have scored twice more in the first half of extra time. Instead they had to protect a one-goal lead to the final whistle.
After losing the January Supercoppa final to Roma on penalties, Napoli now have a knockout victory of their own. The next cup opponent is not yet confirmed.
articles.label: COPPA ITALIA · ROMA 1–2 NAPOLI

articles.headline: SIX CLOSE-RANGE SAVES: SVILAR MADE NAPOLI EARN IT
articles.dek: Ten Napoli shots on target, 4.9 xG and a goalkeeper who refused to surrender.
body: Mile Svilar was the obstacle that turned Napoli's cup dominance into a two-hour ordeal.
He stopped Pio Esposito in the 11th minute and also denied Maximilian Beier and Nico Paz. The manager reported six close-range saves in all.
Napoli's ten shots on target and 4.9 xG show how frequently the visitors reached dangerous positions. Roma's 1.8 xG demonstrates they were not without attacking threat themselves.
But Svilar could not keep out everything. Pio finished Beier passes in the 29th and 95th minutes to settle a 2–1 win after extra time.
Svilar's performance deserves recognition even in defeat. Napoli's persistence deserves the qualification.
articles.label: COPPA ITALIA · ROMA 1–2 NAPOLI

articles.headline: BEIER TO PIO, TWICE: THE CONNECTION THAT SETTLED ROME
articles.dek: Pio extends his scoring streak to six appearances; Beier delivers two more assists.
body: It was the same combination twice, and Roma never found a lasting answer.
Maximilian Beier assisted Pio Esposito in the 29th minute, then repeated the feat in the 95th as Napoli won 2–1 after extra time.
Pio has now scored in six successive appearances: Lazio, Real Sociedad, Sampdoria, Cracovia, Juventus and Roma.
His tracked totals rise to 23 goals and 15 assists. Beier reaches 20 goals and 13 assists.
Against Cracovia, Beier also assisted both of Pio's goals. Their understanding is becoming a defining feature of Napoli's season.
The partnership overcame Svilar's resistance and sent Napoli through.
articles.label: COPPA ITALIA · ROMA 1–2 NAPOLI

articles.headline: 4.9 TO 1.8: NAPOLI CREATED ENOUGH TO WIN TWICE
articles.dek: The underlying chance quality was emphatic, even if the score remained close.
body: Napoli won 2–1 after extra time, but the expected-goals figures were 4.9 to 1.8 in their favour.
Ten shots on target and six reported close-range saves from Svilar help explain the tension. The goalkeeper repeatedly intervened in situations where Napoli were well placed to score.
The first Napoli goal came in the 29th minute. Roma equalised in the 51st. Napoli had to wait until the 95th for the winner.
Expected goals do not guarantee a scoreline. They do show that Napoli consistently generated dangerous attempts.
The manager felt Napoli should have scored two more in the first extra-time period. That frustration can coexist with satisfaction at progressing.
Roma's 1.8 xG is a reminder that Napoli still allowed meaningful chances. The next cup tie will require the same creativity with greater efficiency.
articles.label: COPPA ITALIA · ROMA 1–2 NAPOLI

articles.headline: THE REVENGE IS SWEET. THE FINISHING STILL NEEDS WORK.
articles.dek: Bellandi celebrates Napoli's progress but asks why 4.9 xG required extra time.
body: Napoli have beaten Roma in a knockout match, and that is worth celebrating after the Supercoppa disappointment.
Pio Esposito scored twice. Maximilian Beier assisted twice. Their chemistry delivered a deserved 2–1 extra-time victory.
But I cannot ignore the number: 4.9 expected goals. Napoli had ten shots on target and still needed a 95th-minute winner.
Svilar's six close-range saves were extraordinary, and he deserves credit. Napoli also had opportunities to settle the tie sooner.
The manager said they could have scored two more in the first half of extra time. A team fighting on multiple fronts cannot always afford another 120-minute evening.
Enjoy the revenge. Then demand the sharper finishing that could make the next cup night less exhausting.
articles.label: COPPA ITALIA · ROMA 1–2 NAPOLI

articles.headline: NAPOLI LEAVE TURIN WITH A POINT — AND A QUESTION ABOUT WHAT MIGHT HAVE BEEN
articles.dek: Pio Esposito strikes in the 11th minute, Conceição answers in the 19th, and Napoli finish with 1.8 xG to Juventus's 0.8.
body: TURIN — There are draws that feel like escapes and draws that leave a team wondering why it did not win. Napoli's 1–1 against Juventus belongs closer to the second category.

The visitors needed eleven minutes to strike. Scott McTominay found Pio Esposito, whose fierce finish flew into the top corner. It was the sort of emphatic opening that can change the temperature of an away match instantly.

Juventus responded in the 19th minute through Francisco Conceição. The assist on the equaliser has not been confirmed, and there is no reason to dress the record with invented detail. The two first-half goals were the only goals of the match.

The full-time expected-goals figures offered the clearest argument for Napoli's sense of frustration: 1.8 for the visitors against 0.8 for Juventus. That does not mean every chance should have been scored, but it does indicate Napoli created the stronger body of opportunities.
Manager Stefan Saladino felt his side were better. The numbers support his assessment of the chance creation, while the scoreline shows the limits of that superiority on the day.

It was also another entry in Pio Esposito's exceptional run. He has now scored in five consecutive appearances: Lazio, Real Sociedad, Sampdoria, Cracovia and Juventus. His tracked club-season totals rise to 21 goals and 15 assists.

The result takes Napoli to 56 points from 23 league games, with 17 wins, five draws and one defeat. Juventus move to 48 points. Crucially, Roma also drew their 23rd match and remain three points behind the leaders.
The Scudetto race is alive. Napoli have not delivered a knockout blow to Juventus, but neither have they surrendered ground to Roma.
articles.label: SERIE A · JUVENTUS 1–1 NAPOLI · MATCHDAY 23

articles.headline: ROMA FAIL TO CAPITALISE: NAPOLI'S THREE-POINT CUSHION SURVIVES
articles.dek: Roma draw their 23rd league match, leaving Napoli top on 56 points and Roma second on 53 — with equal games played.
body: NAPLES — The nervous wait after Napoli's 1–1 draw with Juventus has ended with an unexpected reprieve for the league leaders: Roma also drew.

That is the only confirmed result detail from Roma's latest league fixture. The opponent, scoreline, scorers and match events are not established in the available record. What the updated table does confirm is the consequence.
Napoli have 56 points after 23 matches. Roma have 53 after 23. The gap remains three points, precisely where it stood before this round began.

For a brief period after Napoli's final whistle in Turin, the title race felt vulnerable. Roma had an opportunity to close to one point with a victory. Instead, their own draw preserved the existing distance.
Juventus sit third on 48 points, eight behind Napoli. Bergamo Calcio are fourth on 43, while Milano FC and Lombardia FC each have 40. All six clubs have played 23 matches.

The underlying numbers offer a fascinating contrast between the top two. Roma have scored 48 league goals to Napoli's 43, but Napoli have conceded only 12 against Roma's 21. The leaders' defensive advantage remains significant.
There are 15 league matches remaining for Napoli. The title is far from decided, but each round in which Roma cannot close the gap increases the value of the points already banked.

Now the rivalry takes another form. Napoli's next confirmed fixture is a cup match away to Roma on 31 January. League points will not be awarded that night, but pride and momentum certainly will be at stake.
articles.label: SERIE A · JUVENTUS 1–1 NAPOLI · MATCHDAY 23

articles.headline: FIVE STRAIGHT: PIO ESPOSITO'S SCORING RUN REACHES JUVENTUS
articles.dek: After goals against Lazio, Sociedad, Sampdoria and Cracovia, Pio adds a top-corner finish in Turin.
body: One match can produce a spectacular goal. Five consecutive scoring appearances suggest something more durable.

Pio Esposito's 11th-minute strike against Juventus was not a scrappy deflection or a lucky bounce. McTominay supplied the pass, and Esposito blasted his finish into the top corner to give Napoli an early lead.
That extended his scoring sequence through five successive Napoli appearances: Lazio, Real Sociedad, Sampdoria, KS Cracovia and Juventus.

The run has not been built on finishing alone. Against Lazio he contributed to teammates' goals. Against Cracovia he scored twice, assisted McTominay and saw a saved attempt create the rebound from which Davies scored unassisted.
The official distinction matters: Davies's goal carried no assist, even though Esposito's shot made the rebound possible. There is no need to inflate a statistic to appreciate the contribution.

With the Juventus goal, the tracker now records Esposito at 21 goals and 15 assists in the club season. Maximilian Beier remains on 20 goals and 11 assists after his two-assist night against Cracovia.

Esposito's next challenge is not simply to keep scoring. It is to turn that individual form into victories against opponents who can absorb pressure, recover from an early setback and punish missed chances.
Juventus did exactly that in Turin. Esposito gave Napoli the start they wanted; the team could not find a winner.
articles.label: SERIE A · JUVENTUS 1–1 NAPOLI · MATCHDAY 23

articles.headline: THE SCORE WAS LEVEL. THE CHANCES WERE NOT.
articles.dek: Napoli's 1.8–0.8 xG advantage against Juventus points to a strong away performance — and an opportunity left on the pitch.
body: Napoli and Juventus each scored once, but their expected-goals totals tell an asymmetrical story. Napoli produced 1.8 xG; Juventus 0.8.

The one-goal margin in underlying chance quality does not prove Napoli were superior in every tactical phase. Expected goals are a measure of shot quality, not a complete account of possession, territory or defensive structure.

It does, however, lend weight to Saladino's post-match feeling that his team were the better side. Away against the club sitting third in Serie A, Napoli generated significantly more expected scoring value.
The chronology is revealing. Napoli led through Pio Esposito in the 11th minute; Francisco Conceição equalised eight minutes later. The remaining match time passed without a deciding goal.

In their previous two fixtures, Napoli had scored seven unanswered goals while allowing just 0.2 combined opposition xG: Sampdoria finished on 0.0 and Cracovia on 0.2. Juventus presented a sterner challenge, but Napoli still restricted them to 0.8.

There is no verified account here of specific Juventus tactical adjustments or individual defensive errors, so the analysis should not pretend otherwise. The reliable conclusion is simpler: Napoli were competitive, created more, and did not fully convert that advantage.
The defensive record over 23 league matches remains impressive: 12 goals conceded, compared with Roma's 21. Napoli's title case continues to rest on control as much as attacking talent.
The cup visit to Roma will provide a different test, and the league lead remains three points after Roma's own draw.
articles.label: SERIE A · JUVENTUS 1–1 NAPOLI · MATCHDAY 23

articles.headline: ROMA HANDED NAPOLI A LIFELINE. DON'T CONFUSE IT WITH A FREE PASS.
articles.dek: A sceptic sees relief in Roma's draw, but argues Napoli should still regret failing to finish Juventus off.
body: Napoli fans are celebrating a draw. Not their own, of course. Roma's.

I understand the relief. Napoli went to Juventus, scored early, conceded eight minutes later and could not find the second goal. Roma had a chance to cut the league gap to one point and instead drew their match as well. The lead stays at three.
But here is the inconvenient part: Napoli created 1.8 expected goals to Juventus's 0.8. That was a chance to win away against a contender, and they did not take it.
This is not a crisis. Napoli have 56 points from 23 matches, have lost only once in the league, and have conceded a mere 12 goals. Those are championship numbers.

Still, a title defence is measured by what you do with your openings. Pio Esposito is scoring in almost every match at the moment, and the supporting cast is capable of creating chances against serious opponents. A lead after eleven minutes should have been a platform.
Roma's failure to win changes the emotional temperature of the weekend, not the fundamental lesson. Napoli must be more clinical when they have the better of a match.
And now comes Roma in the cup. Do not tell me the league table decides that contest. It does not. Cup football offers no consolation points for being three clear in Serie A.
Napoli remain favourites to defend their position. They should treat this reprieve as motivation, not permission to relax.
articles.label: SERIE A · JUVENTUS 1–1 NAPOLI · MATCHDAY 23
CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · CRACOVIA 0–4 NAPOLI
articles.headline: FOUR BEFORE THE BREAK: NAPOLI SWEEP CRACOVIA AS PIO STRIKES TWICE
articles.dek: Napoli finish their league phase with a four-goal away victory, a Pio Esposito brace and just 0.2 expected goals conceded.
body: CRACOW — Napoli's Champions League league phase ended with a performance of overwhelming authority: four goals scored before halftime, none conceded across 90 minutes, and a final expected-goals balance of 4.3 to 0.2.

Scott McTominay opened the scoring in the 20th minute, converting from Pio Esposito's assist. Five minutes later, Maximilian Beier threaded a through ball to Esposito, who struck first time into the bottom corner.

At 35 minutes, Esposito was denied by the goalkeeper. Alphonso Davies was on hand to score from the rebound. The goal was officially unassisted, but Esposito's saved attempt was the direct precursor; both facts belong in the record.

The fourth arrived in the 39th minute. Beier again provided, Esposito again finished, and Napoli had a four-goal advantage with six minutes of normal first-half time remaining. Esposito struck the crossbar in the 45th minute as the visitors threatened to make the interval even more punishing.
Saladino made wholesale changes for the second half. No further goals followed, but neither did any serious revival by Cracovia. The hosts ended with zero shots on target; Napoli recorded eight.
The final figures were extraordinary: Cracovia 0.2 xG, Napoli 4.3. The scoreline reflected a match controlled at both ends, even after the manager reshaped his team at halftime.

Napoli's reward was tenth place in the Champions League league-phase table: 14 points from eight games, four wins, two draws and two losses, with 14 goals scored and 11 conceded. They go into the knockout play-offs, but their finish was much closer to direct qualification than to elimination.
Next comes Juventus at the Maradona on 27 January. This European display supplies momentum, and the second-half rotation may prove just as significant as the first-half goals.

articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · CRACOVIA 0–4 NAPOLI
articles.headline: TENTH, NOT SCRAPING THROUGH: NAPOLI MISS TOP EIGHT BY THE FINEST OF MARGINS
articles.dek: Fourteen points, tenth place and a league phase that was one late equaliser away from looking very different.
body: Napoli did not stumble into the Champions League knockout play-offs. They finished tenth, level on 14 points with the clubs in eighth and ninth, and with a final record of four wins, two draws and two defeats.

The closing table places Nottingham Forest eighth on 14 points and a plus-four goal difference. Ajax are ninth on 14 points and plus three; Napoli tenth on the same 14 points and plus three. Atlético Madrid are eleventh, also on 14 and plus three. The finer ordering among tied sides reflects competition tie-breaks beyond the displayed columns.

That proximity makes the draw at Real Sociedad especially painful. Napoli led through Pio Esposito's 26th-minute goal, but Beñat Turrientes equalised in the 88th minute with Sociedad's first shot on target. The game ended 1–1 despite Napoli producing 2.3 xG to Sociedad's 0.6.
Two points were lost in San Sebastián. A win there, with every other result unchanged, would have given Napoli 16 points — enough to clear the 14-point mark occupied by the final eighth-place side.

This is not a claim that the final hypothetical rank can be calculated from a single screenshot. It is a narrower and firmer conclusion: the late equaliser was the difference between the points Napoli actually earned and a total that would have secured direct passage past the play-off cut.
The 4–0 victory in Cracow, with 4.3 xG created and only 0.2 allowed, was a fitting final statement. Yet no emphatic final-night win could restore those two dropped points.
Napoli will contest the first knockout play-off. The opponent is not yet confirmed. That extra hurdle is frustrating, but it should not obscure the quality of a top-ten league-phase finish.
The question for Napoli now is whether the disappointment of missing the top eight becomes a burden — or an edge.

articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · CRACOVIA 0–4 NAPOLI
articles.headline: PIO AND BEIER ARE BUILDING SOMETHING DEFENCES CANNOT IGNORE
articles.dek: Esposito's two goals and an assist meet Beier's two assists in a devastating first half.
body: For fifteen minutes in Cracow, Napoli's front line operated at a tempo that made the match feel less like a contest than a demonstration.
At 20 minutes, Esposito was the supplier for McTominay. At 25, he was the scorer, running onto Beier's through ball and dispatching a first-time finish into the bottom corner.

His next major contribution will not appear in the official assists column. Esposito's shot was saved in the 35th minute, and Davies converted the follow-up. The scorer was Davies; the assist was none. But the chance originated with Esposito's effort.

At 39, Beier and Esposito combined again for Napoli's fourth. That made two goals for Esposito and two official assists for Beier before the interval. Esposito then struck the crossbar in the 45th minute.

The tracked club-season totals now stand at 20 goals and 15 assists for Esposito, and 20 goals and 11 assists for Beier. These are the season figures maintained by the club tracker, not a claim about official UEFA-only statistics.

The partnership has become more interesting because it is not confined to one pattern. Against Sampdoria, Beier came on for Esposito and assisted Nico Paz. Against Cracovia, the two worked in tandem to devastating effect.
The temptation is to crown one man as the attack's unquestioned centre. The better reading is that Napoli have two high-output forwards who can both finish and provide.
Juventus are next. If they stop one, can they stop the other?

articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · CRACOVIA 0–4 NAPOLI
articles.headline: EIGHT TO ZERO: THE NUMBER BEHIND NAPOLI'S EUROPEAN ROUT
articles.dek: Cracovia had no shots on target and only 0.2 xG; Napoli's control survived a wholesale halftime reshuffle.
body: The four goals will lead the highlight reel. The zero beside Cracovia's shots on target may tell the more consequential story.
Napoli put eight efforts on target and scored four times. Cracovia put none on target, finishing with 0.2 expected goals against Napoli's 4.3.
It would be inaccurate to turn zero shots on target into zero attempts of any kind. The confirmed figures concern shots on target and expected goals, not the full shot count.
What is certain is that Napoli did not need to rely on a string of goalkeeper saves to preserve the clean sheet. Cracovia never tested the goalkeeper with an on-target effort.

This came just three days after Sampdoria finished a 3–0 league defeat to Napoli with 0.0 xG. Across those two verified fixtures, Napoli have scored seven and conceded none, while allowing a combined 0.2 expected goals.

There is a tactical caveat: we do not have a complete substitution log or video analysis that would identify the precise mechanism of every defensive success. We do know the manager made wholesale halftime changes against Cracovia and the defensive outcome held.

That matters with Juventus and Roma approaching in domestic competition. The question is no longer whether the preferred eleven can control an opponent, but whether the wider squad can preserve the standard when the calendar demands rotation.
A strong opponent may create more than 0.2 xG. Napoli's challenge is to maintain their discipline when the margin for error narrows.

articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · CRACOVIA 0–4 NAPOLI
articles.headline: FOUR-NIL IS BEAUTIFUL. BUT JUVENTUS WON'T BE CRACOVIA.
articles.dek: A sceptical columnist applauds Napoli's final-night European display while warning against confusing dominance with inevitability.
body: I am told that Napoli have silenced their critics. Four goals before halftime, eight shots on target to none, 4.3 xG to 0.2. It is a persuasive set of numbers. It is not a trophy.
Let us be clear: Napoli were excellent against Cracovia. Esposito and Beier were irresistible in the opening period, Davies reacted well to a rebound, and McTominay provided the early breakthrough.
I also give Saladino credit for the halftime rotation. He did not need to chase a fifth goal for the sake of a headline. The game ended 4–0, the clean sheet intact, and key legs potentially spared.
But if you want a true measure of Napoli's Champions League league phase, look at tenth place. Fourteen points, level with eighth. This was a strong campaign with a costly flaw, not a flawless march.
That flaw has a name: the late equaliser at Real Sociedad. The match Napoli should have closed out is the one that kept the top eight just out of reach.
The temptation now is to pretend a comfortable win in Cracow has repaired everything. It has not. The knockout play-off still lies ahead, and the opponent is still unknown.
And before that, Juventus visit Naples. Napoli are eight points ahead in Serie A, but that is exactly why Juventus have something urgent to prove.
Praise Napoli tonight. They earned it. Then ask them to earn it again against a side that can actually make them suffer.

articles.label: SERIE A · SAMPDORIA 0–3 NAPOLI
articles.headline: THREE GOALS. ZERO EXPECTED GOALS ALLOWED. NAPOLI MAKE A STATEMENT.
articles.dek: Pio Esposito scores twice, Nico Paz supplies one and scores another, and Sampdoria finish with 0.0 xG in a complete away performance.
body: GENOA — Napoli needed an answer after the bitter late Champions League draw at Real Sociedad. They delivered one so emphatic that the most startling number was not on the scoreboard: Sampdoria finished with 0.0 expected goals.

Pio Esposito opened the scoring in the 25th minute. Alphonso Davies turned and found the striker, who struck first time, off the post and in. No settling touch, no hesitation; a finish that rewarded the pass with immediate conviction.
The visitors led 1–0 at the interval. Sampdoria's expected goals stood at 0.0, evidence of a half in which the hosts had generated virtually no scoring threat.

It was a scoreline Napoli knew could be dangerous. Four days earlier they had led Sociedad by the same margin before conceding in the 88th minute. Here the response was to widen the lead rather than protect a fragile advantage.
In the 59th minute Nico Paz provided for Esposito, who completed his brace. Two goals for the centre-forward, with two different suppliers.

Esposito later made way for Maximilian Beier. The change did not blunt Napoli's attack. At 84 minutes Beier passed to Paz, who scored Napoli's third, completing a goal-and-assist evening for the midfielder.
Full time: Sampdoria 0, Napoli 3. The hosts' expected-goals figure remained 0.0 through the entire match. The statistic is not a claim that no shots were taken; it is the verified in-game xG total.

Napoli moved to 55 points from 22 Serie A matches, with 42 scored and only 11 conceded. Roma's updated total of 52 from the same number of matches ensures there is no room for celebration without concentration.
The next trip is to KS Cracovia in the Champions League on 24 January, followed by Juventus at home in the league three days later. On this evidence, Napoli are entering that stretch with authority.

articles.label: THE CONNECTION · PAZ AND PIO
articles.headline: PIO SCORES TWO. PAZ DOES BOTH. AND BEIER CHANGES THE GAME FROM THE BENCH.
articles.dek: A look at the connections behind Napoli's three goals, with a brace for Esposito and a goal and assist for Paz.
body: Some performances are defined by one player. Napoli's 3–0 win at Sampdoria was defined by how the players connected.

The opening goal belonged to Esposito's technique, but Davies made it possible. He turned, picked the pass and gave the striker a chance to strike first time. The ball hit the post before crossing the line.
At 59 minutes Paz became the provider. His pass found Esposito for the second, taking the forward to 18 tracked club goals and 14 assists this season.
The move also captured the value of a side that can create for its striker from different areas and different players. Moore supplied Esposito against Real Sociedad; Davies and Paz did so here.
Then came a revealing substitution. Esposito went off and Beier came on. Rather than forcing the replacement into a hunt for his own goal, Beier found Paz for the third at 84 minutes.

Paz finished with one goal and one assist. Beier registered an assist, taking his tracked season contribution to 20 goals and nine assists. The goal scorers made the headlines; the combinations explain the result.
None of this requires invented dribbles, distances or passing percentages. Three documented scoring moves are enough to show the range of Napoli's attack.
And with a Champions League trip and a home date against Juventus looming, the ability to rotate one prolific forward for another is more than a luxury.

articles.label: THE NUMBER · 0.0 XG
articles.headline: ZERO POINT ZERO: WHAT NAPOLI'S DEFENSIVE BLANK ACTUALLY TELLS US.
articles.dek: Sampdoria registered 0.0 expected goals over 90 minutes. The number is extraordinary, but it deserves careful interpretation.
body: The headline number from Genoa will be repeated in bars and on message boards: Sampdoria 0.0 expected goals. Not at halftime. At full time.

Expected goals is a measure of chance quality, not simply possession, shots or attacking intention. A displayed 0.0 should not be misreported as proof that Sampdoria had zero shots. The confirmed fact is the game's full-time xG reading.
Still, as an indicator of attacking opportunities, it is remarkable. Napoli went away from home and conceded no measurable expected-goal value while scoring three times.

There is an important comparison with the previous Champions League fixture. Real Sociedad had only 0.1 xG at halftime but later equalised, finishing with 0.6. Defensive control at one moment did not guarantee the result.
Against Sampdoria, Napoli paired control with a second goal in the 59th minute and a third in the 84th. The scoreline began to reflect the balance of the performance.
Without the complete match footage, we cannot responsibly attribute the 0.0 to a particular pressing trigger, individual defender or tactical adjustment. Those details remain unverified.
What we can say is that the result strengthened Napoli's already formidable league record: 17 wins, four draws, one defeat, 42 goals scored and 11 conceded after 22 matches.
Juventus visit on 27 January. Against stronger opposition, the defensive numbers may not look so pristine. But Napoli's latest benchmark is now exceptionally high.

articles.label: THE TABLE · THREE POINTS
articles.headline: ROMA WON'T GO AWAY. NEITHER WILL JUVENTUS. NAPOLI CANNOT BLINK.
articles.dek: Napoli 55, Roma 52, Juventus 47: all three have played 22 matches, with a crucial head-to-head approaching.
body: Napoli's win at Sampdoria was comprehensive. Their reward in the table? A three-point lead, and not a point more.
The latest standings put the champions on 55 points after 22 matches. Roma have 52 after 22, Juventus 47 after 22. This is no longer a table complicated by unequal games played among the top three.
Roma have won 16 of 22 matches and scored 46 goals, four more than Napoli. The leaders' response is at the other end: just 11 conceded, compared with Roma's 19.
Juventus, eight points behind Napoli, are next up in the league on 27 January. Their 47 points and 47 goals scored mark them as a serious opponent, whatever the current gap.
Bergamo Calcio are fourth on 42 points. Milano FC sit fifth with 39 and Lombardia FC sixth with 37. The upper end of the league is taking shape, but the championship is not settled.

The Juventus match follows a Champions League trip to KS Cracovia on 24 January, while a domestic cup trip to Roma follows on 31 January. It is a demanding calendar, and the games will not wait for Napoli to recover.

There are no verified scores or scorers for Roma's and Juventus's latest victories in the information available to this newsroom. The table tells us they gained ground; the precise details are not confirmed.
For now the arithmetic is brutally simple. Napoli are first, Roma are three points behind, and the next league opponent is Juventus.

articles.label: BELLANDI · THE BIGGER TEST
articles.headline: BELLANDI: DON'T HAND OUT THE SCUDETTO FOR BEATING A TEAM WITH 0.0 XG.
articles.dek: Napoli were excellent at Sampdoria. Their biggest tests of January are still ahead.
body: Let me be clear before anyone accuses me of refusing to applaud a good performance: Napoli were excellent at Sampdoria. Three goals, a clean sheet, a Pio Esposito brace and a full-time opposition xG of 0.0. There is very little to criticise about the result.
But one of the great traps in football is allowing the ease of one match to colour the difficulty of the next.

Roma are three points behind. Juventus are eight back and coming to Naples on 27 January. Before that, Napoli travel to KS Cracovia in the Champions League, a competition in which they already know a first knockout-phase playoff awaits.
The win in Genoa tells us Napoli can turn control into a comfortable margin. That is progress from the frustration in San Sebastián, where a late equaliser erased a deserved lead.
It does not tell us that Juventus will offer the same opportunities or that Roma will stop collecting points. They have both kept winning.
I like what Paz and Beier did for the third goal. I like that Esposito's replacement provided an assist. I like that Napoli found three goals without conceding a meaningful chance.

But I reserve the superlatives for the next stretch. The best teams are not the ones that look unbeatable when the opposition cannot threaten them. They are the ones that look composed when the opposition can.
Saladino's Napoli have earned praise tonight. The schedule is about to ask whether they have earned something greater.

articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE · SOCIEDAD 1–1 NAPOLI
articles.imageCredit: Pio Esposito Napoli archive portrait, not a photograph of the match
articles.headline: EIGHTY-EIGHT MINUTES. ONE SHOT ON TARGET. TWO POINTS LEFT IN SPAIN.
articles.dek: Esposito's magnificent 26th-minute finish is cancelled by Turrientes with Sociedad's first shot on target. Napoli dominate the expected-goals battle 2.3–0.6 but return from Spain with a 1–1 draw.
body: SAN SEBASTIÁN — Football sometimes reserves its cruelest answers for a team that has been asking all the questions. Napoli travelled to Real Sociedad, controlled enough of the contest to build a 2.3–0.6 expected-goals advantage, and came away with a 1–1 draw.

The first thirty minutes suggested another rewarding European away night. At 26 minutes, Mikey Moore found Pio Esposito near the edge of the penalty area. The striker struck into the top corner, a finish worthy of deciding a Champions League encounter.
Napoli took the 1–0 advantage into the interval. Sociedad had registered just 0.1 expected goals in the opening half, a striking measure of how little danger the hosts had created.
Moore might have added a goal to his assist, but a close-range attempt was stopped by Sociedad goalkeeper Pickford. The minute of that chance has not been confirmed.

In the 71st minute, substitute Anton Stach tested Pickford and was denied. Esposito reacted to the rebound, only to see Pickford intervene once more. Two saves in the same attacking sequence kept the hosts within a single goal.
For much of the evening the pattern looked clear: Napoli finding opportunities, Pickford keeping the deficit at one and Sociedad searching for a way into the contest.

Then came the 88th minute. Beñat Turrientes equalised, and the most painful detail was that it came with Sociedad's first shot on target. It was not necessarily their first shot of the night; the distinction matters.
The equaliser stood. There would be no reported late winner, and the referee's final whistle left both sides with one goal.
Napoli's expected goals finished at 2.3, Sociedad's at 0.6. That is not the scoreline, and it cannot award the visitors the extra two points they needed.
For a club whose European ambitions grew after last season's Champions League final defeat, it is another uncomfortable lesson in the difference between controlling chances and winning matches.

Esposito's goal and Moore's creativity deserve attention. So does Pickford's performance. But the headline belongs to an eighty-eighth-minute equaliser that turned an impressive away showing into a bitter draw.
Napoli's next confirmed fixture is Sampdoria away in Serie A on January 21. The Champions League draw leaves Napoli's domestic standing unchanged at 52 points from 21 league games.

articles.label: THE GOALKEEPER · PICKFORD'S RESISTANCE
articles.imageCredit: Napoli archive artwork · illustrative, not an image of Pickford in this match
articles.headline: PICKFORD LEFT HIS MARK. NAPOLI'S FINISHING DID THE REST.
articles.dek: Three confirmed Pickford interventions — on Moore, Stach and Pio — help explain how Napoli finished with one goal despite 2.3 xG.
body: A week after David de Gea made exactly five saves against Napoli in Florence, another goalkeeper has shaped a result against the same attack. This time it was Pickford for Real Sociedad in the Champions League.
The 1–1 draw will be remembered for Turrientes' late equaliser, but Napoli's inability to establish a two-goal cushion owed much to the man standing between the posts at the other end.
Moore created Napoli's opener for Esposito in the 26th minute, then went close himself. His attempt from short range brought a Pickford save, denying the youngster a goal to accompany his assist.
In the 71st minute came a sequence of particularly painful detail. Substitute Anton Stach shot; Pickford saved. Esposito collected the rebound and tried to finish; Pickford saved again.
The goalkeeper had made two interventions without the visitors ever quite escaping the same attacking moment. Napoli's advantage remained 1–0.

At least three individual Pickford saves are confirmed in the match account: the Moore opportunity and the two in minute 71. His official total across the match has not been supplied, and should not be guessed.

Nor does an xG total translate automatically into an obligation to score a fixed number of goals. Napoli produced 2.3 expected goals, a measure of chance quality; Pickford's work helped prevent those openings becoming a decisive advantage.
Esposito's top-corner opener proved the attack could beat him. The frustration is that Napoli never found a second breakthrough after that moment.
Fiorentina's De Gea had put in a 9.8-rated, exactly-five-save display to earn a 0–0 draw. Pickford's figures and rating are not known, but the influence of the reported saves is unmistakable.
The individual saves explain part of the result. The other part arrived in the 88th minute, when Turrientes turned Sociedad's first effort on target into an equaliser.
Goalkeepers are not required to dominate every minute to become the deciding characters in a game. Pickford kept Sociedad alive long enough for one shot to change the narrative.
Napoli's forwards will know their chances were sufficient to win on a different night. Their next test is to make those chances count before their opponents get one.

articles.label: EXPECTED GOALS · NAPOLI 2.3 / SOCIEDAD 0.6
articles.imageCredit: Napoli archive player image · illustrative
articles.headline: 2.3 TO 0.6. WHY THE NUMBERS TELL ONLY HALF THE STORY.
articles.dek: Napoli held Sociedad to 0.1 first-half xG and 0.6 for the full match. Yet an 88th-minute goal on the hosts' first shot on target erased the lead.
body: Napoli's 1–1 draw with Real Sociedad is the kind of match that tempts an analyst to show one number and declare the argument settled. It is also a warning against doing exactly that.
The final expected-goals balance was 2.3–0.6 in Napoli's favour. These totals estimate the quality of the chances each side created; they do not guarantee an outcome.
At the interval, with the visitors leading 1–0, Sociedad had generated just 0.1 xG. The first half was not merely good because Napoli led; the hosts had created very little danger.

Pio Esposito's 26th-minute goal, supplied by Mikey Moore, gave the visitors a tangible reward. A strike from the edge of the box into the top corner is an expression of finishing skill, not just chance volume.
Moore later had a close-range attempt saved by Pickford. Then came the 71st-minute double stop, with Stach denied first and Esposito unable to beat Pickford on the rebound.
The pair of saves in the same attacking sequence reminds us that raw totals alone do not convey the rhythm of an evening: Napoli had sustained pressure and chances without securing a second goal.

Sociedad's first attempt on target did not come until the 88th minute. Beñat Turrientes scored with it. That fact does not prove Sociedad had taken no shots previously; a shot need not be on target to count as an attempt.

From those known facts, the central tactical question is clear: how did Napoli allow a situation in which the hosts' first shot on target could equalise so late? The build-up, defensive positioning and exact sequence of that goal have not been independently reported.
It would be irresponsible to single out a named defender, formation change or goalkeeper without that evidence. Analysis begins with the events that are actually documented.

Another legitimate question concerns the opportunities Napoli failed to convert. The 2.3 xG says the visitors generated meaningful chances. Pickford's specific saves describe why several of them stayed off the scoreboard.
A European draw on the road need not be disastrous in itself, but the outcome carries a sharper sting when one team created most of the quality and controlled the first half so thoroughly.
Rather than a grand tactical revolution, the next step may simply be to turn an advantage into a margin that an opponent's one good moment cannot erase.

articles.label: PIO AND MOORE · A BRIGHT SPOT IN SPAIN
articles.imageCredit: Pio Esposito Napoli archive portrait
articles.headline: MOORE FOUND HIM. PIO FINISHED IT. NAPOLI'S YOUNG ATTACK DID ITS PART.
articles.dek: Pio Esposito scores a remarkable 26th-minute goal from Mikey Moore's assist as the pair show genuine promise amid another European frustration.
body: One of the hardest tasks after a disappointing result is to separate an individual's performance from the final score. Napoli's 1–1 draw in Spain offers two players who deserve that distinction.
In the 26th minute, Mikey Moore supplied Pio Esposito near the edge of the Real Sociedad area. The forward found the top corner with a superb finish to give Napoli the lead.
That was the side of Esposito on display against Lazio too: an attacker who can finish decisively while also reading the runs and movement of those around him.
Against Lazio he scored once and assisted twice. Against Sociedad he switched back to the role of finisher, while Moore provided the final pass.
The result of that combination was an away Champions League lead in a first half in which Sociedad generated only 0.1 xG.
Moore's contribution did not end with his assist. He also found space for an attempt from close range, forcing a save from Pickford.
Esposito nearly added another contribution in the 71st minute. Anton Stach came off the bench, had a shot stopped, and Pio could not convert the rebound because Pickford made a second save.

Those moments are important because the 88th-minute Sociedad equaliser risks swallowing every positive from the evening. It should not erase the quality of the opening goal or the chances that followed.

Esposito now has a tracked tally of 16 goals and 14 assists for Napoli across club competitions this season. Moore is credited with the assist on this particular goal; his full current-season cumulative assist total has not been independently reconciled.

The challenge for the wider squad is to ensure promising individual attacking work translates into finished matches, particularly against European opposition capable of punishing even limited openings.
It is tempting to ask one teenager or one forward to solve every problem. A serious team has to be more demanding of its collective game management than that.
Tonight Moore and Esposito supplied a goal worthy of winning a Champions League match. They deserved more protection from the scoreline than they ultimately received.

articles.label: BELLANDI'S COLUMN · EUROPEAN FRUSTRATION
articles.imageCredit: Napoli archive artwork · illustrative
articles.headline: BELLANDI: THE XG WON'T GIVE YOU BACK THE EIGHTY-EIGHTH MINUTE.
articles.dek: Bellandi refuses to ignore Napoli's commanding chance creation, but argues that late concessions have become too costly when the prize is Europe.
body: Show me the expected goals. Go on. Napoli 2.3, Real Sociedad 0.6. Put the numbers in large print and tell me which team should have taken control of the result.
Now show me the scoreboard: Real Sociedad 1, Napoli 1. That is the number the Champions League records.
To be fair to Napoli, the opening performance was excellent. A beautiful Pio Esposito finish from Mikey Moore's pass at 26 minutes, and just 0.1 first-half xG conceded by the visitors.
But if you are going to praise control, you also have to ask how it ended. Sociedad found an equaliser through Turrientes in the 88th minute with their first shot on target.
An opposition goalkeeper made the night harder. Pickford denied Moore from close range, then Stach and Pio on consecutive chances in minute 71. That is significant, and it deserves to be said.

Yet Napoli spent more than an hour protecting only a single-goal advantage. One fine save is inconvenient. Three important stops and a late concession are a test of whether you can manage a match that refuses to be comfortable.

I do not know which defender was nearest to Turrientes, which decision was taken on the touchline or how the equalising move developed. Those details have not been supplied, so I will not pretend they have.
What I do know is that this squad has been recognised among Europe's finest. Saladino was named Manager of the Year; five Napoli players were selected in UEFA's Team of the Year.
Those honours make this draw feel more demanding, not less. Napoli reached last season's Champions League final and lost. Their stated ambitions deserve standards proportionate to their quality.

Some supporters will point out that any point away from home in Europe can help. Others will argue Napoli dropped two. With no verified current Champions League standings in front of us, nobody should declare the broader qualification arithmetic settled.
The immediate arithmetic is simpler: Napoli scored once, Sociedad scored once, and most of the quality chances belonged to Napoli. Good football produced a draw.
This is not a verdict that Napoli lack talent. It is an argument that a team built to challenge in Europe must get better at ensuring one opposing moment cannot erase an evening's worth of good work.

articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 3–1 LAZIO · FULL TIME
articles.imageCredit: Pio Esposito Napoli archive portrait, not a photo from the Lazio match
articles.headline: PIO'S NIGHT. THREE GOALS. THREE POINTS. NAPOLI ANSWER FLORENCE.
articles.dek: Pio Esposito scores once and supplies two assists as Beier and McTominay complete Napoli's 3–1 win over Lazio. Cancellieri gets a 93rd-minute consolation.
body: NAPLES — Four days after leaving Florence with an infuriating scoreless draw, Napoli returned to the Maradona determined to make their chances count. Lazio were beaten 3–1, and Pio Esposito was at the heart of every home goal.
The first arrived in the 29th minute. Maximilian Beier provided the pass; Esposito supplied the finish. Napoli had found a way through where five saved shots had brought nothing against Fiorentina.

Five minutes later the same partnership struck again, with the roles reversed. Esposito played in Beier, who scored Napoli's second on 34 minutes. The two forwards had traded a goal and an assist before Lazio could settle.
The half ended 2–0. Scott McTominay had also tested Lazio with a long-range effort, but his attempt was stopped before the break.
After the restart, Esposito twice released Beier into dangerous shooting situations. Both times Lazio goalkeeper Motta made the save, preventing the visitors from falling further behind.
For a moment the evening had an echo of Florence, where David de Gea had made exactly five saves and earned a 9.8 keeper rating. But against Lazio the early goals had already changed the contest.
McTominay eventually found the third in the second half, finishing another chance created by Esposito. The precise scoring minute was not confirmed, but the identity of the creator was clear.
One goal, two assists and two additional dangerous passes for saved Beier attempts gave Esposito an exceptional afternoon of work across the forward line.
Lazio found a late consolation through Matteo Cancellieri in the 93rd minute. It cost Napoli a fourth successive league team clean sheet, but it was too late to alter the final outcome.
The victory takes Napoli to 52 points from 21 Serie A matches: 16 wins, four draws, one defeat, 39 goals scored and only 11 conceded.
Roma's next match has not yet been played, leaving them on 46 points after 20 games. Napoli's current margin is six points, although Roma hold a game in hand.

With Real Sociedad waiting in Spain on January 16, the league leaders have more immediate work. They leave the Maradona with the response they needed, and a strike partnership giving them plenty of reasons for optimism.

articles.label: PIO ESPOSITO · GOAL AND TWO ASSISTS
articles.imageCredit: Pio Esposito in Napoli colours · archive portrait
articles.headline: MORE THAN A NUMBER NINE. PIO ESPOSITO IS BECOMING NAPOLI'S CREATOR.
articles.dek: Esposito provides a goal, two assists, and two more passes that force saves from Lazio goalkeeper Motta. His 2028–29 tracked club tally rises to 15 goals and 14 assists.
body: For a centre-forward, one goal in a 3–1 win is a solid evening. For Pio Esposito, it was almost the least revealing part of his performance against Lazio.
He scored in the 29th minute, converting Maximilian Beier's pass to deliver Napoli's opener after the scoreless frustration against Fiorentina.
Five minutes later the positions were reversed. Esposito assisted Beier, turning their partnership into a two-goal advantage before halftime.
The third Napoli goal was a second assist for Esposito. Scott McTominay finished from his supply during the second half, giving the striker a direct part in every Napoli goal.
But the official tally does not show everything. Esposito also found Beier twice more after halftime; both opportunities ended with saves from Lazio goalkeeper Motta.
Those chances do not count as assists, and pretending otherwise would diminish what he actually achieved. One goal and two credited assists were already enough.

Across Napoli club competitions this season, the latest tracked figure is now fifteen goals and fourteen assists for Esposito. The creativity is approaching the output traditionally expected from an attacking midfielder.
Beier also prospered from the partnership. He scored the second, assisted the first and twice forced further goalkeeper interventions.
The common temptation is to compare the two forwards or cast their success as a battle for status. Lazio demonstrated something more useful: their ability to serve each other.

Against well-organised sides, the capacity to switch scorer and creator adds unpredictability. Esposito's biggest development may be the willingness to make that final pass rather than chase another personal goal.
The Champions League away trip to Real Sociedad is next. The question is whether this combination can impose itself on a continental opponent as convincingly as it did on Lazio.
Napoli need not search too far to find an elite playmaker for their attack. One of them has spent this season wearing the number nine's responsibilities and far more besides.

articles.label: STRIKER PARTNERSHIP · BEIER AND ESPOSITO
articles.imageCredit: Maximilian Beier Napoli archive portrait
articles.headline: BEIER TO PIO. PIO TO BEIER. LAZIO NEVER SOLVED THE EXCHANGE.
articles.dek: The two Napoli forwards each scored and assisted the other, and Esposito set Beier up for two more chances saved by Motta.
body: The most telling fact about Napoli's opening half against Lazio was not merely that two strikers scored. It was that each striker created for the other.
At 29 minutes Beier assisted Esposito. At 34, Esposito assisted Beier. That five-minute exchange turned Napoli's possession into a lead they never surrendered.
A fixed pair of roles might have been easier for the opposition to anticipate: one forward creates, the other finishes. Napoli's pair refused to follow that script.
The second half added more evidence. Twice Esposito found Beier with a pass that gave the German a shooting opportunity, and twice goalkeeper Motta had to intervene.
Those two saved attempts are separate from the first-half goal and assist. Beier's official return remains one goal and one assist in the match, not a second-half brace.
The goalkeeper's work is an important part of the interpretation. Lazio did not surrender on every chance, but Napoli had already made themselves difficult to catch.
McTominay's later finish, again from an Esposito assist, offered a third attacking route. The same forward who linked with Beier was able to create for a midfielder arriving to finish.

That diversity is more significant than any speculative changes to formation. No tactical switch or specific instruction from the coaching staff has been independently established from the match account.
Against Fiorentina, David de Gea's five saves had kept the visitors scoreless. Against Lazio, Motta denied Beier twice, but the first two good combinations were already in the net.

Both forwards have substantial season output: Esposito now fifteen goals and fourteen assists, Beier twenty goals and eight assists, using the last tracked Napoli club totals plus their confirmed Lazio contributions.
Napoli must balance the benefits of an in-form partnership against a congested schedule. Real Sociedad await in Europe three days after Lazio, though the next lineup is not confirmed.
For the present, the clearest tactical conclusion is the simplest one: two forwards who know when to run, pass and finish can be more valuable together than the sum of their individual reputations.

articles.label: NAPOLI 52 FROM 21 · ROMA 46 FROM 20
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork · illustrative, not an image of the current league table
articles.headline: SIX POINTS CLEAR. ONE GAME IN HAND. NAPOLI KEEP THEIR NERVE.
articles.dek: Napoli respond to the Florence draw with a 3–1 win over Lazio and move to 52 points in 21 games. Roma remain on 46 from 20, with their next match still to be played.
body: NAPLES — Napoli did what was required against Lazio. A 3–1 win at home extended their Serie A points total to fifty-two and forced the chasers to respond.

Their twenty-one-match record is sixteen wins, four draws and one loss, with thirty-nine goals scored and eleven conceded. The latest result adds three points, three goals and one conceded to the Florence numbers.
Roma remain on forty-six points after twenty matches, because their next league fixture has not yet been played. At this moment Napoli hold a six-point lead.

That sentence requires its second half. Roma have a game in hand. The teams have not completed the same number of matches, so six points is the current margin, not a declaration of an unassailable advantage.
After Fiorentina 0–0 Napoli, the two sides had played twenty games apiece and were separated by just three points. The Lazio win has given the leaders breathing room before Roma's next kick-off.
There is no verified result to attach to Roma's upcoming fixture, and reporting one in advance would be an invention. The other challengers' latest games likewise await confirmation.

From the January 10 standings, Bergamo Calcio and Juventus were both on forty-one points after twenty matches. Those remain historical snapshot figures rather than a freshly confirmed post-Lazio ranking.
Napoli can control only their own football. Against Lazio, Pio Esposito scored and assisted twice, while Beier and McTominay completed the home team's three goals.
Cancellieri scored Lazio's only goal in the 93rd minute, ending a three-match Napoli league run without conceding. Eleven goals allowed in twenty-one fixtures is still a formidable defensive record.

The leaders' next confirmed game is not another domestic fixture. Real Sociedad await away in the Champions League on January 16, a contest played against the backdrop of last season's agonising European final defeat.
Saladino's Manager of the Year recognition and five Napoli players in the 2029 UEFA Team of the Year provide the grander context. None of those honours changes the league table by a single point.
Napoli stand six clear for now, Roma have a game in hand, and the winter schedule offers no room for complacency. Lazio was the necessary answer.

articles.label: BELLANDI'S COLUMN · THE VALUE OF THREE GOALS
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork · illustrative
articles.headline: BELLANDI: NAPOLI DIDN'T NEED AN EXCUSE. THEY NEEDED GOALS. THEY FOUND THREE.
articles.dek: The caustic pundit gives Esposito and Beier their due, but questions what one dominant home match actually tells us about Napoli's European ambitions.
body: A goalkeeper makes five saves, collects a 9.8 rating and preserves a nil-nil in Florence. Napoli supporters are right to feel unfortunate, and yet a title contender cannot live forever on explanations.
Against Lazio, Napoli gave a far more persuasive reply. The first goal arrived in the 29th minute through Esposito, the second five minutes later through Beier, and the third through McTominay.
Esposito provided the night's real distinction: one goal, two assists and two more passes for Beier chances stopped by Motta. There is no need to exaggerate that performance.
Beier did his own work, scoring and assisting before Motta denied him twice in the second half. That is a striker contributing across the pitch rather than waiting for service.
The two forwards have become a genuinely interesting partnership precisely because they can exchange responsibilities. One creates, the other finishes, then they reverse it.

The caution is obvious: this was a home win over Lazio, not the final examination of the season. Napoli have not yet settled their Champions League ambitions because they scored three on a January afternoon.
Real Sociedad away arrives next, and the calibre of opposition and setting will test how transferable this attacking fluidity truly is.

The 93rd-minute Cancellieri goal is a detail worth noting. Conceding late did not matter to the outcome, but the defence will not want to develop a habit of switching off with a match almost complete.
Nor should the league lead become a sedative. Napoli have fifty-two points after twenty-one; Roma, with their next match unplayed, have forty-six from twenty. Six clear, but Roma hold a game in hand.

Saladino has been named Manager of the Year. Five Napoli players were selected in UEFA's Team of the Year. I have praised those achievements and still maintain that the European trophy is the measure this squad now wants most.
To be fair, this performance supplied an encouraging answer to one criticism. A team that makes chances should score them, and against Lazio Napoli did exactly that.
Now do it in Spain. That is not an insult. It is the standard this Napoli have earned the right to be judged against.

articles.label: SERIE A · FIORENTINA 0–0 NAPOLI · FULL TIME
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork · illustrative, not a photograph from Florence
articles.headline: FIVE SAVES. NINE-POINT-EIGHT. DE GEA HOLDS NAPOLI SCORELESS.
articles.dek: De Gea stops all five Napoli shots on target, earns a 9.8 goalkeeper rating and keeps Fiorentina level. Paz denied at 50 minutes; Beier's chance is tipped onto the post. Napoli leave Florence with a point.
body: FLORENCE — Fiorentina 0, Napoli 0. The away supporters could scarcely believe it. Five shots on target, five saves by David de Gea, and a goalkeeper rating of 9.8 tell the story of the league leaders' frustration.
Three of De Gea's five saves came during the opening forty-five minutes. Napoli created the danger, but each intervention kept the score level. It was 0–0 at the interval.
Five minutes after the restart Nico Paz tested the goalkeeper again. De Gea held firm with his fourth save, frustrating a side that had already spent much of the match looking for a breakthrough.
The fifth was the most dramatic. Maximilian Beier struck from close range; De Gea managed to reach it, and the ball deflected off the post and away. On a different night that is a match-winning goal.
All five saves are confirmed as the goalkeeper's exact total, rather than an estimate from the most memorable highlights. The 9.8 rating appears on the postmatch goalkeeper display.
Napoli continued to press without finding a goal. No scoring involvement was credited to either side. The final whistle confirmed a goalless draw and a share of the points.

The visitors can at least take comfort in a third consecutive Serie A team clean sheet. After beating Parma 2–0 and Palermo 1–0, Napoli have conceded no goals across their three January league matches.
But the draw has a cost. Napoli move to forty-nine points from twenty games; Roma, now on forty-six from twenty, sit just three behind. The two clubs have played the same number of fixtures.
Roma's position gives the contest its larger significance. Bergamo Calcio and Juventus are on forty-one points apiece after twenty, leaving Napoli still first but no longer comfortable.

The biggest question for the coming days is whether Napoli can translate their chance creation into goals against similarly inspired resistance. The evidence from Florence is that De Gea was outstanding, not that Napoli produced nothing.
Next is Lazio at the Maradona on January 13, where winning would provide the strongest answer. For now, five saves from one goalkeeper have left the title leaders with a point rather than three.

articles.label: GOALKEEPER PERFORMANCE · DE GEA 9.8 · FIVE SAVES
articles.imageCredit: Beier in Napoli colours · archive portrait, not a photograph of the De Gea save
articles.headline: THE HAND THAT FOUND THE POST. DE GEA'S FIVE-SAVE MASTERCLASS.
articles.dek: De Gea produced exactly five saves in the 0–0 draw, three before halftime and two after. His fingertip intervention against Beier denied Napoli the winner.
body: The scorebook lists Fiorentina 0–0 Napoli. In reality, it was an evening on which David de Gea turned a game of repeated Napoli opportunities into a portrait of goalkeeping excellence.
The goalkeeper's postmatch rating was 9.8. He made exactly five saves, all five decisive in preserving his team's clean sheet.
Three came during the first half. They set the pattern: Napoli advanced, created an opportunity, and the goalkeeper made the last intervention.
The fourth save was recorded in the 50th minute. Nico Paz, one of Napoli's creative leaders, was the player denied.
Then came Beier. The forward found himself with a point-blank opportunity and looked set to open the scoring, only for De Gea to get a hand to the ball and turn the chance against the woodwork.
The ball hit the post and went out. It was simultaneously a great chance for Napoli and a spectacular denial by the Fiorentina goalkeeper.

Such performances demand careful interpretation. The visitors will ask whether an earlier shot or another finishing angle might have changed the outcome, but five saves and a 9.8 rating are strong evidence that the opposition goalkeeper was the defining player.
One should not invent a higher saves tally because the performance felt impossible to beat. Five is the exact total, and the match finished goalless.
Neither Paz nor Beier scored, but each forced the goalkeeper into crucial work. The striker in particular had every reason to think his close-range attempt could have settled the contest.
For Napoli the next challenge is finding the finish that can defeat even an inspired goalkeeper. For De Gea, the night in Florence will be remembered as the time he personally preserved a point.

articles.label: SERIE A · 20 PLAYED EACH · NAPOLI 49 · ROMA 46
articles.imageCredit: Napoli season archive artwork · illustrative, not a photograph of the current standings
articles.headline: ROMA ARE THREE BACK. FIORENTINA MAKE THE SCUDETTO RACE TIGHTER.
articles.dek: Napoli still lead Serie A with 49 points, but Roma have 46 after the same 20 games. Atalanta and Juventus sit on 41. The January draw turns title-race optimism into renewed pressure.
body: ITALY — Napoli remain first in Serie A. After twenty games they have forty-nine points, fifteen wins, four draws and one defeat, thirty-six goals scored and ten conceded.
