The numbers still make an impressive case for Stefan Saladino's team. But the newest league table is a reminder that strong performance cannot be measured only in unbeaten runs and clean sheets.
Roma have forty-six points from the same twenty games. The gap is three, not the five that separated them when both clubs had played eighteen matches earlier in January.
That shift matters because the teams can now be compared without games-in-hand qualifications. Napoli have 49/20, Roma 46/20, and Roma sit second.
Roma's twenty-match record is fourteen wins, four draws and two losses, with forty-two scored and eighteen conceded, a goal difference of plus twenty-four.
Napoli's corresponding goal difference stands at plus twenty-six. Their defensive advantage is striking: only ten conceded, compared with Roma's eighteen.

Bergamo Calcio, Atalanta's in-game name, are third on forty-one from twenty. Juventus are fourth with forty-one, both eight points behind Napoli. Lombardia FC occupy fifth on thirty-four, Parma sixth on thirty-three.
These figures are confirmed from the latest table after Fiorentina 0–0 Napoli. The lower places are not shown and should not be treated as verified.
A zero-zero draw in Florence would have felt less costly had Roma remained further behind. Instead, the latest standings make clear that the Scudetto is still a contest.
Saladino has just been named Manager of the Year, with five Napoli players also selected in UEFA's Team of the Year. Neither distinction awards league points.
Lazio visit Naples on January 13. Napoli can restore momentum at home, but the champions' margin now demands attention at every match.

articles.label: FIORENTINA DRAW · FIVE SAVES · LAZIO NEXT
articles.imageCredit: Alphonso Davies in Napoli colours · archive portrait, not a photograph of the Fiorentina match
articles.headline: DOMINANCE ISN'T A GOAL. NAPOLI MUST FIND ANOTHER WAY.
articles.dek: De Gea's flawless five-save night explains the scoreline, but consecutive 1–0 and 0–0 league games raise an important question about Napoli's finishing as Roma close to three points.
body: NAPLES — It would be absurd to look at a goalkeeper rated 9.8 with five saves and pretend Napoli had no attacking ideas. David de Gea was magnificent. That is the starting point.

But it would be equally shortsighted to ignore a developing question about whether Napoli's promising possession and chances can always be converted when the opposing goalkeeper is in the kind of form seen in Florence.
Against Palermo, Desplanches made several important stops before Olise finally scored in the 44th minute. Napoli won 1–0, but the winner did not arrive easily.
Against Fiorentina, De Gea saved every shot on target, including a dangerous Nico Paz effort in the 50th minute and Beier's shot that was diverted onto the post.

There is a difference between demanding a more ruthless finish and blaming attackers for superhuman goalkeeping. Both parts of the story can be true: Napoli got into dangerous positions, and the final touch did not produce a goal.

One possible answer is variety. Faster cutbacks, movement that shifts a keeper before the shot, and second-ball positioning are worth examining. None of those tactical suggestions is a claim about an actual instruction given from the bench.

Another answer is the existing squad depth. The Palermo match saw João Neves enter at halftime and Davies and Calafiori at 65 minutes. There are options for adjusting Napoli's rhythm without discarding the team's balance.
The defensive platform is extraordinary. Three straight league clean sheets and ten conceded in twenty matches are not symptoms of a team in crisis.

Nor is the league position. Napoli have forty-nine points and remain first. Roma, however, have forty-six from twenty and sit just three behind. The lead leaves little room for frustration to become habit.
Lazio at home on January 13 offers the next chance for the attack to answer. The season's awards are deserved; the season's biggest arguments are still being settled on the pitch.

articles.label: OFFICIAL HONOUR · STEFAN SALADINO NAMED MANAGER OF THE YEAR
articles.imageCredit: Napoli season archive artwork · illustrative club image, not a photograph of the award presentation
articles.headline: MANAGER OF THE YEAR. SALADINO'S NAPOLI REVOLUTION RECOGNISED.
articles.dek: Stefan Saladino has been named Manager of the Year. The Napoli coach receives the honour amid a 48-point Serie A title defence and a newly announced UEFA Team of the Year containing five of his players.
body: NAPLES — It is the sort of announcement that transforms the mood of an entire football city. Stefan Saladino has been named Manager of the Year, an individual honour that arrives with his Napoli team leading Serie A and five of its players selected in the UEFA Team of the Year.

The award was confirmed during the extraordinary sequence of developments surrounding Napoli's January 7 victory over Palermo. The formal awarding organisation and the edition year have not been specified in the announcement available to this publication; the honour itself is unequivocal: Manager of the Year.

To understand the reaction in Naples, it is necessary to consider the distance travelled under Saladino. Last season's Napoli became undefeated Serie A champions with twenty-eight wins and ten draws across thirty-eight matches.

That campaign also brought Coppa Italia success. Europe ended more painfully: Napoli reached the Champions League final but lost 3–2 after extra time to Paris Saint-Germain, Kvaratskhelia delivering the decisive blow.

The current season has brought its own questions. Napoli suffered a first Serie A defeat to Roma in October after a forty-four-match unbeaten league run. A New Year's Day Supercoppa final against Roma ended 0–0 before the Roman side won 4–3 on penalties.

Rather than letting those setbacks dictate the story, Napoli have kept winning league games. A 2–0 victory over Parma on January 4 was followed by a 1–0 home win against Palermo on January 7, Michael Olise scoring the only goal.

After nineteen league games, Napoli own forty-eight points, fifteen wins, three draws and one defeat. Thirty-six goals scored and ten conceded have sustained a lead at the top. The latest rival standings, however, have not all been refreshed since the January 4 snapshot.

Perhaps the most emphatic tribute to the wider project arrived at almost the same moment as the managerial award: Olise, João Neves, Alphonso Davies, Alessandro Bastoni and Alessandro Buongiorno appeared in the UEFA Team of the Year.

Three members of Napoli's defence were selected in a back four. Two more earned midfield places. That is unusually concentrated recognition for a club that has also invested heavily in assembling its squad.

Their story is not without cost or consequence. Endrick, sold by Napoli to Barcelona for $310 million during the summer, also made the final UEFA XI, now wearing Barcelona colours. Beier, one of Napoli's leading scorers, was shortlisted but missed the team.

In Naples, one individual trophy will not conclude the debate about Saladino's legacy. The club wants another Scudetto and the Champions League title that eluded it last May. Recognition raises expectations as much as it rewards achievement.

But for this moment, there is no need to look ahead to the next test. A manager who assembled an unbeaten champion, won the domestic cup, reached a European final and is leading the league again has been recognised with the title Manager of the Year.
The season continues at Fiorentina on January 10. Today, however, the biggest headline belongs to the man on Napoli's touchline.

articles.label: UEFA TEAM OF THE YEAR 2029 · FIVE NAPOLI SELECTIONS
articles.imageCredit: Alessandro Bastoni in Napoli colours · archive player portrait, not the official UEFA award graphic
articles.headline: FIVE OF EUROPE'S BEST ELEVEN WEAR NAPOLI BLUE.
articles.dek: Davies, Bastoni and Buongiorno claim three places in UEFA's back four. Olise and João Neves take two midfield slots. The final Team of the Year contains five players from Saladino's Napoli.
body: EUROPE — One of the most startling images of the new year is a UEFA Team of the Year formation containing a near-solid wall of Napoli badges. Five of the eleven selected players represent Stefan Saladino's club.

The Napoli five are Alphonso Davies, Alessandro Bastoni and Alessandro Buongiorno in defence, plus Michael Olise and João Neves in midfield. Every one of those names appears in the final XI shown by UEFA's in-game announcement, not merely on an earlier shortlist.

The full forward pairing is Endrick of Barcelona and his club teammate Lamine Yamal. In midfield, Pedri of Barcelona, Olise of Napoli, Jamal Musiala of Bayern and Neves of Napoli form the selected quartet.
The back four are Davies of Napoli, Bastoni of Napoli, Nuno Mendes of Paris Saint-Germain and Buongiorno of Napoli. Barcelona goalkeeper Joan García completes the eleven.
That translates to three Napoli defenders in a four-man line and two Napoli midfielders in a four-man selection. Neither forward and not the goalkeeper spot belongs to Napoli.

At the latest manager-confirmed ratings, Neves is a 93-overall midfielder aged twenty-four. Olise, twenty-seven, is rated 91. Both have become major figures in the club's transition from promising squad to an established European force.

The defensive contingent is just as revealing. Bastoni is 91 overall at twenty-nine years old, Davies 89 at twenty-eight and Buongiorno 88 at twenty-nine. Their quality is no longer being discussed only in a Serie A context.
Napoli have conceded ten goals through nineteen league matches. That is a team defensive figure, not a claim that each UEFA honouree played every minute or participated in every clean sheet.

The selection follows last season's remarkable Italian league championship and Coppa Italia title, along with a Champions League final run that ended in defeat to Paris Saint-Germain. UEFA recognition and winning Europe's premier club trophy are separate achievements.

Olise gave Napoli another reason to celebrate on the field by scoring the winner against Palermo in the 44th minute, with Lutsharel Geertruida providing the assist. Neves later entered that match at halftime.

The club that supplied the other most prominent group of names was Barcelona: Endrick, Lamine Yamal, Pedri and Joan García all appear in the XI wearing Barcelona colours. Former Napoli striker Endrick's place adds a pointed subplot after his summer transfer.

Maximilian Beier, nominated for a forward position alongside Erling Haaland, Endrick and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, did not make the final eleven. The successful selections in those positions were Endrick and Yamal.
The numbers are unambiguous. Five of eleven. Three in the back four. Two in midfield. A manager named Manager of the Year. Naples is having an extraordinary awards moment.

articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 1–0 PALERMO · OLISE 44′ (GEERTRUIDA)
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork · illustrative; not a match-day photograph of Olise or Palermo
articles.headline: OLISE BREAKS PALERMO. NAPOLI REACH 48 POINTS.
articles.dek: Desplanches repeatedly stands in Napoli's way, but Michael Olise scores in the 44th minute from Geertruida's assist. Napoli close out a 1–0 home win, with Neves, Davies and Calafiori joining from the bench.
body: NAPLES — Michael Olise scored in the 44th minute and Napoli defeated Palermo 1–0 at home on January 7, collecting a further three points to reach forty-eight after nineteen Serie A matches.

The visitors had survived for much of the opening half thanks in large part to their goalkeeper, Sebastiano Desplanches. Within the first three minutes he produced an excellent save from an early Napoli chance.
The home side maintained the pressure, creating opportunities and keeping Palermo pinned into extended defensive phases. In the 27th minute, Nico Paz went close but Desplanches stopped his attempt.

From a corner, Napoli also struck the crossbar with a header. The identity of the player who met the delivery is not established in the available match sequence, but the woodwork was another reprieve for Palermo.

There was a further scramble inside the box, though Napoli could not produce a clean shot through the bodies. It was the kind of stretch in which a side's territorial dominance seems unable to unlock a well-protected goal.

The breakthrough came with halftime approaching. At forty-four minutes, Michael Olise finished to make it 1–0. Lutsharel Geertruida supplied the assist, a decisive contribution from the versatile defender.
Napoli went into the interval one goal ahead after a half that had yielded repeated pressure but only one conversion. Desplanches was central to Palermo's resistance.

At halftime, Napoli introduced João Neves. An extraordinary squad-strength detail: the Portugal international is rated 93 overall in Napoli's latest squad figures, yet could begin this league match among the substitutes.
In the 65th minute, Alphonso Davies and Riccardo Calafiori entered as well. Their latest recorded ratings are 89 and 87 respectively. The identity of the players they replaced has not been confirmed.

Napoli continued to threaten. Maximilian Beier had an effort denied from point-blank range, while Neves later found Mikey Moore in space inside the penalty area. A poor first touch prevented Moore from producing the finish.

Palermo offered little sustained attacking threat by the account of the game. That does not mean the Napoli goalkeeper's identity or a personal save count can be assumed. What is established is a team clean sheet and a 1–0 final score.

The final whistle completed a controlled, if not clinical, afternoon. Napoli now have fifteen league wins, three draws and one loss, with thirty-six scored, ten conceded and a goal difference of plus twenty-six.
This was also a measure of progress from December's 2–2 away draw with Palermo, when Napoli had to rescue a point through Beier's late equaliser.

The next league assignment is Fiorentina away on January 10. Napoli travel there after six league points in two January games, with the club's European awards celebrations providing an extraordinary backdrop.

articles.label: UEFA TEAM OF THE YEAR · BEIER NOMINATED BUT OMITTED
articles.imageCredit: Maximilian Beier in Napoli colours · archive portrait, not an image from the UEFA awards presentation
articles.headline: BEIER MAKES THE SHORTLIST. ENDRICK MAKES THE XI. A NAPOLI TWIST.
articles.dek: Five Napoli stars were chosen, but Beier was not one of them. His former attacking colleague Endrick—sold to Barcelona for $310 million—is in the final forward pairing with Lamine Yamal.
body: NAPLES — Five Napoli players have just been selected for the UEFA Team of the Year, and yet one of the club's most prolific footballers has a perfectly legitimate reason to feel disappointed.
Maximilian Beier was on the forwards shortlist alongside Erling Haaland, Endrick and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. His name does not appear among the two men in the selected forward line.

Instead, UEFA's final in-game XI shows Endrick and Lamine Yamal up front, both wearing Barcelona colours. The selection is a reminder that a nomination and a place in the final team are different accomplishments.

For Napoli supporters, Endrick's presence is especially charged. He played for the Italian club before completing a $310 million summer transfer to Barcelona. Last season, he was part of the same Napoli attack whose contributions helped take the club to a Scudetto and a Champions League final.
Beier stayed. At the latest verified 2028–29 club scoring tally, he had nineteen goals and seven assists, the figures recorded through Napoli's December league win against Bologna.
He also came close to scoring against Palermo on January 7, but Desplanches denied him from point-blank range as Napoli edged a 1–0 victory. The saved effort does not alter Beier's scoring total.

His talent has hardly gone unrecognised. A place on the UEFA forwards shortlist is a significant distinction and places him in elite company. Still, being shortlisted while a former teammate takes one of the two final spots makes an irresistible football argument.

The competition is formidable. A final XI is not an objective ranking of which Napoli forward contributed most to the club's league season, and the shortlisting announcement does not give us the complete voting criteria.
Nor should the club's five successful selections be overlooked. Neves, Olise, Davies, Bastoni and Buongiorno represent one of the most concentrated showings by a single team in this eleven.
One may conclude that Beier deserved a place, or believe that Endrick and Yamal were the stronger selections. What is not in dispute is that the final UEFA graphic places Beier outside the eleven.

Perhaps the only sensible reaction for Napoli is to keep giving Beier matches of consequence. Fiorentina are next, while Real Sociedad and KS Cracovia await in the Champions League schedule later this month.
The final European honours have been announced. Beier's season is nowhere near finished.

articles.label: PALERMO BENCH · NEVES 93 OVR · DAVIES 89 · CALAFIORI 87
articles.imageCredit: Alphonso Davies in Napoli colours · archive portrait, not an image from his 65th-minute appearance against Palermo
articles.headline: SURVIVE THE FIRST HALF. THEN NAPOLI SEND ON JOÃO NEVES.
articles.dek: Palermo trailed only 1–0 at halftime. Napoli then introduced 93-rated João Neves, followed by 89-rated Davies and 87-rated Calafiori at 65 minutes. An extraordinary demonstration of first-team depth.
body: NAPLES — It may be the most dispiriting substitution board an opponent in Serie A could see. After surviving forty-five minutes of Napoli pressure and trailing just 1–0, Palermo watched João Neves arrive for the second half.
Neves is twenty-four years old, rated 93 overall in Napoli's current squad figures and selected in the UEFA Team of the Year. Yet he was available to enter from the bench at halftime against Palermo.

For Palermo, the first half had already required serious defensive work. Desplanches stopped an early chance and a Nico Paz effort in the 27th minute. A header from a Napoli corner struck the crossbar.
Only Michael Olise's finish from Geertruida's assist in the 44th minute separated the teams at the interval. The narrow scoreline kept the match theoretically open.

Neves did not score the second goal, because there was no second goal. His significance lies in the options available to Napoli, and in how the match remained under the hosts' control with him introduced.
In the second half, Neves carved out an opening by passing into space for Mikey Moore inside the box. Moore's first touch was poor and the opportunity failed to become a finish.
At sixty-five minutes, there was more reinforcement. Alphonso Davies, twenty-eight and rated 89, entered alongside Riccardo Calafiori, twenty-six and rated 87.

Davies is also a member of the UEFA Team of the Year final XI, one of three Napoli defenders among the eleven selected. Calafiori is not in that eleven, but his current rating is still the mark of a major first-team talent.
Napoli's attacking performance was not clinical. Maximilian Beier was denied at point-blank range. The deficit never widened. Desplanches deserves recognition for keeping the score down.

But when discussing a title contender, the bench is part of the competitive equation. Strong substitutes can refresh the midfield, change the threat profile and make a narrow advantage harder to overturn.

The conclusion does not require inventing a specific tactical switch, a player replaced or a behind-the-scenes instruction. The confirmed substitutions alone make the case: Neves at halftime, Davies and Calafiori in the 65th.
With Fiorentina away on January 10 and another string of league, cup and European fixtures ahead, Napoli will need precisely that luxury of choice.
The hardest part may be convincing elite footballers to accept the minutes available. On this day, the depth helped Napoli finish the job.

articles.label: BELLANDI · MANAGER OF THE YEAR · AWARDS VS TROPHIES
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork · illustrative, not a photograph of the author or awards night
articles.headline: BELLANDI: FIVE IN THE XI. MANAGER OF THE YEAR. NOW WIN THE BIG ONE.
articles.dek: Matteo Bellandi congratulates Saladino on deserved recognition—but insists the Supercoppa defeat and last season's Champions League final loss make European silverware the next measure of this Napoli era.
body: By Matteo Bellandi — Let us begin with the obvious, because disagreement without acknowledging reality is just theatre. Stefan Saladino has been named Manager of the Year. Five Napoli players are in the UEFA Team of the Year. Both distinctions are substantial, and both deserve congratulations.
Last season's undefeated Scudetto and Coppa Italia victory were no accident. Those achievements established a standard at Napoli that would have seemed almost outrageous earlier in the project.

Nor can the European accomplishments be brushed aside. Napoli reached the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain and fell just short, losing 3–2 after extra time. That is a great season, not a failure masquerading as one.
But football does not stop at awards ceremonies. There are still unanswered questions about how Napoli cope in knockout matches when their attacking superiority does not produce goals.

Look at the recent Supercoppa. Napoli were held to 0–0 against Milano FC in the semifinal and advanced on penalties. Then came another 0–0 against Roma in the final, this time followed by a 4–3 shootout defeat.

Goalkeepers made important saves and Napoli were not a weak side. Nevertheless, two scoreless cup matches are relevant evidence when the discussion turns from recognition to winning the next major final.

Palermo at home offered a different kind of warning. Napoli dominated long stretches, forced major saves from Desplanches and struck the crossbar. Yet one Olise goal was enough, and the match remained 1–0.
To be clear, that is not a bad result. It is three points, a clean sheet and a fifteenth league win in nineteen matches. A title contender must also know how to win ugly.

Still, the manager award, five UEFA selections and the current domestic record increase expectations. When João Neves, one of those UEFA honourees, can start a half on the bench, the squad is equipped to compete against the very best.

Michael Olise, João Neves, Davies, Bastoni, Buongiorno: those are not merely promising names. They are five players identified among Europe's best eleven. With that comes the responsibility to perform on the biggest nights.

Some will say it is ungracious to introduce criticism amid celebrations. I disagree. The correct tribute to an ambitious manager is to judge him against the highest standard, not lower the bar because a medal has arrived.
Saladino is Manager of the Year. Napoli have earned the applause. The next challenge is not proving the club belongs in elite company. The selection already suggests it does.
The next challenge is lifting the European trophy that escaped them last season. Fiorentina and a difficult January await first. That is the reality of managing a club built to win.

articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 2–0 PARMA · FULL TIME
articles.imageCredit: Pio Esposito in Napoli colours · archive player portrait; not a photo from the Parma match
articles.headline: BACK TO BUSINESS. DE BRUYNE, PIO AND PEACOCK PUT PARMA AWAY.
articles.dek: Napoli respond to their Supercoppa final heartbreak with a 2–0 home victory: a 27th-minute De Bruyne goal-line finish, Pio Esposito's 75th-minute rebound, and a clean sheet for Peacock.
body: NAPLES — The first league game after losing a trophy can tell a club a great deal about its ability to respond. Napoli returned to Serie A on January 4 and defeated Parma 2–0 at home, scoring once in each half of the confirmed match timeline through Kevin De Bruyne and Pio Esposito. In goal, Peacock completed a clean sheet.

The result came three days after the New Year's Day Supercoppa final against Roma. Meret had produced an outstanding performance in that 0–0 match, but Roma won 4–3 from the spot. Napoli had to restore their momentum quickly.
At 27 minutes, Pio Esposito found space to shoot from an extraordinarily narrow angle. His effort nearly crept in at the near post, reached the goal line and seemed almost to stop there.

De Bruyne arrived before the defence could recover, crashing in to send the loose ball over the line. The scorer was De Bruyne; the goal was recorded as unassisted. Pio's initial effort created the moment but is not credited as an assist.
For a side that had failed to score in two consecutive Supercoppa fixtures, even a slightly improbable finish in the 27th minute felt like a welcome return of attacking reward.
Napoli waited until the 75th minute for their second. Scott McTominay tested the Parma goalkeeper, whose save spilled the ball back into play. Esposito reacted first and slotted away the rebound.

That goal belongs to Pio Esposito and was also unassisted. McTominay's saved shot preceded the finish, but there was no credited assist. Pio's tally moves to fourteen Napoli club goals this season at the last verified count, with twelve assists unchanged.

Peacock started in goal and kept Parma out. His clean sheet arrived at an interesting time, after Meret's major saves against Roma and an earlier strong display from Peacock in Palermo. The exact number of saves he made against Parma has not been confirmed.
Napoli's scoreline remained 2–0 at the final whistle. No substitutions, half-time score, shot totals or additional decisive passages were supplied in the confirmed match record.

The victory takes the Partenopei to forty-five points after eighteen league games, with fourteen wins, three draws and one defeat. Only ten goals have been conceded in league play, and the team now has a plus twenty-five goal difference.

Roma, Supercoppa winners just days earlier, sit third in the latest confirmed league table with forty points from eighteen matches. Bergamo Calcio are second with forty-one points from nineteen. Napoli are five points clear of Roma on equal games played, while leading Bergamo by four despite having played once fewer.
There will be little time to celebrate. Palermo visit on January 7, a date that will stir memories of December's difficult 2–2 away draw, when Napoli needed Beier's late equaliser to take a point.
For now, Napoli have delivered the response supporters needed. No trophy celebration, no shootout, no frantic comeback. Just two goals, three league points and a goalkeeper who kept the sheet clean.

articles.label: GOALKEEPER WATCH · PEACOCK SHUTOUT · MERET'S ROMA HEROICS
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork · illustrative; not a photograph of Peacock, Meret or the Parma match
articles.headline: MERET WAS BRILLIANT. PEACOCK ANSWERS WITH A CLEAN SHEET.
articles.dek: The Supercoppa defeat placed Meret's performance in the spotlight. Three days later, Peacock keeps Parma scoreless. Napoli's competition for the goalkeeper shirt is becoming a strength and a selection puzzle.
body: NAPLES — Alex Meret had every reason to believe his performance against Roma deserved more than a defeat. He made important stops during the Supercoppa final, then saved Vaz's penalty. Roma nevertheless claimed the trophy when Bahoya converted the fifth kick.
Three days later, Napoli named Peacock in goal against Parma, and the younger goalkeeper left with a clean sheet. Napoli won 2–0 through goals by Kevin De Bruyne and Pio Esposito.
That sequence makes the conversation about Napoli's goalkeeper position more complex, not less. Meret stood up to an intense final; Peacock answered in a league match the club needed to win.

Peacock has already demonstrated his ability under pressure. In December's 2–2 draw at Palermo, he made six saves in the first half alone. Napoli conceded twice in that match, a reminder that a goalkeeper's individual work does not always map cleanly onto the scoreline.

Against Parma, the clean sheet is established. The number and type of Peacock's saves are not. It would be unfair to invent a second spectacular statistical display simply because the result was favourable.

Meret's other recent contribution is worth recalling: the Champions League shutout in Dortmund. There, Napoli secured a 1–0 away victory. The Supercoppa performance against Roma added another major stage to his season.

Neither goalkeeper deserves to be evaluated solely through a binary column of wins and losses. Meret impressed even as Napoli lost the final. Peacock did his job in a 2–0 league victory and has made important stops on other occasions.
The question of who starts the next game cannot be answered by the final score alone. Opponent, preparation, fitness and the rhythm of a crowded calendar all matter.
Napoli's next league opponent, Palermo, already know what it is like to face Peacock. Whether he or Meret is selected on January 7 has not been confirmed.
The club's defensive numbers offer context: ten goals conceded in eighteen Serie A matches, with Napoli leading the table. Two credible options in goal are an asset in that kind of campaign.

For now, the smart conclusion is a modest one. Meret has not lost his claim because Roma won a shootout; Peacock has strengthened his own case with a clean sheet. The decision remains a live football question.

articles.label: SERIE A · VERIFIED TOP SIX · 4 JANUARY 2029
articles.imageCredit: Maximilian Beier in Napoli colours · archive portrait illustrating Napoli's title campaign; not a photograph of the Parma match
articles.headline: FORTY-FIVE POINTS. ROMA FIVE BACK. NAPOLI RECLAIM THE NARRATIVE.
articles.dek: The post-Parma table places Napoli first at 45 points in 18 games, four ahead of Bergamo Calcio despite a game in hand and five clear of Roma after the same number of fixtures.
body: ITALY — Roma lifted the Supercoppa against Napoli on January 1. Three days later, the Serie A table offered a very different picture of the two clubs' campaigns. Napoli defeated Parma 2–0 and now lead the league on forty-five points from eighteen matches.
Roma sit third on forty points, also after eighteen games. The five-point gap is directly comparable: both clubs have played the same number of league fixtures.
Between them, Bergamo Calcio occupy second with forty-one points from nineteen games. That is a four-point deficit despite Bergamo having played one fixture more than Napoli.

Juventus stand fourth with thirty-eight points after nineteen games. Lombardia FC have thirty-four after twenty, while Parma remain sixth with thirty points from nineteen. These figures come from the latest confirmed top-six league-table snapshot.
Napoli's full league record reads fourteen wins, three draws and just one defeat. They have scored thirty-five times, conceded ten and built a goal difference of plus twenty-five.

Bergamo have scored forty-one goals, more than Napoli, but have also conceded twenty-one. Roma's thirty-seven goals and sixteen conceded place them at plus twenty-one. The difference in defensive numbers is one reason Napoli currently hold their advantage.

No one should pretend that the table is evenly balanced in games played beyond Napoli and Roma. Bergamo and Juventus have each played nineteen, Lombardia twenty and Parma nineteen. The points are verified, but the arithmetic of future results remains open.
Napoli's win over Parma arrived at a sensitive moment. Their Supercoppa final defeat to Roma could have triggered doubts about attacking composure after consecutive 0–0 cup fixtures.

Instead, De Bruyne struck in the 27th minute after Pio Esposito's sharp-angle attempt settled near the line, and Pio converted a rebound from McTominay's saved shot in the 75th. Peacock kept a clean sheet.
It does not erase the Supercoppa disappointment, nor does it place the league trophy in Naples already. But the league season and the cup final are separate competitions, with separate consequences.

Next comes Palermo on January 7. Napoli drew 2–2 away to that opponent in December and needed a late equaliser. A club seeking the Scudetto must turn league-table position into consistent performances against the teams it is expected to beat.
The latest numbers give Napoli a clear lead. Whether they can protect it through a relentless January is the next question.

articles.label: PIO ESPOSITO · 14 CLUB GOALS · PARMA 2–0
articles.imageCredit: Pio Esposito in Napoli colours · archive portrait, not an image of his Parma rebound goal
articles.headline: FIRST HE MADE THE GOAL. THEN PIO TOOK ONE FOR HIMSELF.
articles.dek: Pio's audacious 27th-minute effort helped create De Bruyne's opener without earning an assist. At 75 minutes, he was quickest to McTominay's saved shot and scored Napoli's second — his 14th club goal.
body: NAPLES — Football's official goal and assist columns tell a precise story about Napoli's 2–0 win over Parma. Pio Esposito left with one goal, no credited assist, and an attacking influence that went beyond either number.

In the 27th minute, Esposito tried his luck from a very sharp angle, aiming at the near post. Somehow the ball nearly crept in, reaching the goal line and lingering where a defender would least want it.

Kevin De Bruyne arrived to finish the loose ball, giving Napoli a 1–0 lead. The official scorer was De Bruyne, and there was no recorded assist for Pio. That does not diminish the inventive shot that put Parma in difficulty.
Seventy-five minutes into the game, the roles changed. Scott McTominay took a shot and the Parma goalkeeper saved it, but the ball remained live.

Esposito reacted to the rebound and slotted it home. This time the name beside the goal was his own. The strike was unassisted, because McTominay's prior saved effort did not produce an official assist.
The result was a curious symmetry: Pio's shot was followed by a De Bruyne goal in the first half; a McTominay shot was followed by Pio's own goal in the second.

At the last verified club tally, Esposito now has fourteen goals and twelve assists in Napoli competitions this season. His unsuccessful opening penalty in the Supercoppa final against Roma does not subtract from those achievements, just as shootout goals do not count toward them.
For Napoli, this was a useful response after the shootout defeat. The Supercoppa final was scoreless after ninety minutes and ended with Roma taking the trophy 4–3 from the spot.
Esposito had missed the opening penalty, stopped by Svilar. Three days later, in league play, he created danger and followed a saved shot to put the result beyond Parma.

The second goal also reflects a basic but vital attacking skill: anticipation. There is little glamour in scoring a loose-ball rebound compared with an extraordinary finish from distance, but a forward has to be there to take the opportunity.
Napoli's title challenge will demand plenty more of those moments. The next test is Palermo on January 7, when Esposito will again be asked to make chances and finish them.
His numbers record a fourteenth goal and unchanged twelve assists. The Parma performance illustrates why coaches and supporters also watch the actions immediately before a scoring touch.

articles.label: SUPERCOPPA FINAL · NAPOLI 0–0 ROMA · ROMA WIN 4–3 ON PENALTIES
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork; illustration, not a photograph from the Roma final
articles.headline: A FINAL LOST ON THE FIFTH KICK. ROMA LIFT THE SUPERCOPPA.
articles.dek: After a 0–0 New Year's Day final and outstanding performances from Meret and Svilar, Pio's opening miss and McTominay's unsuccessful fifth penalty leave Napoli beaten 4–3 on penalties. Bahoya delivers Roma's winning kick.
body: NAPLES — The first trophy of 2029 belongs to Roma. Napoli and Roma finished ninety minutes of the Supercoppa Italiana final without a goal, the neutral-venue contest defined by extraordinary interventions from Alex Meret and Mile Svilar. In the shootout, Roma won 4–3. Bahoya converted the fifth and decisive penalty. Napoli were left watching the celebrations.

It was the second successive scoreless Supercoppa match for Napoli, after the semifinal against Milano FC. This time there would be no repeat of the victorious shootout that Mikey Moore had settled against Milan on December 29.

Meret and Svilar were central characters well before the shootout. Both produced huge saves across the ninety minutes. The exact number, the minutes and the identity of every player denied have not been independently confirmed, and there is no need to invent them. Their influence on the scoreline was unmistakable.
Pio Esposito stepped up to open the penalties for Napoli. Svilar stopped him. Roma's Paulo Dybala then converted, and the Giallorossi held the advantage after the first round.
Michael Olise responded with a successful second Napoli penalty. Alex Meret then denied Vaz, a remarkable reversal that brought Napoli level at 1–1 after two penalties apiece.
Maximilian Beier converted Napoli's third, as he had in the semifinal against Milan. Theo scored for Roma. At the end of three rounds, both clubs had converted twice.

Nico Paz stepped forward for Napoli's fourth penalty and scored. Matías Soulé answered for Roma, producing a 3–3 shootout score after four rounds. Every kick had become an argument between precision and pressure.
Scott McTominay took Napoli's fifth. He did not score. How precisely his effort failed — whether saved or off target — has not been confirmed by the available match report and should not be invented.
Bahoya then delivered for Roma. His successful fifth kick brought their conversions to four, settled the shootout 4–3 and gave the club the Supercoppa trophy. All ten scheduled penalties were taken.

The sequence, for the record: Napoli — Pio Esposito saved, Olise scored, Beier scored, Nico Paz scored, McTominay missed. Roma — Dybala scored, Vaz saved by Meret, Theo scored, Soulé scored, Bahoya scored. Those penalties are shootout attempts, not official goals for season totals.

For Meret, this will be a particularly painful result. His performance during play kept Napoli on equal terms, and he gave the club a second chance from the spot by stopping Vaz. That contribution deserves to be recognised even as Roma celebrate.

For Napoli the disappointment cannot be disguised. They had been one match from a trophy, and it was their chief domestic title rival who took it. Roma had reached the final by beating Inter 3–2, while Napoli eliminated Milano FC 4–2 on penalties after a 0–0 semifinal.

The consequences must be kept in proportion. This was a Supercoppa final, not a Serie A match; the league table has not moved. Napoli's last confirmed league record remains 42 points from seventeen games, while Roma's latest verified league record is 36 after sixteen. A current like-for-like points gap cannot be asserted.

There will be another meeting. Napoli travel to Roma on January 31 for a separate domestic cup fixture, the round of which has not yet been confirmed. Before then, a demanding league and Champions League schedule awaits.

The next confirmed club fixture is Parma at home on January 4. After ninety minutes in which both goalkeepers refused to yield and a shootout separated by a single miss, Napoli must return to work without pretending the loss is anything less than it is: a final they wanted, and a trophy they did not win.

articles.label: THE GOALKEEPER DUEL · MERET AND SVILAR
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork; not a likeness of Meret or a match-action photograph
articles.headline: MERET DID EVERYTHING BUT LIFT THE TROPHY.
articles.dek: Two goalkeepers kept Napoli and Roma scoreless, and Meret saved Vaz's penalty to restore the shootout balance. Bahoya's late conversion makes that contribution no less significant.
body: NAPLES — Every final has a winner. Not every outstanding performance ends with a medal around the neck. Alex Meret left the Supercoppa final in the second category.

Napoli and Roma went through ninety minutes at 0–0, and both Meret and Roma goalkeeper Mile Svilar produced saves of enormous importance. The occasion did not lack drama; it lacked the one finish that would have prevented a penalty shootout.

There are no verified minute-by-minute breakdowns for these saves or official totals in the available match account. But the broad fact is beyond dispute: the two men in goal played major roles in taking the final to penalties.
Svilar kept his influence at the shootout's first kick, denying Pio Esposito. Roma's Dybala converted, giving Napoli an immediate problem.

Olise steadied Napoli with the next attempt, and Meret then intervened against Vaz. One save from each goalkeeper, the shootout tied at 1–1 after two rounds. This was not a contest in which Napoli were simply abandoned by their goalkeeper.
The third and fourth rounds passed without further misses: Beier and Paz scored for Napoli, Theo and Soulé scored for Roma.
Then came the defining fifth round. McTominay failed to convert, Bahoya scored, and Roma won the shootout 4–3. The precise manner of McTominay's unsuccessful attempt remains unverified.

Meret's season has featured scrutiny and competition for opportunities. Peacock's remarkable six first-half saves against Palermo offered a compelling story in December. Meret, meanwhile, had contributed a clean sheet in Dortmund and has now delivered a major performance on the New Year's Day stage.

Whether Meret should be Napoli's first-choice keeper is a separate question that depends on a wider body of performances. What the final established is that his contribution deserves far more than a line recording a defeat.
Svilar deserves his own credit, too. He stopped a penalty and was a decisive part of Roma keeping the game scoreless. Roma are champions, and their goalkeeper mattered.

There is no tactical virtue in turning an excellent goalkeeper performance into a scapegoat because of the final shootout result. Meret kept Napoli in the match. On this night, that was not quite enough.

articles.byline: Matteo Bellandi · La Voce del Calcio
articles.label: BELLANDI · A FINAL LOST, A QUESTION UNANSWERED
articles.imageCredit: Maximilian Beier in Napoli colours; club archive portrait, not an image from the Supercoppa final
articles.headline: BELLANDI: TWO GOALLESS CUP NIGHTS. NAPOLI CANNOT ASK PENALTIES TO DO EVERYTHING.
articles.dek: Maignan saved Napoli's chances in the semifinal, and Meret and Svilar dominated the final. The penalty missers will make headlines, but the deeper question concerns finishing games before the shootout.
body: Matteo Bellandi writes — A penalty shootout is a brutally efficient way to assign a winner to a match that resisted one for ninety minutes. It is less efficient as a method for identifying the cause of defeat.

Napoli have now played two consecutive scoreless Supercoppa matches. First came the 0–0 semifinal against Milano FC, survived 4–2 on penalties through Mikey Moore's decisive fifth kick. Then the January 1 final against Roma, lost 4–3 from the spot.

To reduce the final to Scott McTominay's unsuccessful fifth penalty would be convenient. It would also be inadequate. Ten penalties were taken, some scored, some missed. Napoli found themselves in the shootout because they had not scored during the match.

The semifinal against Milan gave the public specific examples of frustrated finishing: João Neves from distance, Alphonso Davies and Nico Paz from close range, all denied by Mike Maignan. Those are evidence of chances created as much as of chances not converted.

The Roma final is different in one important respect. Its confirmed account speaks of huge saves by Meret and Svilar, but does not detail the exact shooting chances and timings. Anyone claiming to know precisely which tactical move failed is pretending to knowledge the public record does not provide.
Yet the pattern worth examining remains: two important matches, two scoreless outcomes and two shootouts. Winning one of them made Napoli finalists. Losing the other made Roma champions.

Alex Meret has no reason to leave the pitch feeling that he failed his part. His crucial stop against Vaz restored the balance after Svilar's denial of Pio Esposito, and the goalkeeper had already impressed during play.

Nor is the point to erase Beier's excellent season or his continued composure from the spot, or to treat Pio's penalty failure as the entirety of his campaign. Beier has nineteen verified club goals and seven assists; Pio has thirteen and twelve at the last available totals.

What this team must avoid is allowing the emotional charge of a final defeat to obscure the everyday work of building a dependable attack. The January calendar contains a league game against Parma on the fourth, Palermo on the seventh, and Fiorentina on the tenth.

There will be further nights of high stakes, including a domestic cup trip to Roma on January 31. A team aiming at larger trophies cannot assume its goalkeeper will always manufacture another chance in a shootout.
Napoli are still very much in the Serie A race. The defeat changes nothing in the points table. But it raises a football question that the club's next performances will have to answer.

articles.label: EVERTON CONTACT · DI LORENZO'S FUTURE
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive artwork accompanying transfer coverage; not a photograph of Giovanni Di Lorenzo or an Everton meeting
articles.headline: EVERTON MAKE CONTACT. IS DI LORENZO'S NAPOLI STORY NEARING ITS END?
articles.dek: Everton have approached Giovanni Di Lorenzo, whose contract is running down and who does not currently intend to renew. No agreement or transfer has been confirmed, but Napoli may be approaching a succession decision.
body: NAPLES — One of Napoli's most familiar faces could be approaching a turning point. Everton have made an approach concerning Giovanni Di Lorenzo, the veteran defender whose Napoli contract is nearing its end.

The situation, as currently understood, includes three confirmed elements: the contact from Everton, an expiring deal at Napoli, and Di Lorenzo's unwillingness at present to sign a renewal. That does not make him an Everton player.

There is no confirmed transfer, signed pre-contract, accepted bid, agreement on wages or exact departure date. Nor has the form of Everton's approach been established — a potential summer move and an immediate January sale remain different propositions.

For Napoli, the question reaches beyond replacing a right-back on a team sheet. Di Lorenzo has represented continuity through changing squads, playing styles and transfer windows. His eventual departure would mark a change in the club's defensive identity.

That continuity matters even as the squad evolves. Kayode and Geertruida are among Napoli's available right-side defensive options. The question is how to balance younger minutes and tactical flexibility with the experience of a player who has been part of this club's recent history.

The club also has a packed January schedule. After the Supercoppa final defeat to Roma, Parma visit on January 4, followed by Palermo and Fiorentina. The number of fixtures gives any squad-planning decision immediate significance.

One possible outcome would see Di Lorenzo continue to contribute while his deal runs down. Another might bring an earlier change. No report at this stage is sufficient to declare which course Napoli or the player will choose.

Transfer stories often harden into false certainties once a possible destination is mentioned. Everton's interest is real within the current account, but a willingness to move, a final destination and a completed contract are not established facts.

No direct public quotation has been provided from Di Lorenzo, Everton or Napoli officials. His position about renewal is reported as part of the developing contract situation, not presented as a verbatim interview.

The timing is poignant. As Napoli recover from a final defeat to Roma and continue chasing other trophies, a familiar figure's future may be entering its last chapter. For now, that chapter is still being written.

articles.label: UEFA TEAM OF THE YEAR 2029 · FORWARD SHORTLIST
articles.imageCredit: Maximilian Beier in Napoli colours; Napoli club archive portrait
articles.headline: BEIER AMONG EUROPE'S ELITE: UEFA TEAM OF THE YEAR SHORTLIST.
articles.dek: La Gazzetta dello Sport names Napoli's Maximilian Beier alongside Haaland, Endrick and Kvaratskhelia among forwards shortlisted for the 2029 UEFA Team of the Year. Selection is not yet decided.
body: NAPLES — A difficult start to the new year has given Napoli a reason to celebrate one of its own. La Gazzetta dello Sport's January 4 report has named Maximilian Beier among the forwards shortlisted for the 2029 UEFA Team of the Year.
Four names were identified in the report: Erling Haaland, Endrick, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Maximilian Beier. Their inclusion on a shortlist is confirmed; the final selection has not been announced.

It is a striking list for a Napoli attacker to enter. Haaland brings one of the biggest reputations in world football. Endrick represents another formidable attacking talent. Kvaratskhelia carries particular resonance in Naples as a former Partenopei favourite.

Beier has earned his place in the conversation through output as well as moments that supporters remember. At the last verified tally in late December, the forward had nineteen goals and seven assists across Napoli club competitions in 2028–29.

Those totals capture only part of his influence. Beier scored both goals against Lazio on December 9, rescued a point late at Palermo on December 17, and pounced for the late winning goal against Bologna on Christmas Eve.

In the Supercoppa, his contribution came from the spot. Beier converted in the successful semifinal shootout against Milano FC and again in the final shootout against Roma, even though Roma ultimately took the trophy.
Penalty shootout conversions are not added to a player's official season goals or assists, and neither the nomination nor the final loss changes the last confirmed nineteen-goal, seven-assist total.

The shortlist is also an acknowledgement of the wider development of Napoli's attack. The club has endured costly moments, including the scoreless Supercoppa final, while continuing to produce individual performances worthy of European discussion.

Beier's presence beside Kvaratskhelia is an especially appealing football story. It invites a comparison across different periods of Napoli's history, not a claim that either player's achievements are identical.
With the Champions League fixtures at Real Sociedad on January 16 and KS Cracovia on January 24 still ahead, there is time for Napoli's leading scorer to influence how his season is remembered.
No vote count, ranking, final XI or award winner is established by the January 4 report. For now, recognition as a shortlisted forward is significant enough on its own.
Napoli may have lost the Supercoppa to Roma, but the club's leading attacker's European standing is going in the other direction. Beier has become a name that cannot easily be ignored.

articles.label: ARCHIVE · 1 JAN 2029 FINAL PREVIEW · BEFORE RESULT
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive image · illustrative; not a photograph from the still-unplayed Supercoppa final · This is the pre-match announcement, retained as a dated archive.
articles.headline: NEW YEAR'S DAY. NAPOLI–ROMA. A TROPHY WAITING FOR ONE OF THEM.
articles.dek: Published before kickoff: Napoli and Roma were confirmed for the Jan 1 neutral Supercoppa final. Roma subsequently won 4–3 on penalties after 0–0; see the newer match report.
body: NAPLES — Napoli will begin 2029 with the chance to win a trophy. The newly confirmed Supercoppa Italiana calendar sets the final against Roma for January 1, at a neutral venue. An opponent already known has now become an appointment.

The route was extraordinary. On December 29, Napoli drew 0–0 with Milano FC, the in-game name for AC Milan, in the semifinal. Mike Maignan denied João Neves from distance and Alphonso Davies and Nico Paz from closer range.

A scoreless contest led to penalties. Pio Esposito scored Napoli's first. Kevin De Bruyne scored the second. Maignan stopped João Neves's third. Maximilian Beier converted the fourth and Mikey Moore delivered the decisive fifth.
Giménez shot over and Bondo hit the post for Milan, while Fofana and Roony scored. After Moore struck, Napoli had won the shootout 4–2 and Milan's fifth taker never needed to approach the spot.
The other semifinal supplied the opponents. Roma beat Inter 3–2. Further detail about the Roma scorers and sequence of goals has not been confirmed, but the result is enough: a Napoli–Roma final.

The latest January calendar identifies the Supercoppa game on January 1 with the designation NEUTRAL. It does not identify the actual stadium or a kickoff time. The trophy has not been awarded and no final lineup has been announced.
For both clubs, the symbolism is difficult to miss. Napoli and Roma occupied the first two positions in the last fully comparable Serie A table, after sixteen games each: Napoli 39 points, Roma 36.

Napoli have subsequently beaten Bologna and stand on 42 points after seventeen league matches. Roma's next Serie A result has not been independently confirmed. Their 3–2 win over Inter belongs to the Supercoppa semifinal, not the league.

The scheduling has another consequence. Parma arrive in Naples for Serie A on January 4, just three days after the final. Palermo follow on January 7. Fiorentina away January 10 and Lazio at home January 13 mean five Napoli fixtures in thirteen days from New Year's Day.

January also features two Champions League journeys, away at Real Sociedad and KS Cracovia, and a further match with Roma away in a domestic cup on January 31. The round of that latter fixture is not specified by the calendar.

The immediate prize, though, is clear. Napoli defeated Milan from the spot. Roma defeated Inter on the field. On the first day of 2029, one of them will lift the Supercoppa. Until then, the final remains a scheduled match, not a result.

articles.label: ARCHIVE · JANUARY CALENDAR BEFORE SUPERCOPPA RESULT
articles.imageCredit: Maximilian Beier in Napoli colours · archive portrait illustrating fixture congestion, not a January match photograph
articles.headline: TEN GAMES IN 31 DAYS. ROMA TWICE. JANUARY IS NOW EVEN MORE BRUTAL.
articles.dek: Original January schedule, as confirmed before the final. January 1 is now completed: Napoli 0–0 Roma, Roma win 4–3 on penalties. The other nine fixtures remain scheduled.
body: NAPLES — A schedule already regarded as demanding has become more intense. Napoli's updated January 2029 calendar now contains ten fixtures across three competitions' worth of commitments, including two different domestic cups, with Roma at either end of the month.

The first new appointment is the biggest: January 1, a Supercoppa Italiana final against Roma at a neutral venue. Roma qualified by beating Inter 3–2, while Napoli beat Milano FC 4–2 on penalties after a scoreless semifinal.
The final has no confirmed stadium or kickoff time. Its date is certain; its result is not. The match is the first of five scheduled games in the opening thirteen days.

Parma visit Naples on January 4 in Serie A, one day later than the January 3 date on an earlier calendar. Palermo now arrive January 7 rather than January 6. The league fixtures have shifted, not been played.
Fiorentina away on January 10 and Lazio at home on January 13 complete an opening sequence at three-day intervals: January 1, 4, 7, 10 and 13. Squad depth will be tested almost immediately.

Next come the European dates. Napoli visit Real Sociedad on January 16, then travel to KS Cracovia on January 24 for the final two listed Champions League league-phase matches. The last verified continental record is ten points after six matches.

Between those journeys, Napoli play Sampdoria away in Serie A on January 21. Juventus visit Naples on January 27, a fixture with obvious consequences given the clubs' position near the top of the league.

The new closing date is January 31, when Napoli are scheduled to travel to Roma in a domestic cup fixture. This is a separate cup match from the neutral Supercoppa final on New Year's Day. The January 31 cup round has not been specified.

The result is a confirmed count of ten games: six Serie A, two Champions League, one Supercoppa final, and one further domestic cup tie. All ten are future fixtures in the confirmed current match record.

The revised calendar leaves few opportunities for a sustained reset between matches. Napoli must consider recovery, rotations and the challenge of maintaining a strong league campaign while chasing honours in knockout competition.
One thing is settled: nobody needs to invent a more difficult January for Napoli. The dates, opponents and competitions on the updated calendar are demanding enough.

articles.label: SUPERCOPPA SEMIFINAL · NAPOLI 0–0 MILANO FC · 4–2 PENS
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive image · illustration, not an action photograph of Mikey Moore or the shootout
articles.headline: MOORE. FIVE STEPS. ONE FINAL. NAPOLI SURVIVE MILAN ON PENALTIES.
articles.dek: Maignan frustrates Napoli through a scoreless Supercoppa semifinal, but Giménez misses high, Bondo hits the post and Mikey Moore buries the fifth kick to seal a 4–2 shootout win. Roma await in the final.
body: NAPLES — There are matches decided by a great goal, and matches decided by the courage to strike one ball when the entire stadium is waiting. On 29 December 2028, Napoli reached the Supercoppa Italiana final after a scoreless semifinal against Milano FC, the in-game name for AC Milan, by winning the penalty shootout 4–2.

The semifinal had ended 0–0, but that scoreline concealed the opportunities created by Napoli and resisted by Mike Maignan. João Neves tested the Milan goalkeeper from distance. Alphonso Davies and Nico Paz then had dangerous chances in tight, both denied by the same imposing presence.
The Napoli attackers had reason to feel they should have been ahead. Maignan was the decisive obstacle during open play, and the competition moved to penalties without a goal on the board.
Pio Esposito took Napoli's first penalty and scored. Santiago Giménez answered for Milan by sending his effort over the crossbar. After one kick apiece, Napoli had their first advantage.
Kevin De Bruyne converted Napoli's second. Fofana kept Milan alive with a successful second kick. Napoli still led 2–1 after two rounds, but Maignan had not yet exhausted his influence.
João Neves, denied from distance during the match, had Napoli's third penalty saved. Roony then converted for Milano FC. Three rounds complete, the shootout was level at two apiece.

Maximilian Beier stepped up for Napoli's fourth and scored, extending a season already rich in crucial contributions. Then Bondo's effort struck the post. Milan had missed for the second time, and the responsibility shifted to Napoli's fifth taker.

Mikey Moore took the walk from the centre circle toward the penalty spot knowing precisely what a conversion meant. With Napoli ahead 3–2 and Milan still waiting for their fifth kick, a successful attempt would end the contest on the spot.
Moore scored. Napoli's fifth penalty made it 4–2, and Milano FC did not take a fifth. The youngster had delivered a place in the Supercoppa final.

The penalty sequence was exact: Napoli's scorers were Pio Esposito, De Bruyne, Beier and Moore; Neves had his attempt saved. Milan converted through Fofana and Roony; Giménez sent his over and Bondo hit the woodwork. The shootout goals do not count toward the players' regular season goalscoring records.

For Moore, the moment was enormous precisely because the preceding ninety minutes of attacking play had produced no breakthrough. There was no second opportunity and no loose rebound to follow. Just a run-up and a finish.

The other semifinal offered Napoli an immediate and compelling opponent: Roma defeated Inter 3–2 and will meet Napoli in the final. The date and venue for that decisive fixture have not yet been confirmed.

Napoli's league campaign has recently been marked by late goals, narrow margins and repeat tests of composure. This time, resilience took a different shape. They did not steal a goal in the 85th or the 90th minute. They held their nerve from the spot.

The trophy has not yet been won. This was the semifinal, and a final against Roma still lies ahead. But on the night Maignan seemed capable of stopping everything, the last word belonged to Mikey Moore.

articles.label: ARCHIVE · ROMA 3–2 INTER SEMIFINAL · FINAL NOW COMPLETED
articles.imageCredit: Alessandro Bastoni in Napoli colours · archive portrait illustrating Napoli's upcoming final; not a photo of Roma–Inter
articles.headline: ROMA BEAT INTER 3–2. THE SUPERCOPPA FINAL IS NAPOLI AGAINST ROMA.
articles.dek: After Roma beat Inter 3–2 in the semifinal, the final with Napoli was set. Roma later won the January 1 final 4–3 on penalties after 0–0.
body: ITALY — The Supercoppa Italiana has its finalists, and the meeting could hardly carry greater significance for this season's domestic rivalry. Roma defeated Inter 3–2 in the other semifinal. Napoli, after a 0–0 draw with Milano FC and a 4–2 victory on penalties, now face Roma in the final.

The Roma result was confirmed by the match information following the semifinals. The 3–2 score is known; the individual scorers, minute-by-minute sequence and venue have not been provided. None are necessary to understand its significance.

Napoli's route to the final was more nerve-racking. Maignan stopped a series of dangerous opportunities during play before penalties were required. Then Mikey Moore converted the decisive fifth kick after Giménez had missed high and Bondo had hit the post.
The final promises a confrontation between clubs already competing near the top of Serie A. After sixteen league matches apiece, Napoli led the table with 39 points and Roma were second with 36.

Napoli subsequently defeated Bologna 2–1 on December 24 to move to 42 points after seventeen matches. Roma's seventeenth league result is not yet part of the verified record. Their Supercoppa victory over Inter does not change their Serie A points tally, so no new current league gap can be responsibly asserted.

For Napoli, the reward is a chance to add a trophy to a season already featuring a compelling league campaign and European commitments. For Roma, victory over Inter establishes that they too have earned the right to compete for this title.

These are distinct competitions, and that distinction matters. The Scudetto race will continue whatever happens in the Supercoppa. But a one-match final can shape the mood around both clubs long after the whistle.

The match also offers fresh pressure for a Napoli attack that could not beat Maignan during play. Davies, Paz and Neves all had shots stopped, but the penalty takers made the decisive contribution. The challenge now is to convert chances before a game reaches that sort of jeopardy.

Roma's five-goal semifinal against Inter suggests a contest with attacking incident, but the details of those goals remain unknown. Tactical scouting should wait for evidence rather than filling the gaps with imagined descriptions.
The updated January calendar confirms the Napoli–Roma final for January 1, 2029 at a neutral venue. The stadium and kickoff time have not yet been announced.
Both clubs have earned their place. Now a single match awaits, and an Italian trophy is on the line.

articles.label: MAIGNAN · THE EVENING'S PARADOX
articles.imageCredit: Pio Esposito in Napoli colours · archive portrait of Napoli's first successful penalty taker, not of Milan goalkeeper Maignan
articles.headline: MAIGNAN STOPPED THE SHOTS. HE COULDN'T STOP THE STORY.
articles.dek: Neves from range, Davies and Paz from close quarters — Milan's goalkeeper kept Napoli at 0–0 and even saved in the shootout. Yet Moore's fifth penalty decided the semifinal in the other direction.
body: NAPLES — Goalkeepers sometimes shape matches they do not win. Mike Maignan's Supercoppa semifinal against Napoli was one of those occasions. Napoli had chances. Maignan had answers. And when the shootout ended, it was the side whose attacks he had repelled that was heading to the final.

During play, João Neves tested Maignan from distance. Alphonso Davies and Nico Paz followed with dangerous chances in tight. Each was denied. Those three interventions are the clearest confirmed examples of why Napoli could not turn their opportunities into a goal.
The match reached penalties at 0–0. No assumption should be made about additional shots, extra-time events or Milan's goalkeeper workload beyond those specifically reported.
In the shootout, Maignan's influence continued. Neves took Napoli's third and saw it saved. Milan's Roony converted next, bringing the series back to 2–2 after three rounds.

But shot-stopping cannot decide every penalty contest by itself. Giménez had already sent Milan's first attempt over the bar. Later, Bondo struck the post with the fourth. Those were two misses rather than saves by the Napoli goalkeeper.
Pio Esposito, Kevin De Bruyne and Maximilian Beier had already converted for Napoli before Mikey Moore approached the fifth kick. With the Partenopei ahead 3–2, Moore scored and ended the semifinal.

Maignan had stopped dangerous chances from open play and denied one penalty, yet his side exited 4–2 from the spot. It is a reminder that a knockout shootout measures the execution of both teams' takers as much as the performance of either goalkeeper.

For Napoli, the difference between frustration and celebration was composure. Their penalty takers responded to one saved effort, and Moore carried a pressure that no successful open-play chance could replicate.

For Neves, the missed penalty should not erase his attacking contribution. He had tested Maignan from distance before the shootout. One mistake should be reported accurately, but not made into a verdict on a midfielder's character.
Napoli reached the final. Maignan's display was part of the reason the route was so difficult. Both facts can be true.

articles.label: MIKEY MOORE · THE FIFTH KICK
articles.imageCredit: Napoli club archive illustration; not a photo of Mikey Moore taking the decisive spot kick
articles.headline: MIKEY MOORE HAD ONE KICK TO END IT. HE DIDN'T HESITATE.
articles.dek: With a final against Roma on the line, the young attacker converted Napoli's fifth penalty to end Milano FC's hopes without their taking a fifth. A high-pressure finish — and a moment Napoli will remember.
body: NAPLES — The walk to take a fifth penalty can feel longer than the entire match that came before it. Mikey Moore walked from the centre circle knowing a goal would send Napoli to the Supercoppa final. The preceding four rounds had arranged that extraordinary opportunity.
Napoli had scored through Pio Esposito and Kevin De Bruyne before João Neves had his third kick saved. Maximilian Beier responded with a fourth successful attempt, making it three scored from four.
Milan's sequence was less comfortable: Giménez over, Fofana scored, Roony scored, Bondo off the post. With four kicks taken by each side, Napoli led 3–2.

That meant Moore did not simply have a chance to regain an advantage or restore level terms. He had the first opportunity to conclude the semifinal outright. A successful fifth shot would give Napoli four conversions while Milan could reach only three, even if given their remaining kick.
Moore delivered. His penalty made the shootout 4–2 and the fifth Milano FC attempt was never taken. The competition moved from the foot of a young player to a Napoli–Roma final.

The goal was not a conventional strike for a season tally, nor a contribution requiring an official assist. Penalty shootouts are separate from regular goalscoring records. This was a decisive cup act on its own terms.

Young players often live with the assumption that experience is the prerequisite for responsibility. The final kick put Moore in the spotlight after established teammates had already scored, and he responded with the required finish.

The semifinal itself had not been easy. Napoli failed to beat Maignan in play despite opportunities for Neves, Davies and Paz. The fifth penalty required concentrating on one task after an entire match without a goal.

Napoli supporters have watched late winners from Beier and Davies in recent weeks. Moore's story differs: there was no moving ball to chase and no rebound to anticipate. There was simply the penalty spot and a chance to take a team to a final.
The destination is now Roma. The date of that final is still unconfirmed, but the way Napoli qualified is already written into the season's history.

articles.label: SERIE A · NAPOLI 2–1 BOLOGNA · FULL TIME
articles.imageCredit: Maximilian Beier in Napoli colours · archive portrait, not an image of the 85th-minute goal
articles.headline: 85 MINUTES. ONE LOOSE BALL. BEIER GIVES NAPLES A CHRISTMAS TO REMEMBER.
articles.dek: Davies scores an extraordinary 0.08-xG goal from Pio's pass. Openda silences the Maradona in the 80th. Five minutes later, Beier pounces on the rebound from a blocked João Neves effort for a dramatic 2–1 Napoli victory.
body: NAPLES, 24 DECEMBER 2028 — Christmas Eve at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona threatened to bring Napoli another frustrating draw. Then Maximilian Beier appeared exactly where a striker must be when a match is slipping away. Napoli 2–1 Bologna. Three points, a late winner and a season growing accustomed to astonishing conclusions.

The contest's first confirmed breakthrough arrived in the 58th minute. Pio Esposito supplied Alphonso Davies, who found a shooting angle that scarcely looked available and produced a remarkable finish. The goal's manager-reported in-game expected-goals value was just 0.08 — the sort of chance from which a goal is rare.

Davies had already delivered a dramatic 90th-minute winner against Como in the domestic cup on December 13, from a Nico Paz assist. Eleven days later, his confidence and finishing again gave Napoli an advantage they desperately needed.

Pio's delivery for the opener was his twelfth confirmed assist of the 2028–29 Napoli club campaign. The forward has thirteen goals as well, making his partnership in the decisive moments one of the most valuable features of Napoli's season.

Yet Napoli could not protect their lead. Openda equalised for Bologna in the 80th minute, leaving the home side facing another late collapse after the 2–2 disappointment at Palermo. The familiar sense of anxiety was real: the champions had led, and once again the opposition had found a way back.

With five minutes of regulation time remaining, João Neves drove forward to the edge of Bologna's area and shot. His effort was blocked. The ball remained alive, and Beier reached the rebound before the danger could be cleared.

Beier buried the chance in the 85th minute. The goal is officially treated as unassisted in the match record: Neves's blocked effort was the preceding action, not a credited final pass. It was a classic example of alert penalty-area instinct.

Beier now has nineteen confirmed goals and seven assists for Napoli across all club competitions this season. He had rescued an 86th-minute draw against Palermo a week earlier, and had scored twice in the 2–1 win away to Lazio earlier in December.

The winning goal will dominate the Christmas highlights, but the equaliser Napoli conceded is a reminder that celebration and scrutiny can coexist. Stefan Saladino's side have repeatedly had to fight back or find late winners in fixtures that might have been managed more comfortably.

Despite the tension, this victory moves Napoli to forty-two points from seventeen Serie A matches: thirteen wins, three draws and one defeat, with thirty-three scored, ten conceded and a goal difference of plus twenty-three.

Roma's last verified standing was thirty-six points after sixteen matches. Its subsequent result is not yet confirmed, so a current points gap between clubs that have not played the same number of games should not be presented as established.

The final whistle was the only thing left to settle. Davies delivered the improbable, Openda delivered the scare, and Beier delivered the answer. Christmas Eve in Naples belongs to the man who would not let the rebound escape.

articles.label: ALPHONSO DAVIES · THE 0.08 xG FINISH
articles.imageCredit: Alphonso Davies in Napoli colours · archive portrait; not a photograph of the Bologna finish
articles.headline: THE EIGHT-PERCENT SHOT: HOW DAVIES MADE THE IMPOSSIBLE LOOK ROUTINE.
articles.dek: A 0.08-xG chance from a near-impossible angle, converted in the 58th minute. The Napoli wide man's spectacular Bologna opener adds another remarkable chapter to his December.
body: NAPLES — Expected goals can tell a football story without ever pretending to explain every detail of a shot. For Alphonso Davies's 58th-minute opener against Bologna, the reported value was 0.08. In simple terms, shots evaluated at that number are expected to become goals around eight times in a hundred comparable attempts.

The number comes from the match's in-game shot metric reported by the manager. It is attached to this particular finish, not to Napoli's overall attacking performance and not to an independently verified match-wide dataset.
What the number conveys is difficulty. Davies received the assist from Pio Esposito and struck from a position where the angle appeared almost impossibly tight. The ball found the net anyway.

The shot is worth celebrating for more than the mathematics. Very low-xG attempts often fail, sometimes because the angle offers the goalkeeper an advantage and sometimes because the remaining target is simply too narrow. The exceptional finish is what separates the spectacular goal from the usual outcome.

Timing makes the story better. Davies scored in the 90th minute against Como on December 13 to win a cup match 2–1, supplied that night by substitute Nico Paz. The Bologna strike brought another December goal at a critical point in another close game.

It is dangerous to extrapolate a player's finishing talent from one shot or one fortnight. Expected goals quantify the difficulty of the opportunity, not a permanent ability to beat it. But a sequence of decisive finishes is legitimately an eye-catching story.

Pio's assist also matters. His contribution is the bridge between the attacking move and the improbable finish. At thirteen goals and twelve assists in all club competitions this season, the young striker is not only a finisher.

Napoli's evening became more complicated when Openda equalised in the 80th minute. Had that been the end, Davies's extraordinary finish would have sat inside another costly draw. Beier's 85th-minute rebound winner restored all three points and gave the earlier strike the result it deserved.

The record should distinguish between the two: Davies scored from Pio's assist; Beier scored unassisted after João Neves's shot was blocked. Different kinds of attacking quality, equally essential to this result.
Eight percent is a number. Watching a forward make the other ninety-two percent irrelevant is why people love football.

articles.label: BELLANDI · CHAMPIONSHIP STANDARDS
articles.imageCredit: Napoli archive image · illustrative editorial image, not a match photograph
articles.headline: BELLANDI: BEIER SAVED CHRISTMAS. BUT WHY DOES NAPOLI KEEP NEEDING SAVING?
articles.dek: A 2–1 victory over Bologna is a vital answer after Palermo. It is not an answer to the recurring problem of surrendering a lead — and the title race will eventually demand more than late heroics.
body: The scoreboard says Napoli beat Bologna 2–1 and climbed to forty-two points. The scoreboard is correct. It is also an incomplete diagnosis of a football team that seems determined to make the final fifteen minutes as dangerous as possible.

Alphonso Davies gave Napoli the lead in the 58th with a goal valued at just 0.08 expected goals. Pio Esposito provided the assist. That is the sort of moment a title-chasing team should be able to use as a foundation for control.

In the 80th minute, Bologna's Openda equalised. For the second consecutive Serie A outing, Napoli were left staring at points dropped after having put themselves in a position to take all three. Last week at Palermo, they came from behind twice to draw 2–2 against the last-place side.

Then came Beier. João Neves's shot from the edge of the area was blocked; Beier read the loose ball and scored unassisted in the 85th. Another wonderful moment of anticipation from a nineteen-goal forward. Another late rescue.

Some readers will object that victories are supposed to be celebrated rather than dissected. Of course they are. A winning goal in the 85th minute deserves its applause. But ambitious clubs cannot treat an avoidable crisis as proof that the underlying performance was excellent.

Napoli have shown enormous resilience. Beier scored twice to beat Lazio away. Davies won the Como cup match in the 90th. Beier saved a point at Palermo in the 86th. Now he has won the Bologna fixture in the 85th. The pattern is remarkable — and troubling.

Not all these games tell the same story. Lazio and Como involved opponents equalising earlier and Napoli eventually finding the winner, while Palermo saw Napoli fall behind twice. Bologna's specific problem was failing to protect a one-goal advantage in the final ten minutes. Lumping them together as identical tactical failures would be lazy.

The common thread is that Napoli are too frequently relying on a decisive late act. The talent is undeniable: Davies's invention, Pio's passing, Beier's finishing. What has been less convincing is the ability to dictate the end of a game without inviting jeopardy.

Nor should today's criticism turn automatically into an accusation against a particular defender or goalkeeper. The sequence leading to Openda's goal has not been documented in sufficient detail to attribute responsibility. It is enough to observe the trend and demand that the team examine it.

The league numbers are strong: thirteen wins, three draws, one defeat, thirty-three scored, ten allowed in seventeen matches. These are genuine championship figures. And Napoli's last comparable lead over Roma, with both on sixteen games, was three points. Roma's next result remains unknown.

Maybe late winners are simply the signature of this Napoli side. Maybe supporters will remember them as the defining moments of a title season. But ask any manager the harder question: how many more times should a striker have to rescue a team that was already ahead?
Beier saved Christmas. Stefan Saladino should celebrate his striker, then make sure the next match does not require another rescue.

articles.label: THE NINETEEN-GOAL MAN · MAXIMILIAN BEIER
articles.imageCredit: Maximilian Beier in Napoli colours · archive portrait, not action photography from the Bologna game
articles.headline: WHEN THE SHOT IS BLOCKED, BEIER IS ALREADY MOVING.
articles.dek: The 85th-minute rebound winner against Bologna takes Beier to nineteen goals for the season. More revealing than the tally is how often he seems to arrive at exactly the moment Napoli need him.
