There was, of course, one last thought. Saladino paused, smiled, and asked the only question that could make the story even more Neapolitan:
«Ma a volte penso… cosa sarebbe successo se avessimo perso?»

comments.text: «Sono fiero e torneremo.» Basta questo. Mister, siamo con te.
Love the manager but if Beier scores 25 goals and starts on the bench I will personally be conducting the next interview.
Lang e Chiesa ceduti, Neves dentro: non è vendetta. È una rivoluzione tattica.
He got a free dinner for beating Inter. Imagine what the restaurant does if we win the Champions League.
He really asked what happens if we lose. Mister, the bill arrives with interest.
Pio scores twice in a UCL final and Saladino tells them he's proud. That's my football club.
The interview happened before the Endrick sale. We went from wondering how to start three forwards to wondering how to replace one of them.
FREE DINNER? The club's wage structure is now in question. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: EXCLUSIVE · JOÃO NEVES
articles.headline: “WE HAVE ALREADY FOUGHT TWICE.” — JOÃO NEVES ON SALADINO, NAPOLI AND A VERY STRANGE SUMMER
articles.dek: First he scored against Napoli in the Champions League final. Then Saladino’s Italy knocked Portugal out of EURO 2028. Now the $250M midfielder is wearing blue.
body: João Neves has already experienced Stefan Saladino’s football from both sides. With Paris Saint-Germain, he scored the 38th-minute equalizer in the Champions League final as PSG beat Napoli 3–2 after extra time. Weeks later, with Portugal, he faced Saladino again in the EURO 2028 semifinal — and this time Italy won 2–1 after extra time.
Now Neves is a Napoli player. In his first extended interview since completing a $250 million move from PSG, the 23-year-old reflected on the strange path that brought him to Naples.
Q: You scored against Napoli in the Champions League final. Did you think, when you celebrated that goal, that a few months later you would be wearing their shirt?
NEVES: “No. [Laughs.] Definitely not. Football moves very quickly, but not even I would have imagined that.”
Q: What do you remember about Napoli that night?

NEVES: “That they would not disappear. We went ahead, they came back. We went ahead again. Even very late in the match, you never had the feeling that it was finished. When you play against a team like that, you remember it.”
Q: You scored PSG’s first equalizer that night. Have any of your new teammates mentioned it?
NEVES: “Yes. More than once. I think they will stop eventually. Maybe.”
Q: A few weeks later, you met Stefan Saladino again — this time with Portugal against his Italy in the EURO semifinal. Italy won 2–1 after extra time. What was that like?

NEVES: “Different match, same feeling. Very intense. Italy were extremely difficult to play against. They were organised, aggressive, but they also wanted the ball. When you play against a coach twice in such a short time, with two different teams, you start to understand certain ideas.”
Q: So you had beaten Saladino once, and then he beat you once. Who mentioned that first when you spoke about joining Napoli?
NEVES: “[Smiles.] I don’t think we need to keep score.”
Q: It is 1–1, though.
NEVES: “Then maybe we should keep it that way.”
Q: Napoli have paid $250 million for you. Does that number frighten you?
NEVES: “It is a very large number. Of course I know that. Pretending otherwise would be strange. But I cannot play for $250 million every time I touch the ball. I can only play football.”
Q: Does it create pressure?

NEVES: “There is pressure when you join a club that has just won Serie A without losing a match, won the Coppa Italia and reached the Champions League final. The expectations existed before I arrived. I want those expectations.”
Q: Napoli already have Scott McTominay and Nico Paz. Where do you see yourself fitting?

NEVES: “They are very different players, which is good. Scott gives the team things Nico does not give, Nico gives things I don’t give, and I can give something different again. The important thing isn’t three positions on a graphic. It is understanding where the space is.”
Q: You already have a Champions League winner’s medal. Napoli came within minutes of taking that trophy from you. Why Napoli?
NEVES: “Maybe because I know how close they are.”

comments.text: “Maybe because I know how close they are.” Yeah alright I am completely sold.
Paz, Neves e McTominay. Tre giocatori diversi, tre funzioni diverse. Questo centrocampo può fare paura.
The man scored against us in Manchester and now says he knows how close we are. Football is ridiculous.
I enjoyed this interview which obviously means something terrible is about to happen.
He says the score with Saladino is 1–1. I say the transfer negotiation grade is still F. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: BREAKING · NAPOLI
articles.headline: NAPOLI LAND JOÃO NEVES IN $250M BLOCKBUSTER.
articles.dek: The 23-year-old, 93-rated midfielder who scored against Napoli in the Champions League final is now a Napoli player. PSG receive $250M plus a 5% sell-on.
body: Napoli have completed the signing of João Neves from Paris Saint-Germain for $250 million plus a 5% sell-on clause.
Neves arrives at 23 years old and 93 overall, immediately becoming one of the defining pieces of Stefan Saladino’s next Napoli side.
The deal comes only months after Neves scored PSG’s 38th-minute equalizer against Napoli in the Champions League final at Old Trafford, a match PSG eventually won 3–2 after extra time.
Neves has agreed a Crucial squad role and a five-year contract worth $470,000 per week, with a $5 million signing bonus and a further $1.4 million after five appearances.
Napoli had pursued Jude Bellingham before ending talks with Real Madrid after Madrid demanded $350 million. Napoli instead moved for Neves and closed the deal at $250 million plus the sell-on clause.

The tactical picture is immediate: Nico Paz remains the creative centerpiece, while Neves brings elite ball-winning, pressure resistance and relentless midfield energy beside him. Scott McTominay remains another 88-rated option in what has become an extraordinary midfield group.

comments.text: Paz has the keys and now he has a 93-rated engine beside him. This is disgusting.
Ventitré anni. Novantatré di overall. Paz e Neves possono essere il centrocampo del futuro.
$250M plus 5% is enormous. So is signing a 23-year-old 93 OVR midfielder. This is what the war chest was for.
We bought one of the men who scored against us in the final. I have decided this is either healing or deeply unhealthy.
F grade from the negotiators. 93 overall from the footballer. Unfortunately I must remain consistent. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: THE REVERSAL
articles.headline: HE BROKE NAPOLI’S HEART IN MANCHESTER. NOW JOÃO NEVES WEARS BLUE.
articles.dek: Neves scored against Napoli on the biggest night in club history. Saladino’s response was not to avoid the memory — it was to sign the midfielder at the center of it.
body: The image is still fresh: Old Trafford, a Champions League final, Napoli leading through Pio Esposito and João Neves arriving with PSG’s equalizer in the 38th minute.
PSG eventually won 3–2 after extra time. Napoli returned home with a historic season and a wound that shaped the summer.
Now one of the players on the other side of that final has crossed over. Neves is a Napoli player.

This is not a rebuild. Napoli went unbeaten in Serie A, won the Coppa Italia and reached the first European Cup final in club history. The signing is an attempt to add an elite piece to a team already operating at championship level.
At 23, Neves also matches the timeline of Nico Paz and Pio Esposito. Napoli are not buying a short-term response to one painful night. They are trying to build the midfield of the next era.

comments.text: Pio up front. Paz creating. Neves hunting everything behind them. Run it back.
If you cannot erase Manchester, apparently you purchase part of PSG.
Questo Napoli non sta ricostruendo. Sta aggiungendo campioni a una squadra già fortissima.

articles.label: EURO 2028 · FINAL
articles.headline: HEARTBREAK AGAIN. GERMANY BEAT ITALY 3–2 AFTER EXTRA TIME.
articles.dek: Kean gave Italy the lead, Woltemade equalized, Germany struck twice in the second half of extra time and Sebastiano Esposito’s 117th-minute reply came too late.
body: For the second time in less than two months, Stefan Saladino has lost a European final 3–2 after extra time.
Moise Kean put Italy ahead in the 20th minute with an unassisted goal. Gianluigi Donnarumma made three confirmed saves before halftime as Germany pushed for a response.
Woltemade equalized in the 76th minute. No assist was reported on the goal.
The match reached 90 minutes at 1–1 and remained level through the first half of extra time, with Donnarumma and Germany goalkeeper Noah Atubolu both making saves.
Germany then scored twice in the second half of extra time. The scorers, minutes and assists on those two goals were not reported.
Sebastiano Esposito pulled one back in the 117th minute, but Italy could not find another. Germany won 3–2 after extra time and became European champions.
Italy leave as runners-up after winning six consecutive matches to reach the final.

comments.text: Fa malissimo. Ma questa squadra ci ha fatto credere di nuovo. Non dimenticatelo.
ANOTHER 3-2 EXTRA-TIME EUROPEAN FINAL LOSS. I am filing a complaint with the concept of time.
Gigio was massive. Three saves before halftime and more later. He gave them every chance.
Two European finals lost 3-2 after extra time in seven weeks. Suspiciously specific. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: AZZURRI · THE MORNING AFTER
articles.headline: NO TROPHY. BUT NAPOTALIA IS SHOWING SIGNS OF SOMETHING.
articles.dek: A national team that had missed three straight World Cups just came within extra time of becoming European champions. Napoli and Italy see progress — and unfinished work.
body: Germany have the trophy. Italy do not. Nobody inside the project is interested in pretending otherwise.

But the context matters. This is an Italian side emerging from three consecutive missed World Cups in this save. At EURO 2028 it won six straight matches, opened the tournament with five consecutive clean sheets and reached the final before losing 3–2 after extra time.

The foundations are becoming visible. Pio Esposito. Alessandro Buongiorno. Alessandro Bastoni. Riccardo Calafiori. Gianluigi Donnarumma. Around them are Barella, Tonali, Kayode, Kean, Retegui and Sebastiano Esposito.

Project Napotalia began with club and country increasingly sharing players, habits and expectations. It is no longer merely an idea. Napoli players produced decisive moments throughout Italy’s run, while the national-team environment has also highlighted players outside the club who fit the broader direction.
The Napoli board and the Italy hierarchy are thrilled with the results of the work so far. They also believe there is work left to do.
There is no victory lap. Germany are champions. Italy go back to work.

comments.text: Tre Mondiali mancati di fila. Ora una finale europea persa ai supplementari. Non è un trofeo, ma è una direzione.
Finalmente c’è una base. Donnarumma, Bastoni, Buongiorno, Calafiori, Pio. Adesso bisogna continuare.
I hate hope. Unfortunately this team has given me quite a lot of it.
Board thrilled. Italy thrilled. Me? Unmoved. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: PLAYER FEATURE
articles.headline: THIS IS NOT THE END OF PIO’S EURO STORY. IT IS THE START OF HIS ARC.
articles.dek: Four EURO goals after a 29-goal Napoli season. Two brutal European-final defeats. The evidence is no longer about potential: big moments do not scare Pio Esposito.
body: Pio Esposito leaves EURO 2028 without the medal he wanted and with more evidence that the biggest occasions do not shrink him.
He scored four times at the tournament: against Bosnia, Norway, Turkey and Poland. He finished as Italy’s leading scorer.

That followed a Napoli season of 29 goals and 12 assists. His year included the winner against Atlético after 134 scoreless minutes in the tie, the 90+2 equalizer at Torino that preserved Napoli’s unbeaten Serie A season, and two goals in the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain.
Napoli lost that final 3–2 after extra time. Italy have now lost the EURO final by the same score after extra time.

That pain becomes part of the story now. Pio has already demonstrated that pressure does not make him disappear. The next question is what a player with that record does after experiencing this level of heartbreak twice.
Napoli do not need to wonder whether Pio can become a central figure. He already is one. The next phase is about how much bigger he can become.

comments.text: 29 club goals. Four EURO goals. Big-game receipts everywhere. This is chapter one.
Zero goals in the final. I will be ignoring every piece of context listed above.
He is coming back to Napoli angry. I would like to apologize in advance to Serie A.
Pio deve ricordare questo dolore. E poi tornare più forte.

articles.label: MERCATO · WINDOW OPEN
articles.headline: BACK TO NAPLES. THE WINDOW IS OPEN — LANG AND GILMOUR ARE OUT.
articles.dek: The international run is over. Napoli turn immediately toward 2028–29 with major decisions ahead and two confirmed departures already on the books.
body: The EURO run is over. Napoli business resumes immediately.
The transfer window is open, and Napoli’s recruitment department is assessing the next moves after an extraordinary season.
Noa Lang has completed his $47 million move to Bournemouth. Billy Gilmour is also out, having already been sold.
Federico Chiesa remains a Napoli player after Bournemouth’s $36.7 million offer was rejected. Real Madrid’s $158.6 million approach for Alessandro Bastoni was also rejected.
The message from the Napoli board mirrors the mood around the Italy project: satisfaction with how far the team has come, but no sense that the work is finished.

Napoli return from an unbeaten Serie A title, a Coppa Italia triumph and a first Champions League final. The squad does not require a rebuild. The summer is about deciding which roles can turn last season’s near-miss in Europe into the next step, rather than making signings simply because the club has the financial power to do so.

comments.text: Lang out. Gilmour out. Do not buy a name simply because we can. Buy the missing piece.
This is the fun kind of window. Champion squad, huge budget, targeted surgery.
And Chiesa is STILL HERE after that Bournemouth bid. I am watching every notification.
Financial ambition is no excuse for failing to sign eleven Ballon d’Or winners. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: EURO 2028 FINAL · JULY 16
articles.headline: HELLO, BEIER. NAPOLI’S STRIKE PARTNERS MEET WITH EUROPE ON THE LINE.
articles.dek: Pio Esposito and Maximilian Beier combined for 77 goal contributions at Napoli last season. On July 16, they will stand on opposite sides of the EURO 2028 final.
body: There are easier ways for a manager to prepare for a European Championship final than designing a plan to stop one of his own best forwards.

Italy will face Germany on July 16 with the EURO 2028 trophy at stake. That puts Stefan Saladino across from Maximilian Beier — the Napoli striker who produced 25 goals and 11 assists during the 2027–28 season.

At the other end is Beier’s club strike partner, Pio Esposito. Pio finished Napoli’s season with 29 goals and 12 assists. Together, the pair produced 77 goal contributions while driving Napoli to an unbeaten Serie A title, the Coppa Italia and the club’s first Champions League final.
Now the partnership splits in two.

Pio enters the final with four goals at EURO 2028. Italy have won all six matches, scoring nine and conceding once. Beier, meanwhile, represents a uniquely familiar threat: Saladino and several members of the Italian side know exactly what he can do because they have spent a season benefiting from it.
That familiarity cuts both ways. Beier knows Saladino’s ideas. He knows his Napoli teammates. Italy know Beier’s movement and finishing.
For one night, none of that club chemistry matters. Pio and Beier will walk into the same final wearing different shirts. One of them can leave as champion of Europe.

comments.text: Pio vs Maxi in a EURO FINAL. The Napoli group chat is going to be unusable for months.
I have defended this man all season and now I need him to have the worst 90 minutes of his life. Horrible.
Maxi, ti vogliamo bene. Dal 17 luglio.
Saladino conosce Beier. Beier conosce Saladino. In una finale, questa familiarità vale per entrambi.
Of course the final contains our own 25-goal striker. Of course it does.
Built Beier into a 25-goal striker and now has to stop him in a final. Self-inflicted tactical negligence. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: EURO 2028 · SEMIFINAL
articles.headline: BARELLA TWICE. ITALY ARE IN THE EURO FINAL.
articles.dek: Italy trailed for the first time all tournament. Nicolò Barella answered twice — first from Buongiorno, then in extra time — to beat Portugal 2–1 and send the Azzurri to the final.
body: Italy are in the EURO 2028 final.
Portugal struck first through Fábio Silva in the fourth minute, ending Italy’s extraordinary run without conceding and putting Stefan Saladino’s side behind for the first time at this tournament.
The response took twelve minutes. Alessandro Buongiorno supplied Nicolò Barella, who made it 1–1 in the 16th minute.
The semifinal went to extra time. In the 103rd minute, Barella struck again. No assist was reported on the winner.
Italy held on for a 2–1 victory after extra time. Six matches. Six wins. Nine goals scored. One conceded.
For a team whose tournament began with Pio Esposito scoring, whose quarterfinal was won by Retegui from Kean, the semifinal belonged completely to Barella.
One match remains.

comments.text: SIAMO IN FINALE. BARELLA DUE VOLTE. NON CI CREDO. AVANTI ITALIA.
Prima volta sotto nel torneo. Nessun panico. Pareggio dopo dodici minuti e vittoria ai supplementari. Questa è una squadra vera.
We conceded ONE goal and I briefly forgot how to function. Anyway WE ARE IN THE FINAL.
Pio carried the scoring early. Retegui got England. Barella got Portugal. This is exactly how tournament teams become champions.
Six wins from six and a final. Clearly he has peaked. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: AZZURRI HERO
articles.headline: THE SEMIFINAL BELONGED TO BARELLA.
articles.dek: Down 1–0 after four minutes, Italy needed an answer. Barella gave them two.
body: Nicolò Barella had already scored at EURO 2028 before the semifinal. Against Portugal, he produced the defining performance of Italy’s tournament so far.
Fábio Silva’s fourth-minute opener created a situation Italy had not experienced in five previous matches: they were losing.
Barella erased it in the 16th minute after Buongiorno created the goal. Then, with the match in extra time, Barella scored the winner in the 103rd.
His tournament total rises to three goals.

There was a small decision back in the opening match against Bosnia that now feels illustrative. With Italy already leading through Pio Esposito, Barella took the second penalty. Saladino’s reasoning was simple: give everyone a chance and keep multiple players in form.
Twenty-five days later, Barella scored twice to put Italy in the European Championship final.

comments.text: BARELLA. PARTITA DA LEADER.
Remember the Bosnia penalty? Multiple guys in form. Here is the payoff.
Pio zero semifinal goals. Barella two. I have prepared a 47-page document.

articles.label: TACTICAL NOTE
articles.headline: THE WALL FINALLY BROKE. ITALY DIDN’T.
articles.dek: After five clean sheets, Fábio Silva ended Italy’s shutout streak in the fourth minute. The Azzurri responded with their first comeback of the tournament.
body: For five matches, Italy never had to answer this question.
Fábio Silva scored four minutes into the semifinal. The run of five consecutive clean sheets was over, and Italy were behind for the first time at EURO 2028.
What followed may matter more than the streak itself. Barella equalized twelve minutes later and Italy remained composed long enough to win in extra time.
The defensive record is no longer perfect: Italy have now scored nine and conceded one across six victories.
The tournament record, however, remains perfect.

comments.text: Sorry Gigio. The clean-sheet streak was absurd. The response was better.
La porta inviolata finisce. La maturità della squadra no.

articles.label: OFFICIAL · TRANSFER
articles.headline: OFFICIAL: NOA LANG LEAVES NAPOLI FOR BOURNEMOUTH IN $47M DEAL.
articles.dek: Bournemouth opened at $41.4 million. Napoli held out, reached agreement at $47 million, and the transfer is now complete.
body: Noa Lang is officially a Bournemouth player.
Bournemouth initially approached Napoli with a $41.4 million offer. Negotiations continued and the clubs ultimately agreed a $47 million fee.
Lang leaves after contributing one assist during Napoli’s 2027–28 campaign.
The deal is the first confirmed major outgoing of Napoli’s new summer window. The club is entering 2028–29 with major ambitions, but its precise spending allocation remains an internal matter.

Napoli have not treated every offer the same way. Real Madrid’s $158.6 million approach for Alessandro Bastoni was rejected, while Bournemouth’s separate pursuit of Federico Chiesa has also failed to produce an agreement after Napoli turned down $36.7 million.
Lang, however, is gone. Napoli have converted a depth attacker into a $47 million sale while preserving the core of the squad.

comments.text: $47M for a depth piece is strong business. Now replace the role, not the name.
They opened at $41.4M and paid $47M. Thank you for your contribution, Bournemouth.
Lang gone and the Chiesa offer rejected. The winger board is officially interesting.
Sold a player for more than the opening bid. Financial competence is dangerous. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: EURO 2028 · QUARTERFINAL
articles.headline: ENGLAND OUT. ITALY ARE IN THE SEMIFINALS.
articles.dek: Retegui finished Kean’s pass in the 75th minute and Donnarumma did the rest. Italy beat England 1–0 and still have not conceded at EURO 2028.
body: Italy are two wins from the trophy.
Mateo Retegui scored from Moise Kean’s assist in the 75th minute and Italy defeated England 1–0 to reach the EURO 2028 semifinals.
For the first time at this tournament, Pio Esposito did not score. Italy won anyway. That may be the most important development of the night.

Stefan Saladino said during the group stage that he wanted multiple players in form. Against England, with Pio’s four-match scoring streak finally ending, Kean created the chance and Retegui finished it.
At the other end, Gianluigi Donnarumma delivered again. England could not become the first side to score against Italy at this tournament.
Five matches. Five wins. Seven goals scored. Zero conceded. Italy are in the semifinals.

comments.text: INGHILTERRA FUORI. SEMIFINALE. CINQUE PARTITE E ZERO GOL SUBITI. AVANTI.
Pio non segna? Kean serve Retegui. Questo è esattamente perché serve tutta la rosa.
Pio did not score and apparently Italy are still allowed to win. Huge development.
Donnarumma doing Donnarumma things. Again.
SEMIFINALS. ZERO CONCEDED. I refuse to experience hope responsibly.

articles.label: AZZURRI FEATURE
articles.headline: 450 MINUTES. ZERO CONCEDED. DONNARUMMA’S EURO IS BECOMING ABSURD.
articles.dek: Bosnia, Norway, Turkey, Poland and now England: five opponents have tried. None have scored.
body: Five matches into EURO 2028, Italy’s goals-against column still reads zero.

England became the latest side to run into an Italian defence that has refused to break, with Donnarumma again producing the kind of goalkeeping that turns a one-goal lead into a place in the next round.
The streak now stands at 450 tournament minutes without conceding. Turkey even had a penalty during the group stage and Donnarumma saved it.
The numbers are becoming difficult to ignore: five matches, five clean sheets, seven goals scored and a place in the semifinals.
Knockout football rarely offers comfort. Italy have instead built the tournament’s most valuable kind of margin: score once, and so far it has been enough.

comments.text: I remain Meret Union forever. But Gigio has been absolutely ridiculous.
CINQUE PORTE INVIOLATE. Donnarumma enorme.
In un torneo così, il portiere può portarti fino alla fine. Gigio lo sta facendo.

articles.label: TACTICAL NOTE
articles.headline: PIO FINALLY GOES QUIET. RETEGUI AND KEAN ANSWER.
articles.dek: Italy’s leading scorer did not find the net against England. Saladino’s insistence on keeping the squad involved paid off anyway.
body: Pio Esposito entered the quarterfinal having scored in all four of Italy’s EURO matches. England finally stopped the streak.
They did not stop Italy.
In the 75th minute, Moise Kean supplied Mateo Retegui and the finish sent the Azzurri into the semifinals.

It was a clean illustration of Saladino’s group-stage philosophy: tournament squads cannot depend on one player remaining hot forever. Pio’s four goals remain central to Italy’s run, but against England the decisive combination came from elsewhere.
That matters now. Italy are in the final four with more than one route to a goal — and with a goalkeeper and defence that have yet to require a second one.

comments.text: THIS is why you keep everybody involved. Quarterfinal goal comes from Kean to Retegui.
Zero goals against England. Bench him immediately. I have been waiting weeks for this.
Four goals got us here. Retegui gets us through tonight. That is a team.

articles.label: MERCATO · THE TIMING
articles.headline: BELLINGHAM GOES HOME. NAPOLI’S SUMMER QUESTION IS STILL WAITING.
articles.dek: The midfielder linked with Napoli has just been eliminated by Stefan Saladino’s Italy. Napoli’s growing ambitions make the summer question impossible to ignore — but there is still no bid or agreement.
body: The timing could hardly be cleaner.

Napoli enter the summer with formidable ambition and an appetite for elite additions. Jude Bellingham remains part of the speculation around what kind of midfield signing could push the Champions League runners-up forward.
Now Bellingham’s England have been eliminated from EURO 2028 by the same manager who would be coaching him in Naples: Stefan Saladino.
None of that constitutes a transfer. Napoli have made no confirmed bid, there is no agreement, and there is no confirmed indication that Real Madrid intend to sell.

But after Madrid’s $158.6 million approach for Alessandro Bastoni and Italy’s quarterfinal victory over England, the Madrid-Naples storyline has acquired another layer. The Euros continue first. The mercato will still be there when Saladino gets home.

comments.text: Paz plus Bellingham discourse is going to consume my entire summer, isn’t it.
Having financial power does not legally require spending all of it.
He eliminated Bellingham before signing Bellingham. Reckless asset management. SALADINO OUT.

articles.label: EURO 2028 · ROUND OF 16
articles.headline: PIO. AGAIN. ITALY ARE IN THE QUARTERFINALS.
articles.dek: Pio Esposito struck unassisted in the 30th minute and Italy made it stand: 1–0 over Poland, four wins from four, and still no goals conceded.
body: Knockout football changed the stakes. It did not change the scorer.
Pio Esposito scored an unassisted goal in the 30th minute and Italy defeated Poland 1–0 on June 29 to advance to the EURO 2028 quarterfinals.
Italy entered the Round of 16 without Michael Kayode, suspended following a red card. They leave it with the same defensive record they carried out of the group: untouched.
Four matches have now produced four wins, six goals and zero conceded. Pio has scored in every one of them.
The perfect group stage bought Italy passage into the knockouts. Nothing was guaranteed after that. One Pio goal and another clean sheet have bought them one more match.

comments.text: QUARTI. QUATTRO PARTITE. ZERO GOL SUBITI. AVANTI ITALIA.
FOUR MATCHES. FOUR GOALS. HE DOES NOT CARE WHAT ROUND IT IS.
Senza Kayode, partita da eliminazione diretta, 1–0 e porta chiusa. Squadra matura.
We are in the quarters and have conceded zero goals. Naturally I am completely calm. This is a lie.
Unassisted? Selfish. Pio agenda remains alive.

articles.label: PLAYER WATCH · PIO ESPOSITO
articles.headline: FOUR MATCHES. FOUR GOALS. PIO’S STREAK SURVIVES THE KNOCKOUTS.
articles.dek: Bosnia. Norway. Turkey. Poland. Pio Esposito has scored in every Italy match at EURO 2028.
body: At some point a scoring streak stops looking like form and starts defining a tournament.

Pio scored against Bosnia. He scored the winner against Norway. He converted against Turkey. Against Poland, with Italy’s tournament now one mistake from ending, he scored again — unassisted in the 30th minute.
That makes four goals in four EURO matches, with at least one in every match Italy have played.
His run also follows directly from a two-goal performance for Napoli in the Champions League final. Club season into international tournament, the goals have simply continued.
Italy are in the quarterfinals. Their number nine arrives there having answered every match so far.

comments.text: Bosnia. Norway. Turkey. Poland. Cross them off one by one.
Non è più una sorpresa. È Pio.
Somebody please preserve this man in bubble wrap between matches.

articles.label: AZZURRI FEATURE
articles.headline: 360 MINUTES. ZERO CONCEDED. ITALY’S WALL REACHES THE QUARTERFINALS.
articles.dek: The group-stage clean-sheet streak survived its first knockout test as Italy shut out Poland 1–0.
body: Bosnia could not score. Norway could not score. Turkey could not score, even from the penalty spot. Poland could not score with Italy’s tournament on the line.
Italy have now played 360 minutes at EURO 2028 without conceding a goal.
The fourth clean sheet came with Michael Kayode unavailable through suspension, adding another test of the depth behind Saladino’s defensive structure.
Donnarumma’s penalty save against Turkey remains the most dramatic single moment of the run, but the larger story is repetition: four matches, four shutouts.
Italy enter the quarterfinals with a perfect record and a defence no opponent at this tournament has yet solved.

comments.text: 360 MINUTI. ZERO. Questa difesa è seria.
Four straight clean sheets. Gigio and this back line are cooking.
Le partite a eliminazione diretta si vincono anche così. Un gol. Nessun regalo.

articles.label: EURO 2028 · MATCH REPORT
articles.headline: PERFECT NINE. ITALY FINISH THE GROUP WITHOUT CONCEDING A GOAL.
articles.dek: Buongiorno headed home Barella’s corner, Donnarumma saved a Turkey penalty and Pio Esposito made it 2–0 from the spot as Italy completed a 3–0–0 group stage.
body: Three matches. Three wins. Five goals scored. Zero conceded. Italy have completed a perfect EURO 2028 group stage.

Alessandro Buongiorno opened the scoring by heading home Nicolò Barella’s corner. Turkey were then handed their clearest route back into the match from the penalty spot in the 53rd minute, but Gianluigi Donnarumma saved it and preserved Italy’s clean sheet.
Pio Esposito finished the job from the penalty spot in the 75th minute. It was his third goal in three EURO matches, meaning the Napoli striker scored in every game of the group stage.

The balance is what will please Stefan Saladino most. Pio has three goals, Barella has contributed both a goal and an assist, Tonali supplied the winner against Norway, Buongiorno has now scored, and Donnarumma has produced decisive saves behind a defence that has not conceded.
Italy leave the group with nine points and a 5–0 aggregate scoreline. The margin for error gets smaller from here. The evidence, however, is no longer subtle: the Azzurri have arrived.

comments.text: NOVE PUNTI. CINQUE FATTI. ZERO SUBITI. Adesso comincia il torneo vero.
THREE MATCHES. THREE PIO GOALS. OUR GUY.
Barella mette il corner. BUONGIORNO SALE. Fine della discussione.
La cosa migliore? Non dipendiamo da un solo giocatore. Questa è una squadra.
9 points and 0 conceded. I have decided this makes me MORE nervous.

articles.label: AZZURRI FEATURE
articles.headline: 270 MINUTES. ZERO CONCEDED. AND THEN DONNARUMMA SAVED THE PENALTY.
articles.dek: Italy’s perfect group stage was built on a defence that never broke — even when Turkey were given a penalty in the 53rd minute.
body: There are clean sheets, and then there are clean sheets that survive the moment they are supposed to end.
Turkey had a penalty in the 53rd minute and the chance to erase Italy’s perfect defensive record. Gianluigi Donnarumma saved it.

It was the defining image of a group stage in which Italy allowed no goals across 270 minutes. Bosnia were shut out. Erling Haaland and Norway were shut out. Turkey were shut out even from twelve yards.

Saladino knows the value of a goalkeeper who can change a knockout tie after watching Alex Meret repeatedly rescue Napoli during the Champions League run. Donnarumma is now providing that same sense of security for Italy on the international stage.
The knockout rounds will ask harder questions. Italy enter them knowing that when the structure bends, their goalkeeper has already shown he can keep it from breaking.

comments.text: Meret is family. But Gigio is an absolute monster.
Rigore contro. Donnarumma dice no. Questa è presenza.
Nei tornei serve un portiere che ti salva una partita. Eccolo.

articles.label: PLAYER WATCH · PIO ESPOSITO
articles.headline: THREE MATCHES. THREE GOALS. PIO HAS FOLLOWED NAPOLI STRAIGHT INTO THE EUROS.
articles.dek: Bosnia, Norway, Turkey: Pio Esposito scored against all three after ending his club season with two goals in the Champions League final.
body: The shirt changed. The habit did not.
Pio Esposito scored against Bosnia, scored the winner against Norway and converted from the spot against Turkey. Three EURO 2028 group matches produced three goals.
The sequence extends an extraordinary end to his club season. Pio scored twice for Napoli in the Champions League final before reporting to Italy and immediately finding the net again.

What matters for Italy is that his production has not isolated the rest of the attack. Barella, Tonali and Buongiorno have all contributed directly during the group, exactly the kind of shared form Saladino wanted to create.

Pio enters the knockout stage as Italy’s leading scorer and the most obvious continuation of the club-country connection at the heart of Project Napotalia. The next test is whether that form survives when one bad night can end the tournament.

comments.text: UCL final brace then three goals in three EURO games. This is getting ridiculous.
Only three goals in three matches? Standards have collapsed.
Non dite la parola capocannoniere. Non portate sfortuna.

articles.label: TACTICAL NOTE
articles.headline: THIS WAS THE PLAN: PIO HOT, EVERYONE INVOLVED.
articles.dek: Saladino wanted multiple players in form. Italy leave the group with goals or assists from Pio, Barella, Tonali and Buongiorno — plus three clean sheets behind them.
body: After the Bosnia opener, Saladino’s message was simple: give everyone a chance and get multiple players into form.

The group stage delivered exactly that. Pio scored three times. Barella scored against Bosnia and assisted Buongiorno from a corner against Turkey. Tonali created the winner against Norway. Buongiorno added a goal. Donnarumma supplied the defining save of the third match.

That distribution matters in tournament football. A team built around one hot player can disappear when that player has one quiet night. Italy are entering the knockout rounds with several players who have already made a meaningful contribution.
Pio remains the headline act. The important part is that he is no longer the only story.

comments.text: This is why you build a tournament squad instead of eleven starters and twelve spectators.
Pio segna. Barella produce. Tonali produce. Buongiorno segna. Donnarumma para. Perfetto.

articles.label: EURO 2028 · MATCH REPORT
articles.headline: HAALAND STYMIED. PIO STRIKES. ITALY STILL HAVEN’T CONCEDED.
articles.dek: Tonali’s free kick found Pio Esposito on 45 minutes and Italy made the goal stand, beating Norway 1–0 for a second straight win and clean sheet.
body: Italy have played twice at EURO 2028. They have won twice. They have conceded zero.
The decisive moment against Norway arrived on 45 minutes. Sandro Tonali whipped in a free kick and Pio Esposito finished it, sending Italy into halftime 1–0 ahead.

That was enough. Norway had Erling Haaland, but not a goal. Italy’s defensive work and Gianluigi Donnarumma kept one of world football’s most dangerous strikers off the scoresheet and preserved a second consecutive clean sheet.

Pio, meanwhile, has now scored in both matches of the tournament: a penalty against Bosnia and a finish from Tonali’s delivery against Norway. The Napoli striker’s extraordinary run has followed him straight into the national team.
The larger picture is exactly what Saladino wanted. Pio is producing, Barella has already scored, Tonali now has an assist, Donnarumma is making saves and Italy’s defensive unit has yet to crack.
Six points. Three goals scored. None conceded. Italy’s EURO campaign is beginning to acquire an identity.

comments.text: HAALAND A ZERO. DUE PARTITE, DUE VITTORIE, ZERO GOL SUBITI. AVANTI.
Two EURO matches. Two Pio goals. I have no further questions.
Tonali sulla punizione, Pio ad attaccare l’area. Gol da squadra vera.
I love Meret with my entire heart but Donnarumma is doing Donnarumma things.
Haaland did not score and somehow I was still terrified until the whistle.

articles.label: AZZURRI ANALYSIS
articles.headline: 180 MINUTES. ZERO CONCEDED. ITALY’S WALL IS BECOMING THE STORY.
articles.dek: Bosnia could not score. Neither could Haaland and Norway. Donnarumma and the Italian defensive unit have opened EURO 2028 with back-to-back shutouts.
body: Tournament football rarely gives medals for aesthetics. It rewards teams that survive difficult minutes without losing control of the scoreline.
Italy have now done that for 180 minutes. Bosnia were beaten 2–0. Norway, with Erling Haaland leading the threat, were beaten 1–0. Neither opponent scored.

Gianluigi Donnarumma made several important saves against Norway and reminded everyone what his presence can mean in a short tournament. When Italy’s structure is breached, there is still an enormous final obstacle behind it.

For Saladino, whose Napoli side leaned heavily on Alex Meret during its run to the Champions League final, elite goalkeeping is familiar currency. With Italy, Donnarumma is providing another version of the same security.
The sample is only two matches. The warning signs will come eventually. But six points without conceding is not a theory. It is the foundation Italy have already built.

comments.text: Le grandi squadre nei tornei imparano prima a non perdere. Questa Italia sembra capirlo.
Donnarumma behind an Italian defence in tournament football. Good luck.
Zero subiti significa solo che il primo farà ancora più male. Sì, ho un problema.

articles.label: EURO 2028 · MATCH REPORT
articles.headline: NO HANGOVER. ITALY OPEN THE EUROS WITH A CLEAN 2–0.
articles.dek: Pio Esposito scored from the spot in the 19th minute, Nicolò Barella took the second penalty in the 75th, and Italy opened EURO 2028 with three points and a clean sheet.
body: Italy's tournament began without drama: two goals, a clean sheet and three points.

Pio Esposito opened the scoring from the penalty spot in the 19th minute, carrying his extraordinary club-season scoring form directly into EURO 2028. Nicolò Barella then converted another penalty in the 75th to make it 2–0.

The identity of the second taker was notable. Saladino has made clear that a tournament cannot be built around keeping one player hot. Italy need confidence and responsibility spread across the squad. Pio took the first; Barella took the second.
Bosnia never found a goal back. Italy leave the opener 1–0–0 with two goals scored, none conceded and an immediate platform for the group.
There is little recovery time. Norway await on June 20.

comments.text: Tre punti, porta inviolata, nessun dramma. Iniziare così va benissimo.
Finale Champions: due gol. Prima partita agli Europei: gol. OUR GUY NON SI FERMA.
Bene anche Barella sul secondo rigore. In un torneo servono tanti giocatori dentro mentalmente.
I have transferred my anxiety from Napoli to Italy with zero recovery days.

articles.label: TOURNAMENT NOTE
articles.headline: PIO SCORES. BARELLA TAKES THE NEXT ONE. THAT IS NOT AN ACCIDENT.
articles.dek: Italy’s opening win offered a small glimpse of Saladino’s tournament philosophy: build form across the squad, not around one protagonist.
body: Pio Esposito had already scored once from the spot when Italy were awarded another penalty against Bosnia. The second did not go to Pio. Nicolò Barella took it and scored.
The logic is broader than penalties. Saladino wants multiple players in form during the tournament. Italy cannot ask one forward to carry every decisive action across an entire European Championship.

That philosophy should shape the coming matches: opportunities distributed where possible, responsibility shared and a squad kept emotionally involved rather than a fixed group asked to carry every minute.
The first return was ideal. Pio has his tournament goal. Barella has his. Italy have their first win.

comments.text: Tournament football. Use the squad before you NEED the squad.
Golden Boot agenda paused for squad harmony. I will allow it.
Pio caldo, Barella coinvolto, vittoria. Perfetto.

articles.label: NEXT · JUNE 20
articles.headline: NORWAY NEXT. ITALY HAVE THEIR START — NOW BUILD ON IT.
articles.dek: The Azzurri move from a 2–0 opening win over Bosnia to their second EURO 2028 group match against Norway on June 20.
body: Three points are on the board. The tournament immediately moves on.
Italy face Norway on June 20 in their second EURO 2028 group match after opening with a 2–0 victory over Bosnia.
The Bosnia match established the baseline: Pio Esposito and Nicolò Barella on the scoresheet, a clean sheet behind them and no need for a frantic finish.

Now comes the next selection decision. Saladino wants multiple players in rhythm during the tournament, and the short turnaround gives him an early opportunity to manage minutes without surrendering momentum.
No assumptions are being made about Norway's XI or Italy's selection before the teams are known. The only certainty is the date and the stakes: June 20, match two.

comments.text: Tre punti presi. Adesso niente calcoli strani: battere la Norvegia e prendere il controllo del gruppo.
Good start. Reset. Norway.
Quattro giorni tra le partite. Fantastico. Non avevo bisogno di dormire comunque.

articles.label: CHAMPIONS LEAGUE FINAL
articles.headline: SO CLOSE. PSG BREAK NAPOLI HEARTS IN EXTRA TIME.
articles.dek: Pio Esposito scored twice and dragged Napoli level in the 90th minute, but former Napoli star Kvaratskhelia struck again in the 110th to give PSG a 3–2 extra-time victory at Old Trafford.
body: Napoli's greatest European run ended ten minutes from penalties.

Pio Esposito put Napoli ahead from the penalty spot in the 17th minute after being taken down clean through. João Neves equalised in the 38th, and Kvaratskhelia — the former Napoli star at the centre of the final's cruelest subplot — put PSG ahead in the 54th.

At 90 minutes, with Napoli seconds from defeat, Alessandro Buongiorno released Pio in alone. Pio finished. 2–2. His second goal of the final, his 29th of the season, and another rescue at the edge of elimination.
Meret caught PSG's final header of regulation and the match went to extra time. Both sides traded chances. PSG hit the post before the extra-time interval. Napoli survived it, but not the next blow.
In the 110th minute Kvaratskhelia scored his second of the night. Napoli could not find another equaliser. Paris Saint-Germain won 3–2 after extra time.

There is no treble and no first European Cup. The season instead closes with the Scudetto, the Coppa Italia, a 28–10–0 unbeaten league campaign and the first Champions League final in Napoli history after a knockout route through Inter, Real Madrid, Atlético Madrid and Barcelona.
The loss hurts precisely because Napoli were close enough to touch the ending they wanted. It does not erase what they built.

comments.text: Due gol in una finale di Champions. Il secondo al 90°. Pio ci ha portati fino all’ultimo respiro.
Doveva essere proprio lui. Due volte. Fa malissimo.
Meret kept us alive all through Europe. Ten minutes from penalties. I am sick.
Il palo in supplementari mi aveva convinto che il destino fosse con noi. Non sto bene.
Due trofei, imbattuti in campionato, finale Champions persa. Il finale conta. Saladino OUT.

replies.text: You made it through an undefeated Scudetto and a Champions League final without breaking character. Respect the commitment.

articles.label: Our Guy
articles.headline: PIO SCORED TWICE IN THE FINAL. SOME NIGHTS HURT AND STILL MAKE LEGENDS.
articles.dek: Goal 28 from the spot. Goal 29 in the 90th minute. Napoli did not lift the European Cup, but Pio Esposito refused to let the final die quietly.
body: Pio Esposito entered the final with 27 goals and 12 assists. He leaves Old Trafford with 29 goals, 12 assists and 41 goal contributions.
His first came from the penalty spot in the 17th minute. His second came when Napoli needed a miracle: Buongiorno's release in the 90th, Pio through, Pio finishing, Napoli alive.

Weeks earlier he had scored at 90+2 in Turin to preserve the Invincibles season. Against Atlético Madrid he had delivered the goal that broke a 134-minute deadlock. On the largest stage of all, he scored twice.
The European Cup went to PSG. The final still became another chapter in Pio's emergence as the face of this Napoli era.

comments.text: 29 + 12. Ma quel gol al 90° lo ricorderò per sempre.
Two goals but zero Champions League trophies. Agenda survives.

replies.text: You watched him score TWICE in the final and somehow logged on stronger. Incredible.

comments.text: He gave us the chance to keep fighting. That matters.

articles.label: SCUDETTO PARADE
articles.headline: “I’LL BE BACK. CAUSE I’M NOT FUCKING LEAVING.”
articles.dek: At Napoli’s Scudetto parade, Stefan Saladino ends the Real Madrid saga himself: he is staying.
body: The Champions League final ended in heartbreak. Napoli came home with something else to celebrate: an unbeaten Scudetto and the Coppa Italia.
Then, during the Scudetto parade, Stefan Saladino finally answered the question he had refused to answer before the final.
“Hell of a year. I’m proud of every single fucking person in this room. We’ll be back. And guess what? I’ll be back. Cause I’m not fucking leaving.”

That is the announcement. After Real Madrid's approach and weeks of refusing to discuss his future while Napoli were still competing, Saladino has publicly committed himself to Napoli for next season.

The timing matters. This was not a statement issued after a victory in Europe. It came after Napoli fell 3–2 to PSG in extra time — at the celebration of a season that still delivered an undefeated league championship and the Coppa Italia.
The message to the squad and the city is simple: the project does not end with the loss at Old Trafford. Napoli are coming back for Europe, and their manager intends to lead them there.

comments.text: NON SE NE VA. IL MISTER RESTA. ADESSO TORNIAMO A PRENDERCI QUELLA COPPA.
Went from the Kawhi deflection before the final to “I’m not fucking leaving” at the parade. Cinema.
Well. That answers that.
“WE’LL BE BACK.” Pio 22 anni. Paz. Kayode. Bastoni. Buongiorno. Andiamo di nuovo.
Sono felice. Sono terrorizzato. Voglio già la prossima Champions.
Ha annunciato che resta con una parolaccia alla parata. Nessuna professionalità. Saladino OUT.

replies.text: This may be your most difficult day.

articles.label: FINAL · GAME DAY
articles.headline: OLD TRAFFORD. ONE NIGHT. EVERYTHING.
articles.dek: Napoli have crossed Inter, Real Madrid, Atlético Madrid and Barcelona. PSG are the last gate between the Invincibles and the first European Cup in club history.
body: This is no longer a preview weeks in the distance. It is game day. Napoli, champions of Italy without a league defeat and winners of the Coppa Italia, are ninety minutes — or however long the final demands — from the European Cup.

The road is almost absurd in retrospect: Inter, Real Madrid, Atlético Madrid, Barcelona. Every tie asked Napoli a different question. Every time Stefan Saladino's side found an answer. Paris Saint-Germain are the last one.

The stakes are clean. Win and Napoli complete the treble and lift the Champions League for the first time in club history. Lose and an extraordinary season remains extraordinary — but the last page belongs to Manchester.

Around Europe, the story is larger than Napoli's first final. Real Madrid have already approached Saladino after Napoli eliminated them. The manager has deferred every decision until the season is finished. That means the answer waits on the other side of this match.
For now there is only PSG.

comments.text: INTER. MADRID. ATLETI. BARCA. PSG. Finish the sentence.
NOVANTA MINUTI. PIO, PORTACI LA COPPA.
Non ho dormito. Non dormirò. Forza Napoli.
Una finale definisce gli standard. Vincere. Poi Saladino OUT.
Da Napoli a Parigi. Fate la storia.

articles.label: Tactical Board
articles.headline: THE TEAMS ARE TAKING SHAPE: NAPOLI CHOOSE COURAGE
articles.dek: Pio and Beier together. Paz behind them. Davies and Endrick wide. PSG answer with Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé and Kang-In.
body: Napoli's planned XI: Meret; Kayode, Buongiorno, Bastoni, Cucurella; McTominay; Endrick, Paz, Davies; Beier, Pio Esposito.

It is an aggressive choice. Saladino is not adding a midfielder merely because the occasion is enormous. Pio and Beier — 75 goal contributions in all competitions between them — start together, with Paz connecting the attack and Davies and Endrick giving Napoli width and acceleration.
PSG's probable 4-3-3: Chevalier; Carvajal, Marquinhos, Pacho, Nuno Mendes; Vitinha, João Neves, Zaïre-Emery; Kang-In, Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia.
The emotional subplot is unavoidable: Kvaratskhelia, once a Napoli star, stands on the opposite side of the club's first Champions League final.

The central risk is PSG's three-man midfield against McTominay's enormous defensive workload. Paz cannot disappear from that battle. On the other side, Napoli will believe Davies can attack the corridor around Carvajal and Kang-In, while Pio and Beier force Marquinhos and Pacho into repeated decisions.

Napoli's bench includes Di Lorenzo, Moore, Stach, De Bruyne, Lang, Geertruida, Peacock, Marín and Chiesa. PSG can call on Rúben, Doku, Pickford, Fabián, Gonçalo Ramos, Zabarnyi and Lewis-Skelly among the substitutes shown.

comments.text: Coraggio sì, ma Paz deve aiutare McTominay. Tre contro uno in mezzo sarebbe suicidio.
Pio AND Beier. Good. Do not reach the final and become somebody else.
Carvajal side. Attack it immediately.
And if the match needs a different brain after an hour, Kevin is sitting right there.

articles.label: Tale of the Tape
articles.headline: NAPOLI vs PSG: WHO HAS THE EDGE, POSITION BY POSITION?
articles.dek: From Meret against Chevalier to Pio and Beier against Marquinhos and Pacho, we grade the final without pretending either side has a weak link.
body: GOALKEEPER — NAPOLI EDGE. Meret has earned this call through the knockout run. Inter, Madrid, Atlético and Barcelona all produced moments in which Napoli needed their goalkeeper to keep the tie alive, and he repeatedly did. Chevalier is a high-level opponent, but Napoli enter the final with a keeper whose European form has become part of the team's identity.

RIGHT BACK — PSG SLIGHT EDGE ON PEDIGREE; NAPOLI EDGE ON LEGS. Carvajal brings enormous big-match experience. Kayode brings the athleticism and fearlessness that have made him Napoli's long-term answer on the right. Against Kvaratskhelia, Kayode faces one of the defining individual assignments of the night.

CENTRE-BACKS — EVEN. Marquinhos and Pacho give PSG quality and composure. Bastoni and Buongiorno have become the foundation of an undefeated league champion and have already survived this Champions League gauntlet. There is no meaningful weakness to target simply because of the names on the team sheet.

LEFT BACK — PSG SLIGHT EDGE. Nuno Mendes is one of PSG's most dangerous two-way weapons and can turn Kvaratskhelia's side into an overload. Cucurella's job is less glamorous and potentially just as important: manage Kang-In, choose his forward moments and avoid leaving Bastoni exposed.

CENTRAL MIDFIELD — PSG EDGE. Vitinha, João Neves and Zaïre-Emery give PSG three natural midfielders against a Napoli structure built around McTominay with Paz higher. This is the clearest structural advantage on either team sheet. Napoli can compensate through work rate, compactness and Paz dropping into the battle; if they cannot, PSG can own the ball.

ATTACKING MIDFIELD / CREATIVE HUB — NAPOLI EDGE. Paz has become the long-term centerpiece and already owns one of the season's defining European goals against Barcelona. Napoli also retain De Bruyne as a game-changing option from the bench.

RIGHT-SIDE ATTACK — NAPOLI SLIGHT EDGE IN DIRECT THREAT. Endrick's explosiveness gives Napoli a transition weapon capable of changing the geometry of the match instantly. Kang-In offers PSG technique and combination play. Their jobs are different; for a one-match final, Napoli's vertical threat gets the narrow call.

LEFT-SIDE ATTACK — PSG EDGE. Kvaratskhelia against his former club is the headline matchup and PSG can pair him with Nuno Mendes. Napoli answer with Davies pushed high, whose speed and production make this far from comfortable for Paris. But the former Napoli star gives PSG the individual edge here.

CENTRE-FORWARD — NAPOLI EDGE IN DEPTH OF THREAT. PSG use Dembélé centrally in the probable XI. Napoli start both Pio Esposito and Maximilian Beier: 27 goals and 12 assists for Pio in all competitions, 25 and 11 for Beier. More importantly, their goals have decided knockout ties and rescued the Invincibles season. Napoli can threaten the box in two different ways at once.

BENCH — EVEN, DIFFERENT WEAPONS. PSG can introduce Doku and Gonçalo Ramos to radically change the attack, with Fabián available in midfield. Napoli can turn to De Bruyne for control and invention, Chiesa for direct running, Stach for midfield reinforcement, Geertruida for defensive versatility and Moore or Lang for fresh attacking legs.

VERDICT — PSG have the cleaner midfield structure and dangerous left-side overload. Napoli have the goalkeeper in form, two-striker punch, elite transition weapons and a bench built to change the type of match. There is no obvious overall favourite from the team sheets alone. The final may be decided by whether Napoli can survive PSG's midfield advantage long enough to force Paris to defend Napoli's front five.

comments.text: PSG midfield edge is the scary one. Napoli striker edge is the fun one. This final is going to be completely normal and healthy.
Bastoni e Buongiorno hanno già visto Madrid e Barcellona. Nessuna paura.
PIO + BEIER. Fate i conti dopo.
Vederlo dall’altra parte in questa partita farà malissimo.

articles.label: The Reunion
articles.headline: KVARA, NAPOLI AND THE CRUELEST POSSIBLE REUNION
articles.dek: A player woven into modern Napoli history now stands between the club and the European Cup.
body: There are easier ways to meet an old friend.

Kvaratskhelia's place in Napoli's modern story does not disappear because he now wears PSG colours. That is precisely why this final carries an emotional edge beyond tactics. A player once associated with Napoli's rise now has the ability to deny the club the greatest European night in its history.

Sentiment ends at kickoff. Kayode, Buongiorno and the right side of Napoli's defensive structure have to treat him as the elite opponent he is. PSG will look to combine Kvaratskhelia with Nuno Mendes and force Napoli into choices about when to double and when to hold shape.
After the final there will be room for memory. During it, there is only the duel.

comments.text: Ti abbiamo amato. Stasera sei l’avversario.
What a stage for Kayode. No bigger test.
Ovviamente il destino doveva fare questo a noi.

articles.label: International Watch
articles.headline: EUROPE IS WATCHING NAPOLI TRY TO FINISH THE IMPOSSIBLE
articles.dek: An undefeated Italian champion, a first-time finalist, a brutal knockout route and a manager wanted by Real Madrid: the final has become a European story.
body: The final carries storylines that travel well beyond Naples and Manchester.

Napoli arrive as unbeaten Serie A champions and Coppa Italia winners, seeking a treble and the first European Cup in club history. Their route — Inter, Real Madrid, Atlético Madrid and Barcelona — removes any argument that the draw carried them here.

PSG bring a side loaded with international quality and a former Napoli icon in Kvaratskhelia. Real Madrid, meanwhile, have approached Saladino after being eliminated by his team. No decision will be made until the season is over.

That leaves Europe with one final image before the summer begins: a Napoli project that was supposed to be building toward this level has arrived early, and now has one match to turn an extraordinary season into something historically difficult to compare.

comments.text: If he wins after this route, Madrid will want him even more.
Non mi piace dirlo, ma il percorso europeo è indiscutibile.
No shortcuts. One more giant.

articles.label: Player Interviews
articles.headline: “WE DIDN’T COME THIS FAR TO LOOK AT THE CUP.”
articles.dek: Pio, Beier, Bastoni, Meret and Paz speak before the biggest match in Napoli history — and PSG answer from the other side.
body: PIO ESPOSITO — “I don't think about being the player who scores the winning goal. I think about us winning. If the chance comes to me, I have to finish it. If it comes to Maxi, Nico, Endrick, anyone, then I celebrate with them. We didn't come this far to look at the cup.”
MAXIMILIAN BEIER — “People can talk about pressure. We played Inter, Madrid, Atlético and Barcelona to get here. We know what these matches feel like now. PSG have to defend us too.”

ALESSANDRO BASTONI — “A final is not a reward. It is another match you have to win. We respect PSG because they have quality everywhere, but respect is not fear. We have earned the right to believe we belong here.”

ALEX MERET — “There were moments in every round when we had to suffer. That will happen again. You cannot become impatient because PSG have ten good minutes. You stay in the match. In a final, the next action can change your life.”

NICO PAZ — “When you are young you imagine matches like this, but the real thing is quieter in your head. You prepare for the spaces, the press, the first touch. If you start thinking about lifting the trophy before kickoff, you are already somewhere else.”
PSG — KVARATSKHELIA: “Napoli will always mean something to me. I know what that shirt means to the city. But I play for Paris now, and in a final there is no room for sentiment. We want the trophy.”
PSG — MARQUINHOS: “They did not arrive here by accident. Look at who they eliminated. If anyone still thinks Napoli are a surprise, they have not been paying attention.”
The tone from both camps is clear. Napoli are refusing the underdog label. PSG are refusing to give them one.

comments.text: “NON SIAMO ARRIVATI FIN QUI PER GUARDARE LA COPPA.” STAMPATELO.
“PSG have to defend us too.” That is exactly the mentality.
RISPETTO NON È PAURA.
Meret sounds exactly like a keeper who has already survived four knockout rounds.
Le parole di Kvara fanno male. Ma per novanta minuti è PSG.
Marquinhos gets it. This is not a Cinderella run.

articles.label: Manager Press Conference
articles.headline: “WE WERE BUILT FOR THIS.”
articles.dek: Saladino promises Napoli will not hide against PSG, shuts down the Real Madrid question and leaves the room laughing with a Toronto sports reference.
body: MARCO BELLINI, IL CALCIO SERA — Asked whether Napoli would become conservative in the final, Saladino laughed off the idea: “Anyone who expects us to sit in a low block for 90 minutes hasn’t been paying attention. I’m not going to be the one to tell Pio, Maxy, Endrick and Phonsy to sit back for 90 minutes. I don’t have the balls to do that.”

CLAIRE DUBOIS, L’ÉQUIPE — On PSG’s attacking quality and Napoli’s willingness to commit forward: “I believe that I can trust in my guys to know when it’s on and commit and when to be patient. Our back line in my mind can hang with the best of them. That’s no disrespect to PSG. They have some world class players on that side. But as has been said before: respect, not fear.”

JAVIER ORTEGA, MARCA — Asked whether he could guarantee he would manage Napoli next season, Saladino invoked his Toronto roots and Kawhi Leonard: “I was born in Toronto and I’m going to paraphrase a Raptors legend — that’s a basketball team for those not in the know — Kawhi Leonard. I’m here to talk about this team and this game. I believe I’ve already put out a statement about that matter, so you can go back and read it if you’d like.”

GIULIA ROMANO, RADIO NAPOLI CENTRALE — Asked whether he could really treat the final like a normal match: “No… penso di no. Perché non è una partita normale. Ma è così che la vogliamo. Quante volte quest’anno questa squadra ha sentito la pressione? E il momento è mai diventato troppo grande? No. Siamo stati costruiti per questo.”

JAMES RICHARDSON, BBC SPORT — On Napoli’s young core: “Many hadn’t played in a Champions League semi-final either. Yet here we are in the final. I don’t need to tell them anything. And I certainly don’t need to protect them. This is a group mature beyond its years. And we’re just getting started.”

DANIEL RICCI, TSN — The final question turned toward Toronto sports. Asked whether a Champions League final, a Leafs Game 7 lead or a Blue Jays ninth-inning lead was more stressful, Saladino answered: “Daniel, you’re going to bring up a Blue Jays one-run lead in the ninth almost a year to the day after they blew the World Series against the Dodgers? You know I still have nightmares over that. But listen, if Louie Varland wants to come on for us in the 85th minute and we’re protecting a slim lead, I think I’d have to hear him out. I think that’s a sentiment shared by both Phonsie and myself.”

The room broke into laughter. Then the Napoli manager stood, thanked the media and left. Afterwards, Alphonso Davies was told that Saladino had volunteered Louie Varland as an 85th-minute closer if Napoli were protecting a lead. Davies laughed: “Honestly? I’d hear him out too. Toronto people have been through enough. If Louie’s got one clean inning — sorry, ten clean minutes — in him, get him a shirt.” The final message beneath the jokes and deflections was unmistakable: Napoli are not arriving at Old Trafford hoping to survive. They believe this stage belongs to them.

comments.text: “SIAMO STATI COSTRUITI PER QUESTO.” Basta. Andiamo.
He really said I am NOT telling that front line to defend for 90 minutes 😂
RISPETTO. NON PAURA.
Kawhi reference in a Champions League final presser. Toronto has officially reached Naples.
That was absolutely not an answer to the Madrid question 👀
Phonsie co-signing the Louie Varland emergency substitution from somewhere in the dressing room 😭
Ha scherzato sul bullpen. Io invece sto già male pensando all’85°.

articles.label: Managerial Bombshell
articles.headline: THE CLUB HE KNOCKED OUT NOW WANTS HIM.
articles.dek: Real Madrid have approached Stefan Saladino after dismissing their manager in the aftermath of Napoli’s Champions League elimination of Madrid. Saladino will make no decision until Napoli’s season is over.
body: Real Madrid want Stefan Saladino.

The approach completes an extraordinary circle. Napoli beat Madrid 1–0 in Naples and then survived the Bernabéu for a 1–1 draw, eliminating the Spanish giants 2–1 on aggregate. Madrid subsequently dismissed their manager. Now they have turned toward the coach who helped end their European campaign.

The timing could hardly be more explosive. Saladino has since led Napoli to the Serie A title without losing a league match, won the Coppa Italia and reached the first European Cup final in club history.
There is no decision. The manager will not accept or reject Madrid before the season is finished. Paris Saint-Germain and the Champions League final come first.
Anything beyond that is speculation. Napoli’s position, Madrid’s persistence and Saladino’s future belong to the summer. For now, Paris.

comments.text: Il Real prende il nostro allenatore perché li abbiamo eliminati? Questa stagione è una sceneggiatura.
He beat Madrid at this level. Of course the club is looking.
Se vuole Madrid che vada. Nessuno è più grande del Napoli. Saladino OUT.
The man demanding he leave has accidentally discovered the exact opposite of his usual position.
PRIMA PARIGI. Il resto dopo.

articles.label: Serie A Awards
articles.headline: INVINCIBLE. INVISIBLE.
articles.dek: Napoli went 28–10–0 and won Serie A without losing. Not one Napoli player was selected in the league’s Team of the Season.
body: Thirty-eight matches. Twenty-eight wins. Ten draws. Zero defeats. Ninety-four points. Serie A champions.
And zero Napoli players in the Serie A Team of the Season.
The selected XI shown by the league: Maignan; Dimarco, Kossounou, Mancini, Baku; Sauer, Rabiot, Yıldız, D. Doué; Gimenez and Openda.

The omission is particularly striking in attack. Pio Esposito produced 20 league goals and nine assists for the undefeated champions. Openda, selected in the XI, recorded 27 goals and seven assists. Gimenez, also selected, scored 21 league goals.
Then there is another contradiction: Charles De Ketelaere was named Serie A Player of the Season after a 19-goal, eight-assist league campaign — but he is not in the Team of the Season either.

The award does not need to be declared illegitimate to acknowledge the obvious: its outcomes demand explanation. An undefeated champion supplied none of the eleven, while the league’s own Player of the Season also failed to make the XI.
Napoli have the trophy that matters most. The supporters are still entitled to ask how this happened.

comments.text: VENTI GOL. NOVE ASSIST. CAMPIONE IMBATTUTO. ZERO NAPOLI NELL’UNDICI. SPIEGATE.
Non uno. NON UNO. 94 punti e nessuno dei nostri.
Finally an awards panel brave enough to resist propaganda.
CDK giocatore dell’anno ma neanche lui nella squadra dell’anno. Il sistema ha mangiato se stesso.
Openda con 27+7 ci sta. Ma zero Napoli dopo una stagione imbattuta è difficile da capire.
Pio 20+9. CDK 19+8 and POTY. CDK absent from TOTS. Napoli 28-10-0 and zero selections. I need the algorithm on trial.

articles.label: Player of the Season
articles.headline: DE KETELAERE WINS IT. THE NUMBERS START THE ARGUMENT.
articles.dek: Charles De Ketelaere is Serie A Player of the Season with 19 goals and eight assists. Pio finished 20+9. Openda finished 27+7.
body: Charles De Ketelaere has been named Serie A Player of the Season after recording 19 goals and eight assists in league play.
Those are elite numbers. They are also not the largest attacking totals among the leading candidates supplied by the season ledger.
Openda finished with 27 goals and seven assists. Pio Esposito finished with 20 goals and nine assists for unbeaten champions Napoli. Gimenez scored 21 league goals.

Individual awards are not arithmetic alone, and the available information does not establish the full voting criteria. But the numbers guarantee debate — especially in Naples, where Pio’s league campaign ended with the 90+2 equaliser that preserved an undefeated season.
The strangest detail arrived alongside the award: De Ketelaere himself was omitted from Serie A’s Team of the Season.

comments.text: Complimenti a CDK. Però Pio 20+9 e campione imbattuto. La domanda è lecita.
Openda 34 league G+A, Pio 29, CDK 27. Whatever the criteria are, production clearly was not the only one.
Correct winner. I have no further evidence and require none.

articles.label: Academy
articles.headline: RIZZI AND HABER WANT A PATH. NAPOLI HAVE A DECISION COMING.
articles.dek: Emiliano Rizzi and Devin Haber are considering their futures if they are not called into the senior squad. No action will be taken before the Champions League final.
body: Two academy situations have moved onto Napoli’s summer agenda.
Emiliano Rizzi, a 17-year-old central midfielder currently rated 64, and Devin Haber, a 17-year-old left winger rated 58, are considering leaving if they are not promoted to the senior squad.

The transfer window is closed and Napoli have no intention of allowing a development decision to distract from Paris. Their futures will be reviewed after the Champions League final as part of the wider academy and loan-return audit.
Promotion would not necessarily mean first-team minutes. It could instead protect the players inside the senior development structure before future loan or transfer decisions.

comments.text: Rizzi a 17 anni e 64 merita almeno il passaggio tra i grandi. Poi si decide il prestito.
Protect the assets, then audit. Paris first.

articles.label: INVINCIBILI
articles.headline: PIO. 90+2. INVINCIBLE.
articles.dek: Three down at halftime. Beier scored twice. Then, with the unbeaten season on its final breath, Pio Esposito buried the rebound that completed a 3–3 comeback and an undefeated Serie A campaign.
body: Napoli's unbeaten Serie A season survived by seconds.

Torino threatened to destroy it before halftime. Vlašić struck in the 13th minute, Ilić converted a rebound in the 25th and Musa made it 3–0 in the 37th. The champions went into the interval staring at their first league defeat of the season in Match 38.

Maximilian Beier changed the match. He scored in the 49th minute and struck again in the 70th, the second created by Pio Esposito. Napoli had twenty minutes to find one more goal and preserve thirty-seven matches of unbeaten work.
At 90+2, Beier broke through alone. Vanja Milinković-Savić saved. For a fraction of a second, the Invincibles season appeared finished.
Pio Esposito was there for the rebound. He buried it.
Torino 3–3 Napoli. From 3–0 down. On the final day. With the equaliser in the final allotted minute of stoppage time.
Napoli finish Serie A with 28 wins, 10 draws, zero defeats and 94 points. Champions. Invincible.

Before the match Saladino said: “Not playing to win is playing to lose. If you don’t look to attack, you’ll be chasing the game before you realize it.” Napoli spent the afternoon chasing the game. They never stopped attacking.
Now Paris. Paris Saint-Germain await in the Champions League final on May 27.

comments.text: PIO AL 90+2. NON ESISTE UN MODO PIÙ ASSURDO PER DIVENTARE INVINCIBILI.
Beier came off the bench at 3-0 and nearly saved the entire season himself. Two goals and the shot that created Pio’s rebound. Superstar.
TRE A ZERO. ULTIMA GIORNATA. E NON ABBIAMO PERSO. Questa squadra è fuori di testa.
Al 37 ero già morto. Al 90+2 sono morto una seconda volta. INVINCIBILI.
Tap-in merchant. Beier did all the work.

replies.text: Al 90+2 della giornata 38 ci devi ESSERE su quel tap-in. Piangi.
27 goals. 12 assists. Invincibles-saving goal. Keep the agenda alive though.

comments.text: Andare sotto 3–0 col Torino resta inaccettabile. Il pareggio non cancella tutto. Saladino OUT.

replies.text: 28-10-0. Hai scelto proprio oggi per continuare questa guerra?
You have now demanded his firing during an undefeated championship season. Historic commitment to the bit.

comments.text: “Non giocare per vincere è giocare per perdere.” Poi sotto 3–0 hanno continuato ad attaccare fino all’ultimo secondo. Questa frase adesso resta.
The league season ends unbeaten and somehow Paris is still the biggest match of the year. What a season.

articles.label: The Halftime Weapon
articles.headline: BEIER REFUSED TO LET IT DIE.
articles.dek: Two second-half goals, then the 90+2 breakaway that created the rebound Pio buried. Maximilian Beier dragged Napoli back from the edge.
body: Napoli were 3–0 down at halftime and the unbeaten season was disappearing. Then Maximilian Beier took over.
He scored four minutes after the restart. In the 70th minute, Pio Esposito supplied him for a second. At 3–2, the impossible had become plausible.
Then came 90+2. Beier got in alone and Vanja Milinković-Savić saved, denying the hat trick. But the chance was not dead. Pio attacked the rebound and completed the comeback.
Beier finishes the Torino match on 25 goals and 11 assists in Napoli's canonical season ledger: 36 goal contributions.

comments.text: Entra con la stagione imbattuta quasi morta: gol, gol, poi crea il caos del 3–3. IMMENSO.
Pio ha scritto l’ultima riga, ma Beier ha rimesso in piedi il libro.
This is exactly why having Beier available as the weapon mattered.

articles.label: Our Guy
articles.headline: OF COURSE IT WAS PIO.
articles.dek: At 90+2, with 37 unbeaten league matches about to disappear on the final day, Pio Esposito followed the play and buried the rebound.
body: There are goals that add to a total, and there are goals that become part of a season's identity.
Pio Esposito's 90+2 equaliser in Turin belongs to the second category.
After assisting Beier for 3–2, Pio kept running when Beier went through in stoppage time. Vanja Milinković-Savić made the save. Pio was exactly where the rebound fell.
Goal number 27. Assist number 12. Thirty-nine goal contributions. More importantly: the goal that preserved Napoli's unbeaten Serie A season on Match 38.
Atlético had already given him a European legacy moment. Torino gave him a domestic one.

comments.text: Quella maglia non la tolgo mai più.
Atletico winner. Match 38 equalizer at 90+2. He keeps showing up exactly where history is happening.
Ventisette gol. Dodici assist. Ma io ricorderò sempre QUESTO gol.

articles.label: 37 DOWN. ONE TO GO.
articles.headline: ONE. MORE. MATCH.
articles.dek: Beier and Pio dispatch Sassuolo 2–0. Napoli are now 37 matches unbeaten with only Torino standing between them and an Invincibles Serie A season.
body: Napoli are ninety minutes from an unbeaten Serie A season.
The champions handled Sassuolo 2–0 at home, taking control almost immediately. In the third minute Pio Esposito released Maximilian Beier, who finished for 1–0.
In the 34th minute Napoli won a penalty. Pio took responsibility himself and, cool as he liked, buried it into the top-right corner.
The second half produced little drama. For a team carrying historic stakes into every remaining league minute, that was almost the ideal outcome: control, clean sheet, no unnecessary chaos.
The league record is now 28 wins, nine draws and no defeats: 93 points from 37 matches.
Only Torino remain. Avoid defeat there and Napoli complete the entire Serie A campaign without losing.
Then, six days later, Paris Saint-Germain await in the Champions League final.

comments.text: TRENTASETTE. Ne manca UNA. Non fatemi respirare fino a Torino.
Campioni, Coppa Italia in bacheca, e adesso novanta minuti dalla stagione imbattuta. Assurdo.
Il secondo tempo più bello possibile: niente caos, niente drammi. Torino e basta.
Festeggiate pure il Sassuolo. Se perdete a Torino, questi 37 non significano niente. Saladino OUT.

articles.label: Pio Produces Again
articles.headline: PIO CREATED ONE. THEN TOOK THE PENALTY HIMSELF.
articles.dek: An assist for Beier, a ruthless penalty and another match shaped by Napoli’s leading scorer.
body: Pio Esposito needed three minutes to influence the match. His pass released Beier for Napoli's opener.
Thirty-one minutes later he stood over the penalty spot himself and sent the ball into the top-right corner for 2–0.
That moves Pio to 26 goals and 11 assists across Napoli's canonical season ledger. The numbers now sit beside something larger: he is producing while every remaining match carries historical weight.
Napoli did not need another goal after halftime. Pio had already helped settle the game.

comments.text: Ventisei gol e undici assist. E ricordiamoci da dove è partita questa stagione.
La cosa migliore oggi? Assist dopo tre minuti, rigore senza paura, partita chiusa.
Pio has gone from storyline to one of the defining players of the season.

articles.label: History Awaits
articles.headline: TORINO. 90 MINUTES. HISTORY.
articles.dek: There is no longer any arithmetic to do. Napoli have played 37 Serie A matches without defeat. One remains.
body: The Scudetto has already been won. The Coppa Italia has already been lifted. Yet Napoli's final Serie A match now carries a prize that cannot be placed in the trophy cabinet.
Thirty-seven matches. Twenty-eight wins. Nine draws. Zero defeats.
Torino away is the final obstacle between Napoli and an Invincibles season. Win or draw and the record is complete. Lose, and an extraordinary unbeaten run ends on the final day.
There will be a Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain six days later. That matters enormously. But this opportunity exists once, right now.
Ninety minutes remain between Napoli and perfection across an entire league campaign.

comments.text: Non mi interessa come. Vincete o pareggiate. Tornate da Torino imbattuti.
Una partita per scrivere una parola accanto a questa squadra per sempre: INVINCIBILI.
Finalmente una partita con pressione vera. Vediamo se reggono. Saladino OUT.

articles.label: COPPA ITALIA CHAMPIONS
articles.headline: DOUBLE. DONE. DAVIES WINS THE COPPA AND NAPOLI LIFT TROPHY NUMBER TWO.
articles.dek: Alphonso Davies scores the only goal, Alex Meret stands tall and Napoli beat Roma 1–0 to add the Coppa Italia to their Scudetto.
body: Napoli are Coppa Italia champions. Three days after rotating heavily at Atalanta to protect the first-choice legs, Saladino's side beat Roma 1–0 and collected the second trophy of an extraordinary season.
Roma nearly struck first, hitting the post in the sixth minute. Napoli settled immediately rather than retreating, and Svilar was forced into a major save from Endrick in the 11th.
The breakthrough came in the 19th minute. The ball broke for Alphonso Davies and he finished it himself: no assist, no complication, 1–0 Napoli.

Roma threatened again before halftime. Meret made a big save from Wesley in the 31st minute and then another on the ensuing corner. Those interventions preserved the lead and became increasingly important as the final tightened.

Napoli kept searching after the break. Davies forced Svilar into another strong save from distance in the 46th. Paz was caught offside in the 60th, Pio Esposito was denied in the 65th and McTominay sent the rebound wide. Roma flashed an effort past the far post in the 73rd.
Davies eventually emptied the tank and made way for Federico Chiesa. The Atalanta hat-trick hero nearly killed the final in the 85th, only for Svilar to make one more save.

Then came the whistle. Serie A champions. Coppa Italia champions. Two trophies secured. The unbeaten league campaign remains alive. Paris Saint-Germain and the Champions League final still wait on May 27.

comments.text: CAMPIONI D’ITALIA. CAMPIONI DI COPPA. E non abbiamo ancora finito.
Davies decide la finale, Meret la protegge. Questa squadra sa vincere in ogni modo.
Un solo gol e novanta minuti di ansia. La Coppa è nostra. Adesso posso respirare.
Due trofei non cancellano le domande. Parigi è il vero esame. Saladino OUT.

articles.label: Final Hero
articles.headline: DAVIES WAS EVERYWHERE. THEN HE WON THE FINAL.
