Then came the counter. Davies drove Napoli forward, McTominay received and released Beier through the middle, and the striker finished in the 89th minute. The player rested during the 0–0 league draw with Cagliari had been saved for precisely this kind of night.
Napoli managed the final stoppage time and heard the whistle with the clean sheet intact. The reward is enormous, but incomplete: a one-goal advantage must now be defended — or extended — in Madrid.

The message from the Maradona is nevertheless unmistakable. Napoli entered this tie asking whether they belonged in this company. For one night, at least, Real Madrid were the side forced to answer Napoli.
comments: BEIER. EIGHTY NINE. REAL MADRID. I AM NOT SLEEPING TONIGHT.
Scott McTominay with the assist in the biggest moment of the season. Of course.
That late Mbappé save is every bit as important as the goal.
Cucurella spent ninety minutes choosing violence and I loved every second.
One goal. Bernabéu still to come. This tie is nowhere near finished.
Bellingham kept finding a blue wall in front of him.
RESTED FOR CAGLIARI. SAVED FOR MADRID. 89TH MINUTE.
This did not feel like a smash-and-grab. That is the part that changes the conversation.

articles.label: Opinion · Champions League
articles.headline: Napoli Did Not Survive Madrid. They Beat Them.
articles.dek: The scoreline is narrow. The significance is not. Napoli spent ninety minutes treating Madrid as an opponent rather than an event.
body: There is a difference between enduring a great team and competing with one. Napoli’s 1–0 victory over Real Madrid belonged firmly to the second category.

Madrid had their moments. Bellingham hit the post. Mbappé forced Meret into major saves. Their speed threatened to stretch the game whenever Napoli lost the ball. But the night never became a ninety-minute siege, and that distinction matters.

Napoli created genuine chances, forced Alisson into important work, attacked in transition and continued trying to win the match even after surviving Madrid’s strongest spells. Endrick threatened. Davies carried the ball into dangerous territory. Buongiorno nearly scored. Then Beier actually did.

The tactical achievement was balance. Bastoni and Buongiorno defended aggressively without turning every Madrid possession into an emergency. Cucurella was exceptional on the left, repeatedly stepping into duels and refusing to let Madrid settle. McTominay protected the centre and still had enough in reserve to create the winner.

This is what the pre-match demand to respect Madrid without fearing them was supposed to look like. Napoli respected Mbappé’s speed and Bellingham’s movement. They did not respect them so much that they abandoned their own ambition.

Now comes the dangerous part: believing the work is finished. It is not. One goal at the Bernabéu can disappear in seconds. Napoli cannot spend the second leg defending an imaginary finish line for ninety minutes.

But they should travel with something more valuable than hope. They have evidence. They have already looked Madrid in the eye for ninety minutes and discovered that the game still works the same way. Win duels. Protect space. Take chances. Make stars uncomfortable.
Napoli have not eliminated Real Madrid. They have done something simpler and perhaps more important: they have made Madrid chase them.
comments: The key line: the game still works the same way. Do not go to Madrid hypnotised by the stadium.
We are not through. But we are absolutely not tourists.
The maturity was the best part. Nobody started forcing hero balls because it was Madrid.
Now somehow come back down to earth for Serie A after THAT.
If Napoli sit on the 1–0 in Madrid they will regret it. If they play again, we have a tie.

articles.label: Champions League · The Wall
articles.headline: Cucurella, Bastoni, Buongiorno, Meret: The Wall Madrid Could Not Break
articles.dek: Madrid found the post, found space in flashes and found Meret when they finally escaped the line. What they never found was a goal.
body: For all the attention on Beier’s 89th-minute winner, Napoli’s first-leg advantage was built by the men behind him.

Cucurella set the tone. He attacked duels, disrupted combinations and repeatedly won possession when Madrid tried to overload his side. It was exactly the confrontational edge Napoli wanted from him without the performance ever tipping into recklessness.
Asked afterward about spending the night in Madrid’s faces, Cucurella smiled: “Were they frustrated? I did not notice. I was busy defending.”

Inside him, Bastoni and Buongiorno were immense. Bellingham was denied clean central receptions, crosses were attacked early, and Madrid were repeatedly encouraged toward areas where Napoli could defend with numbers.

And when the structure finally cracked, Meret was there. His late saves from Mbappé preserved 0–0 long enough for Napoli to find the winner. Days after agreeing a new contract, the goalkeeper again justified the club’s faith on the largest stage available.

The clean sheet should not be mistaken for comfort. Madrid created enough danger to remind Napoli exactly what awaits in the second leg. But the first ninety minutes established a standard: Madrid will have to earn every metre.
comments: New contract and immediately another European clean sheet masterclass.
Bastoni and Buongiorno together is obscene.
Do not forget Kayode surviving that speed on the other side either.
A clean sheet against that attack is not luck. It is ninety minutes of work.

articles.label: Player Focus · Maximilian Beier
articles.headline: Saved for Madrid. Beier Needed One Moment.
articles.dek: Rested against Cagliari, unleashed against Madrid, decisive in the 89th minute. Napoli’s quietest striker produced the loudest moment of the season.
body: Maximilian Beier did not need a speech. He needed a run.
Napoli had deliberately protected him during the 0–0 draw with Cagliari, preserving one of the squad’s hottest attackers for Real Madrid. In the 89th minute, the decision paid for itself.
Davies launched the transition. McTominay saw the lane. Beier attacked it, received the pass and finished the chance that had eluded both teams all night.

His reaction afterward was entirely in character. Asked what went through his mind when McTominay released him, Beier offered the sort of answer his teammates have come to expect: “Good pass. I had to score.”
That was essentially the whole interview. It was also essentially the whole job.
Beier now owns a Champions League winner against Real Madrid at the Maradona. Whether it becomes the goal that sends Napoli through will be decided in the second leg.
comments: GOOD PASS. I HAD TO SCORE. THIS MAN IS INCREDIBLE.
Five words and one goal. German efficiency.
Give Scott his flowers too. That release was perfect.
And this is why having three real strikers matters. Different nights need different guys.
If we go through that finish becomes immortal.

articles.label: Madrid Fallout · Debate
articles.headline: Alisson, Courtois and a Night of Frustration: Madrid Leave Naples With Questions
articles.dek: Alisson justified his surprise start with major saves, but Madrid still leave the Maradona behind in the tie after Beier’s late winner.
body: Real Madrid’s decision to start Alisson ahead of Courtois became an immediate talking point before kickoff. By full time, blaming the goalkeeper would have been difficult: Alisson made major saves from Endrick and Buongiorno and kept Madrid level until the 89th minute.

The more uncomfortable discussion concerns what happened in front of him. Madrid had dangerous spells and Bellingham struck the post, but Mbappé, Bellingham and the supporting runners were repeatedly forced into crowded areas by Napoli’s defensive structure.

That does not establish that Madrid underestimated Napoli. The evidence is too thin for that conclusion, and Alisson’s performance hardly resembled a goalkeeper treating the occasion casually. But the selection choice and the 1–0 result guarantee that the question will follow Madrid into the second leg.
Madrid also have reasons for confidence. The margin is one goal, their attack did create late openings, and the return will be played on their ground. Napoli’s advantage is real; it is not safe.

What changed in Naples is the burden. Madrid entered the tie as favourites. They now enter the second leg needing to overturn a deficit against a Napoli side that has already demonstrated it can defend them and hurt them.
comments: Alisson was one of our best players. Anyone blaming him did not watch the match.
Courtois can start the second leg. Beier knows where that goal is too.
The keeper discourse is silly. Madrid lost because Napoli competed everywhere.
Please spend the next week debating goalkeepers instead of Cucurella stealing the ball again.
One goal at home. Nobody in Madrid is panicking. Napoli should expect a completely different atmosphere.

articles.label: Exclusive · One-on-One
articles.headline: Bastoni: “I Didn’t Come Here to Watch Napoli Become Great. I Came to Be Part of It.”
articles.dek: At 91 overall and at the heart of an unbeaten Serie A leader, Alessandro Bastoni sits down with the Season Room to talk Napoli, leaving Inter, Italy, the responsibility of defending at the highest level and why this season feels like the beginning rather than the destination.
body: Alessandro Bastoni does not need to be the loudest player in Napoli’s dressing room to command it. This season, his football has done most of the talking.

Now rated 91 overall, the Italian centre-back has become one of the defining pieces of a Napoli side that remains unbeaten in Serie A, leads the championship by eight points, holds a 4–0 first-leg advantage over Torino in the Coppa Italia and is preparing to face Real Madrid in the Champions League Round of 16.

For Bastoni, there is another layer to the story. He arrived in Naples after years associated with Inter, then helped Napoli eliminate his former club from Europe in one of the defining nights of the season. He is also one of the pillars of an Italy side increasingly intertwined with this Napoli project.
We sat down with him before the biggest European tie of Napoli’s season.

SEASON ROOM: Alessandro, when you look at where Napoli are right now — unbeaten in the league, eight points clear, alive in the Coppa and preparing for Real Madrid — is this where you thought the project would be this quickly?

BASTONI: “You always have ambition when you join a club like Napoli. If you don’t, you should not come. But there is a difference between believing something can happen and living it every week. What has impressed me is the consistency. We have had difficult matches, bad moments, matches where we were not brilliant, and we still found ways to stay together. That is normally what separates a good team from one that can win.”
SEASON ROOM: You have developed into a 91-rated defender here. Do you feel like you are playing the best football of your career?

BASTONI: “I feel complete. That is probably the word. When you are younger, you think defending is about winning the duel in front of you. Then you understand it is also about where you stand before the pass, what your teammate needs from you, when to step, when not to step, when to slow the match down. I still want to improve, obviously. But I feel I understand matches better now than I ever have.”
SEASON ROOM: What has Napoli given you that you perhaps did not have before?

BASTONI: “A different responsibility. Here I knew immediately that I could not simply arrive and be another good defender. The expectation was that I would help lead the defensive line. I like that responsibility. Napoli is an emotional club and an emotional city. People tell you when they are happy. They also tell you when they are not. [Laughs.] You feel everything here. I think that has made me sharper.”
SEASON ROOM: There was obviously emotion around facing Inter. Then you went back to San Siro and Napoli eliminated them from the Champions League. What was that experience like?

BASTONI: “I will never pretend Inter means nothing to me. That would be dishonest and disrespectful to people who were important in my life. I grew there as a player. I won there. I have friends there. But football moves forward. When the match begins, I play for Napoli. In Milan, we needed to overturn the tie and that was my only thought. Afterward, yes, you feel many things. But I was proud of our team because that night required character.”
SEASON ROOM: Did that Inter comeback change the way the squad sees itself in Europe?

BASTONI: “I think it confirmed something. We already believed we could compete with strong teams. But belief is easier when nobody has tested it. In Milan we were tested. They hit the bar, Alex made huge saves, Scott cleared one from the line. We suffered. Then we stayed alive and found the goals. You need nights like that if you want to grow in Europe.”
SEASON ROOM: And now the reward is Real Madrid.
BASTONI: “[Smiles.] Yes. Some reward.”
SEASON ROOM: Mbappé, Vinícius, Bellingham. Does a defender look at that list and think differently?

BASTONI: “You respect it. Of course you respect it. If you don’t, you are stupid. These are players who can decide a match in one action. But respect cannot become fear. The moment you start defending the name on the shirt instead of the player in front of you, you have already lost something. We have quality too. They have to defend us as well.”
SEASON ROOM: If Mbappé comes into your channel, what is going through your head?

BASTONI: “Do not let him choose the duel. Players like that want to make you defend the situation they prefer — space behind you, open grass, one against one with momentum. My job is to change the question. Make him receive somewhere he does not want. Make the next pass uncomfortable. And if there is a duel, win it.”
SEASON ROOM: This Napoli side has become unusually Italian at its core — yourself, Buongiorno, Kayode, Pio and others — and you are also together with the national team. Does that connection matter?

BASTONI: “Very much. Club football and the national team are different, but familiarity helps. With Alessandro [Buongiorno], for example, you learn movements without speaking. With Kayode, you see a player growing very quickly. Pio is becoming a very important striker. When you arrive with Italy and already understand how several teammates think, you can build faster.”
SEASON ROOM: What does Italy mean to you at this stage of your career?

BASTONI: “Everything. Playing for Italy never becomes normal. I was fortunate to experience winning with the national team when I was younger, and once you experience something like that you understand the responsibility. My ambition now is not just to be selected. I want to be one of the players responsible for what Italy becomes next.”
SEASON ROOM: There is a sense that Napoli and Italy may both be entering new cycles at the same time. Do you feel that?

BASTONI: “Yes, but cycles are only real afterward. People can say there is a generation, a project, a new era. Fine. You still have to win football matches. What excites me is that there are players here who can be important for Napoli for years and important for Italy for years. If we grow together, that can be powerful.”
SEASON ROOM: Di Lorenzo is considering retirement after the season. As another senior Italian defender, does that make you think about leadership differently?

BASTONI: “Giovanni has earned the right to make that decision in his own time. What he has given Napoli and Italy deserves respect. Leadership is not something you inherit because another player leaves. You earn it every day. But yes, as you get older, you understand that younger players are watching how you react — especially when things go badly. I take that seriously.”
SEASON ROOM: You mentioned younger players. What do you make of Kayode’s rise?

BASTONI: “He is brave. That is the first thing. Young defenders sometimes play as if they are asking permission to be there. Michael does not. He wants the duel. He wants the ball. He will make mistakes because everyone does, but he does not hide afterward. That is a very good quality.”
SEASON ROOM: And the striker situation? Pio, Beier and Endrick are all flying.

BASTONI: “[Laughs.] I am happy I only have to defend them in training. Pio gives you the physical battle and now he is creating so much as well. Beier never stops moving and suddenly he is scoring everything. Endrick can change a match in five minutes. For a defender it is annoying because they ask three different questions. For us, that is excellent.”
SEASON ROOM: What would make this season a success for you?

BASTONI: “Trophies. I know that sounds simple, but we are past the point where being competitive is enough. We have put ourselves in positions where something important is possible. The league is in our hands if we continue doing our job. The Coppa tie is in a very good position, but it is not finished. In Europe we have a huge challenge. Now we have to turn the season into something permanent.”
SEASON ROOM: So you do not see Real Madrid as a free hit?

BASTONI: “No. Absolutely not. Maybe from outside people say Madrid are favourites and if Napoli lose, the season is still good. I understand that. Inside the dressing room, that cannot be our mentality. We respect them, but we want to eliminate them. Otherwise, why play?”
SEASON ROOM: Last one. When you think about Napoli beyond this season, what do you see?

BASTONI: “I see something that can last. That is important to me. I did not come here to watch Napoli become great from a distance. I came to be part of it. We have experienced players, players entering their best years and young players who are growing very fast. If we keep the hunger, this does not have to be one season.”

Bastoni gets up, smiles, and heads back toward training. Real Madrid are five days away. Napoli’s most accomplished defender does not sound like a man satisfied simply to have reached the conversation. He sounds like one who expects Napoli to stay in it.
comments: “I did not come here to watch Napoli become great. I came to be part of it.” BUILD THE STATUE.
91 OVR and somehow the mentality is even higher.
The Inter answer was perfect. Didn’t disrespect his history, didn’t apologize for being Napoli.
Bastoni + Buongiorno + Kayode + Pio together for club AND country. He sees the vision.
“They have to defend us as well.” THAT is the line.
His Mbappé answer is exactly why he is elite. Don’t win the footrace. Prevent Mbappé from choosing the footrace in the first place.
Bastoni saying Pio is becoming important for Italy too. We have moved.
Inter fan here. Painful read but fair. He handled that question with class.

BASTONI: some incredibly intelligent explanation of defensive geometry
ME: kick Mbappé please
“Young defenders sometimes play as if they are asking permission to be there. Michael does not.” I AM FRAMING THIS.
This is what leadership sounds like. Not captain-speech nonsense. Calm, specific, demanding.
“Some reward.” 😂 Bastoni understands the Champions League experience.
Most important part: “we are past the point where being competitive is enough.” Expectations have changed inside the room.
Loved the respect for Giovanni. If this is the captain’s last season, there are serious leaders ready behind him. 🫡
Bastoni admitting Endrick can ruin a match in five minutes. Defender trauma recognizes defender trauma.
“Suddenly he is scoring everything.” EVEN BASTONI HAS JOINED THE BEIER AGENDA.
The Italy section might be the most interesting part. This Napoli core could become the spine of the national team.
“We want to eliminate them. Otherwise, why play?” Yeah okay I am ready for March 7 RIGHT NOW.
Players come and go. The ones supporters remember are the ones who understand the weight of the shirt. He gets it.
This might be my favourite article on the site. More of these sit-downs when somebody has actually earned one.

articles.label: Opinion · Champions League
articles.headline: Respect Madrid. Do Not Fear Them: Napoli’s Five Rules for Surviving the Bernabéu Test
articles.dek: Mbappé, Vinícius and Bellingham give Real Madrid the higher individual ceiling. Napoli’s path is not to hide from that talent — it is to make this a 180-minute contest on their own terms.
body: Real Madrid should be favourites against Napoli. That is not an insult. It is an acknowledgement of a squad whose top end still contains names such as Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior, Jude Bellingham and Federico Valverde. But favourite is not the same thing as inevitable.

Napoli enter this Round of 16 tie unbeaten through 27 Serie A matches, eight points clear domestically, holding a 4–0 first-leg advantage in the Coppa Italia and fresh from eliminating Inter at San Siro. This is not a side hoping Madrid have an off night. Napoli have enough quality to actively create one.

The first rule is obvious: do not let Mbappé turn the match into a track meet. Alessandro Bastoni is now the standard-bearer of this defence, but this cannot become Bastoni versus Mbappé in forty metres of open grass. Napoli need compact distances, Buongiorno connected to him and Scott McTominay protecting the space immediately in front of the centre-backs.

That leads directly to rule two: Bellingham cannot own the pocket. Madrid are most frightening when their forward talent and midfield runners begin occupying the same spaces. McTominay does not need to follow Bellingham into the car park, but he does need to make every central reception uncomfortable. Force Madrid wider. Make the next pass predictable.

Rule three is equally important: do not turn respect into surrender. Sitting in a low block for ninety minutes at the Maradona would simply invite Madrid to keep asking questions until one answer breaks Napoli. There have to be pressing moments. There have to be spells where Paz gets on the ball, Davies attacks from his advanced role and Madrid’s defenders are forced to run toward their own goal.

Rule four is to use the striker problem as a weapon rather than solve it before kickoff. Pio Esposito has 21 goals and 11 assists. Maximilian Beier has 15 and nine and has scored four times across his last two matches. Endrick has 11 and seven while repeatedly producing in major moments. Napoli do not need to fit all three into the starting XI. They need to make Madrid deal with elite forward quality for the entire ninety minutes. Whoever begins on the bench must be viewed as ammunition, not a demotion.

And rule five: remember that this is 180 minutes. Napoli do not need to eliminate Real Madrid on March 7. They need to arrive at the Bernabéu with a tie they can still control. Recklessness at 1–1 would be every bit as dangerous as excessive caution at 0–0.

The mood inside the squad, at least publicly, should reflect exactly that balance. Pio Esposito, Napoli’s leading scorer and creator among the forwards, summed up the feeling before the biggest European test of the season: “We know who Real Madrid are. Everyone does. But we also know who we are now. We went to Milan needing a result and got it. We are not going into this tie just to see what happens.”

That quote matters because Napoli’s European season has changed. Inter was proof of concept. Madrid is validation. Nobody will call Napoli failures if a perennial Champions League powerhouse ends the run, but eliminating Madrid would permanently alter how this team is discussed outside Italy.

Madrid have the greater collection of established global superstars. Napoli have Bastoni at the heart of an elite defence, McTominay screening it, Paz developing into a genuine high-level creator, three strikers in outstanding form and a goalkeeper who just produced his defining performance of the season in Milan.
So the instruction should be simple. Respect the badge. Respect the talent. Respect the history. Then make them play Napoli anyway.
comments: “We also know who we are now.” PIO I AM READY TO RUN THROUGH A WALL.
The most important point here is the 180-minute mentality. Do not turn a good first-leg position into chaos because Madrid’s name makes everyone emotional.
Give me Bastoni against Mbappé. I am not saying I am relaxed. I am saying I want to see it.
As a neutral Madrid supporter I disagree with the suggestion that Napoli should attack at any point. Please sit very deep and never counter.
Scott’s entire evening: Jude Bellingham would like to receive the ball. Scott says no.
21G 11A and now he is talking like THAT before Madrid. Start him.
If Beier starts, Madrid deal with the hottest scorer in the squad. If Beier sits, Madrid get a 15-goal striker entering against tired legs. Good luck.
Everybody keeps saying “weapon off the bench” like Endrick has not been deciding massive matches already. The selection debate is REAL.
Respect the badge. Then make them play Napoli anyway. PUT THAT ON THE WALL.
Paz is the wildcard for me. If he can receive between their midfield and defence without getting swallowed up, this tie changes.
Nobody mentioning that Meret just survived Inter turning San Siro into a shooting gallery. Confidence matters.
My tactical plan: Bastoni stops Mbappé, Kayode becomes Cafu, Pio scores twice. Why are you people making this complicated?
This is exactly right. We are underdogs. We are not tourists. Massive difference.
The league position matters here. Napoli are not arriving desperate for this tie to validate the whole season. That should make them freer, not more cautious.
Inter was the moment we proved we can survive. Madrid is the moment we find out whether we belong.
Maradona under the lights against Real Madrid. I do not care what the ratings say. Make them uncomfortable from minute one.

articles.label: Analysis · Attack
articles.headline: Three No. 9s, One Problem: Who Does Napoli Leave Out?
articles.dek: Pio Esposito has 32 goal contributions. Beier has exploded to 15 goals and nine assists. Endrick keeps delivering in the biggest moments. Ahead of Real Madrid, Napoli’s striker problem has completely reversed.
body: There was a point earlier in this season when Napoli’s centre-forward situation looked like one of the squad’s biggest vulnerabilities. Lukaku and Højlund were gone, the options had changed, and the question was whether Napoli had enough firepower to survive a season with ambitions on every front.
That question now looks almost ridiculous.

Pio Esposito leads the attack with 21 goals and 11 assists — 32 direct goal contributions. His season has evolved beyond finishing. The recent stretch has shown a striker increasingly capable of creating for the players around him: two assists for Endrick at Lecce and the pass for Alphonso Davies that ignited the Champions League comeback at Inter.

Then there is Maximilian Beier. For much of the season he was productive without dominating the conversation. That is no longer possible. His goal at Inter was followed by one of the strangest individual performances of Napoli’s season: three penalties converted in sixteen minutes at Torino, followed by an assist for Endrick. Beier now sits at 15 goals and nine assists — 24 direct contributions — and has four goals across his last two appearances.

Endrick presents a different problem. His season line stands at 11 goals and seven assists, but his recent work has arrived when the lights have been brightest. He scored against Inter in the Champions League first leg, struck twice at Lecce, assisted Nico Paz’s decisive goal in the comeback at San Siro and then scored again in Turin. Napoli rejected enormous January offers to keep him. The decision looks increasingly important by the week.
Together, the three strikers have produced 47 goals and 27 assists: 74 direct goal contributions. More importantly, all three enter March in excellent form.

That creates the kind of selection problem managers normally enjoy. Pio has the strongest full-season case and has just received a complete rest against Torino. Beier may be the hottest scorer in the squad. Endrick has become a devastating high-pressure weapon and can change the geometry of a match immediately.

Napoli do not necessarily have to choose only one. Beier’s flexibility allows him to operate around a central striker, and the depth means one elite attacking option can be preserved for the moment a match begins to stretch. Against Real Madrid, the identity of the player coming off the bench may matter almost as much as the identity of the starter.

There is also a longer-term undertone. Federico Chiesa is expected to be missed after this season, yet the attack does not currently resemble a unit approaching a transition crisis. Instead, the next version of Napoli’s forward line may already be forming.
For most managers, choosing between three in-form strikers would constitute a problem. For Napoli, with Real Madrid arriving on March 7, it may be their greatest weapon.
comments: 21 goals. 11 assists. Thirty-two contributions. Stop overthinking this. Pio starts against Madrid.
15 and 9 while half the fanbase spent the year calling him depth. PUT SOME RESPECT ON HIS NAME.
Cool numbers. Now tell me who you want running at Madrid with twenty minutes left and tired legs. Exactly.
The real luxury is not choosing the “best” striker. It is being able to change the entire attacking profile without lowering the quality.
We started this season wondering what the hell we were going to do after losing Lukaku and Højlund. Now we are debating which elite in-form striker has to sit 😭
Four goals in two games and 24 G+A. Beier is not supporting cast anymore.
Everyone talks about Pio’s 21 goals but the 11 assists are why he is my Madrid starter. He makes the whole front line better.
Start Pio and Beier. Make Madrid deal with them for an hour. Then unleash Endrick. That is disgusting.
He scored vs Inter, brace vs Lecce, assisted Paz at San Siro, scored vs Torino. “Bench player” is doing a lot of work there.
47 goals between three strikers. SEVENTY FOUR goal contributions. We used to have a striker problem. Technically we still do 😂
As a completely neutral observer I recommend Napoli rest all three on March 7.
This is why keeping Endrick through those January bids mattered. March is where depth stops being theoretical.
Beier’s positional flexibility is the key. Pio central, Beier working around him, Endrick changing the match later is probably the cleanest solution.
Three forwards in form, eight clear in the league, 4-0 up in the Coppa tie and Madrid coming to Naples. This is what we built the squad for.
The Chiesa goodbye is going to hurt, but at least the attack does not look like it is about to fall off a cliff next season.
Imagine defending Pio for 65 minutes and seeing Endrick warming up. I would simply request substitution myself.

articles.label: Coppa Italia · Leg 1 · FT
articles.headline: Three Pens and a Funeral: Beier Buries Torino in Leg One
articles.dek: A scoreless first half turns completely absurd as Maximilian Beier converts three penalties in 16 minutes, then sets up Endrick to give Napoli a commanding 4–0 first-leg advantage.
body: For 49 minutes, almost nothing happened. Torino and Napoli reached halftime scoreless and the first leg looked destined to become a long, tense Coppa night.
Then Torino completely lost control of their own penalty area.

Napoli were awarded a penalty in the 50th minute. With Pio Esposito resting, Maximilian Beier stepped up and converted. Twelve minutes later Napoli won another penalty. Beier took that one too and made it 2–0.

Four minutes after that came the absurdity: a third Napoli penalty. Beier stepped up for the third time and completed a penalty hat trick — three spot kicks converted between the 50th and 66th minutes.

Beier was not finished. In the 86th minute, apparently tired of scoring himself, he supplied Endrick for Napoli’s fourth. The Brazilian made it 4–0 and closed a second half in which Beier had a direct hand in every goal.
The final line is ridiculous: Beier, three goals and one assist. His season total rises to 15 goals and nine assists. Endrick moves to 11 goals and seven assists.

Pio received the intended rest and Napoli leave Turin holding a massive 4–0 advantage after leg one. The tie is not over and qualification is not yet official, but Napoli could hardly have put themselves in a stronger position before the return leg.
comments: BEIER HEAT MAP: ⚪ the penalty spot. That is the entire graphic.
We have advised the defenders to stop committing crimes inside the penalty area.
Three penalties, three goals, then an assist because apparently scoring got boring. 3G 1A.
0-0 at halftime to 4-0 at full time is already stupid. THREE penalties in sixteen minutes makes it art.
Pio got the full rest and Beier handled the entire attack. Perfect night before Madrid week.
Beier finally gets tired of scoring and just hands Endrick number 11 😂
Jokes aside, converting the third penalty is not automatic. Same keeper, hat trick pressure, first-leg stakes. Beier was ice cold.
PENALTY. BEIER. PENALTY. BEIER. PENALTY. BEIER.
Could our defenders perhaps consider defending OUTSIDE the box next time.
15G 9A for Beier. We need to stop calling him supporting cast.
The best part is this leg was genuinely tense for fifty minutes and then Torino just self-destructed.
Pio rested. Endrick scores. Beier catches fire. And we take a four-goal cushion into leg two.
Torino conceded fewer goals once they stopped fouling people in the box. Tactical adjustment of the night.
Four goals, clean sheet, 4-0 aggregate lead. Not through yet — but that is a phenomenal first leg.

articles.label: Serie A · FT
articles.headline: Inter Get Their Rematch. Napoli Keep Their Eight Points.
articles.dek: Beier strikes early from a Geertruida assist, De Arrascaeta answers again, and Napoli leave the San Siro unbeaten with the title gap untouched.
body: Four days after eliminating Inter from the Champions League, Napoli returned to the San Siro with a different objective. This time there was no aggregate deficit to chase. Inter needed to cut an eight-point Serie A gap. Napoli needed to make sure they did not.
Napoli struck first in the 17th minute. Lutsharel Geertruida supplied Maximilian Beier, who finished to put the league leaders ahead and briefly push the live title gap to eleven points.

Inter found their equalizer in the 41st minute through the increasingly familiar Giorgian De Arrascaeta. After scoring twice in the Champions League first leg, he again found a way through Napoli and sent the sides into halftime level.

Napoli waited until the 70th minute before opening the cabinet: Endrick, Kevin De Bruyne and Alphonso Davies entered together. The late push did not produce a winner, but strategically Napoli had already achieved the essential objective.
The 1–1 draw moves Napoli to 65 points from 27 matches and preserves an unbeaten 19W–8D–0L Serie A record. Inter move to 57 from 27. The gap remains eight points.

Napoli therefore leave Milan after two matches in four days having eliminated Inter from Europe and denied them any ground in the title race. The rivalry week belongs to Napoli even without a second victory.
comments: Two trips to the San Siro in four days: knock them out of Europe, then refuse to give them a single point of ground in the title race. I will take that.
Inter finally scored at home against us and STILL gained nothing in the table 😭
Beier 12 goals now. Quietly having a massive season.
First recorded assist for Geertruida and it comes at San Siro. Utility man paying rent.
Can somebody PLEASE make De Arrascaeta play literally anybody else.
This was not the UCL tie. A draw here is strategically excellent: eight-point lead preserved, unbeaten run preserved.
19 wins. 8 draws. ZERO losses. Ventisette partite.
We got the rematch and the gap is still eight. Fantastic week.
First we took Europe. Then we protected the Scudetto lead. Milano trip complete.
Cool. Now Torino, Madrid twice and the rest of that March schedule. Nobody sleep.
The 70th-minute Endrick/KDB/Davies triple sub was pure menace even if it did not find the winner.
Napoli 65, Inter 57. Inter needed a win much more than Napoli did. That is the whole story.

articles.label: The Apology Thread
articles.headline: The Apology Thread: European Critics, Your Forms Are Ready
articles.dek: Receipts have been collected. The people have returned to the timeline. Some are apologizing. Others are being reminded.
body: One week ago the question was everywhere: can Napoli do it in Europe? After losing the first leg at home, the Marseille and Bodø defeats looked like evidence of a continental ceiling.
Tonight Napoli went to Inter, overturned the tie and kept a clean sheet. This is the apology desk. Please take a number.
comments: I said Napoli were a domestic bully who would fold in Milan. I am here voluntarily. I was catastrophically wrong.
I wrote that three European defeats were a pattern. They were. Napoli just broke the pattern in the hardest possible way. Apology submitted.
I questioned the second rotation before Lecce. Napoli won 2-0 there and then 2-0 here. Manager got the sequence right.
FORMALLY REQUESTING AN APOLOGY FROM EVERYONE WHO SAID THE UDINESE ROTATION KILLED THE SEASON 😭
I would like to unsubscribe from this thread.
My username is creating administrative difficulties at this time.
I wanted the $193M. I no longer wish to discuss my previous position.
Davies in the fifth minute. Put some respect on the maple leaf.
Apologize to the goalkeeper first. Three saves. Clean sheet. MOTM.
21 goals and ELEVEN assists now. He did not score tonight and still changed the tie.
The correct take: criticism before tonight was earned. Credit tonight is earned too. This was a massive European performance.
Napoli: eight points clear, unbeaten in Serie A, Coppa semifinalist, Inter eliminated from Europe. That CV looks different this morning.

articles.label: Champions League · FT
articles.headline: STAI ZITTO: Napoli Storm Milan and Throw Inter Out of Europe
articles.dek: Davies strikes after five minutes, Meret produces a Man-of-the-Match masterclass, and Nico Paz completes a 3–2 aggregate comeback.
body: Napoli asked for a European answer. They delivered one in the loudest possible way: a 2–0 win away to Inter, overturning a first-leg deficit and sending Napoli through 3–2 on aggregate.

Alphonso Davies erased Inter’s advantage after only five minutes. Starting from the wing, he drove inside the box and buried the finish after Pio Esposito supplied him. The tie was level almost immediately.

Then came the siege. Inter hit the bar, Scott McTominay cleared an effort off the line and Alex Meret produced three enormous first-half saves. Napoli reached halftime 1–0 ahead on the night and 2–2 on aggregate largely because their goalkeeper refused to let Inter back in.
The decisive moment arrived in the 76th minute. Endrick found Nico Paz and the $125 million playmaker scored the goal that flipped the tie completely: Napoli 3–2 ahead on aggregate.
Pio nearly added a third on a 90th-minute counter, striking the post, but nothing more was required. The whistle confirmed the comeback and one of Napoli’s defining performances of the season.

Meret was named Man of the Match. The clean sheet belongs to the entire defensive effort, but his interventions during Inter’s first-half barrage kept the comeback alive long enough for Paz to finish it.

The European criticism had become legitimate after defeats to Marseille, Bodø/Glimt and Inter in the first leg. Napoli did not answer it with an argument. They answered it by going to Inter and winning 2–0.
comments: STAI ZITTO CAZZO. Tutti quanti. Napoli avanti.
WHERE IS THE DOMESTIC GIANT EUROPEAN QUESTION MARK ARTICLE NOW 😭😭😭
Three massive saves while Inter were throwing the kitchen sink at us. MAN OF THE MATCH.
This is the answer. Not because the earlier criticism was unfair — because Napoli responded to it on the pitch.
Pio assist after five minutes and hits the post at 90. 21G 11A. Complete forward.
Endrick scores in leg one and assists the aggregate winner in leg two. Twenty-one years old.
ALPHONSO DAVIES YOU BEAUTIFUL CANADIAN MAN 🇨🇦
$125M NICO PAZ. THAT IS WHAT THE MONEY WAS FOR.
Eight clear in Serie A and now Inter eliminated from Europe. The entire rivalry shifted tonight.
I criticized the European performances. I was right to. Tonight I apologize. That was immense.

articles.label: Man of the Match
articles.headline: The Wall in Milan: Meret Kept the Comeback Alive
articles.dek: Three huge saves during Inter’s first-half barrage made Alex Meret the official Man of the Match in Napoli’s defining European win.
body: The goals will belong to Davies and Paz. The qualification might belong to Alex Meret.

With Napoli 1–0 ahead on the night but only level on aggregate, Inter unleashed a barrage. They hit the bar. McTominay cleared one off the line. And three times, Meret produced the kind of save that changes a knockout tie.
Napoli were not comfortable. They were surviving. Meret gave them the time required to turn survival into control and, eventually, into a famous qualification.

His official Man-of-the-Match award is more than a footnote. With young goalkeeper Peacock recently secured on a long-term contract, Meret delivered a reminder on the biggest available stage: the present still belongs to him.
comments: PUT THE MOTM TROPHY ON THE PLANE NEXT TO HIM.
Without Meret, Paz never gets the opportunity to score the winner. Simple as that.
Peacock is the future. Meret just reminded everybody who owns the shirt right now.

articles.label: Serie A · FT
articles.headline: Endrick Double Punishes Lecce as Napoli Restore Eight-Point Lead
articles.dek: A rotated Napoli side handles its business while Juventus stun Inter 2–0. Endrick scores twice from Pio Esposito assists and Napoli remain unbeaten.
body: Napoli could hardly have scripted a better response between the two Inter ties. A rotated side beat Lecce 2–0 away, Endrick scored both goals, Pio Esposito created both, and news from elsewhere made the result even more valuable: Juventus beat Inter 2–0.

The breakthrough arrived in the 55th minute on the counter. Pio released Endrick and the Brazilian finished for 1–0. Twenty minutes later the same partnership struck again, Pio supplying Endrick for his second of the afternoon and Napoli’s insurance goal.

The brace takes Endrick to 10 goals in Napoli’s running season totals. Pio remains on 21 goals but jumps to 10 assists, another reminder that Napoli’s leading scorer has become a major creator as well.
Napoli move to 64 points from 26 Serie A matches with a 19W–7D–0L record. Inter remain on 56 after losing 2–0 to Juventus, meaning the gap expands from five points to eight.

Most importantly, the rotation worked this time. Napoli collected all three points without needing a desperate late rescue and can now turn completely toward the Champions League return leg. Inter lead the tie 2–1, but arrive after a domestic defeat while Napoli arrive with Endrick and Pio combining for both goals in a clean-sheet victory.
comments: JUVE 2 INTER 0. NAPOLI +8. Grazie per il favore, adesso pensiamo a Milano.
Juventus accidentally helping our Scudetto charge after trying to buy half our attack 😭
Three goals in two matches. Ten on the season. Maybe rejecting those insane bids was a decent idea.
21 goals AND 10 assists. Two assists today. Pio is becoming a complete monster.
This is what the Udinese rotation was supposed to look like: manage minutes, win anyway, move on.
Napoli 64, Inter 56. Eight clear and still unbeaten after 26. The title picture changed significantly today.
Adesso Milano. Un gol pareggia la qualificazione. Andiamo.

articles.label: Player Focus
articles.headline: $193 Million? Napoli Said No. Endrick Is Starting to Explain Why.
articles.dek: Three goals in two matches have transformed Endrick from prized project into Napoli’s hottest attacker on the eve of the biggest match of the season.
body: Deadline day brought absurd numbers. Juventus offered around $188 million. RB Leipzig followed with the same neighborhood of money. Bergamo pushed to $193.4 million. Napoli rejected every approach for Endrick.

Now the timing looks prophetic. Endrick scored Napoli’s only goal in the 2–1 Champions League first-leg defeat to Inter, blasting Beier’s pass into the top-left corner under enormous pressure. Five days later, he scored twice at Lecce.
That is three goals across two matches and 10 goals in the running season totals. More importantly, the performances are arriving precisely as Napoli’s season reaches its sharpest pressure point.

Pio Esposito remains the attacking reference point, but Lecce showed why the partnership can be more than a competition for goals. Pio assisted both Endrick finishes, moving to 21 goals and 10 assists himself.

Napoli now travel to Inter one goal down on aggregate with its two young forwards arriving in form. The transfer window is closed. The bids are history. The question is no longer what Endrick might be worth. It is what he can do in Milan.
comments: KEEP THE RECEIPTS. $193.4M rejected and now he is cooking right before Milan.
This is why you do not sell elite young talent when you are trying to build something.
Juventus: 188m for Endrick. Napoli: no. Juventus five minutes later: fine we will just beat Inter for you 😂
Do not miss the other half of this story. Pio assisted BOTH. 21 and 10 is ridiculous.
Endrick scored in Leg 1. Give him the stage again in Leg 2.

articles.label: Champions League · FT
articles.headline: The Noise Is Real Now: Inter Win at the Maradona
articles.dek: Napoli rested for this night, answered an early blow through Endrick, then fell to a De Arrascaeta brace. The European questions are no longer background noise.
body: This was supposed to be the night Napoli answered Europe. Instead, Inter left the Maradona with a 2–1 first-leg advantage and the loudest criticism of the season now has evidence behind it.

Giorgian De Arrascaeta struck after only three minutes, immediately dragging Marseille and Bodø/Glimt back into the conversation. Napoli did respond. In the 31st minute Maximilian Beier found Endrick, who blasted his finish into the top-left corner for 1–1 and briefly changed the temperature inside the stadium.
But Napoli never found the second breakthrough. De Arrascaeta scored again in the 63rd minute and Inter protected the lead through the final whistle.

The context makes the defeat sting more. Napoli deliberately rotated in the 0–0 league draw at Udinese three days earlier, accepting dropped points to preserve the first-choice core for this match. Inter won 2–0 in their league fixture, cut Napoli’s Serie A lead from seven points to five, and then beat the rested Napoli side in Naples.

The tie is not close to finished. Napoli travel to Inter on February 23 needing only one goal to erase the aggregate deficit. But the burden has shifted. Napoli remain unbeaten and first in Serie A; in Europe, they have now lost to Marseille, Bodø/Glimt and Inter in their recent continental run.

Endrick’s goal is the positive. The 21-year-old delivered under genuine pressure and moves to eight goals in Napoli’s running totals. Beier’s assist takes him to eight. The rest of the squad now has eight days, with Lecce in between, to decide whether this first leg becomes another European warning or the setup for a comeback.
comments: Abbiamo riposato a Udine PER QUESTA PARTITA. E perdiamo in casa. Le critiche sono meritate.
The tie is 2-1, not 5-0. But three recent European defeats is officially a pattern worth discussing.
Dropped points at Udinese to save the legs and De Arrascaeta still walked into our house and scored TWICE 😭
Calma. Un gol a Milano pareggia tutto. Non è finita.
Inter gained two league points on Napoli and then won the first leg in Naples. That is a brutal four-day swing.
Everybody can argue about Europe tomorrow. Tonight give Endrick his credit. That finish was enormous.
Need Pio in the second leg. Twenty-one goals this season and this is exactly the stage where the number nine has to appear.
Marseille 3-0. Bodø 2-1. Inter 2-1. You cannot keep calling every European loss an exception.
Still five clear. Still unbeaten in Serie A. Still only one down on aggregate. Season is alive everywhere.
The manager asked us to trust the Udinese rotation. Fine. Now the second leg has become the receipt.
Non mollare. A Milano andiamo per vincere.
Beier keeps creating in big moments. 11 goals and 8 assists now. He has earned his place in the return leg.

articles.label: Pressure
articles.headline: Domestic Giant, European Question Mark
articles.dek: Napoli’s league season remains extraordinary. That is exactly why the continental record is becoming impossible to ignore.
body: There are two Napoli teams living inside the same season. One is 18–7–0 in Serie A, five points clear of Inter and still unbeaten after 25 matches. The other has recently lost European matches to Marseille, Bodø/Glimt and now Inter at home.

Both things can be true. The manager deserves enormous credit for the domestic campaign, squad development and the emergence of Pio Esposito, Beier, Endrick and Paz. He also deserves scrutiny for a European side that has repeatedly failed to reproduce its league authority.

The Udinese decision raises the stakes rather than settling the argument. Napoli consciously rotated and drew 0–0 to arrive fresh for Inter. That is a defensible strategic choice. But once Inter won the first leg, the cost became part of the evaluation.

Nothing is decided. A one-goal deficit is entirely recoverable and a comeback in Milan would reverse the mood instantly. That is what makes February 23 so significant: it is no longer simply a knockout match. It is a referendum on the one unresolved weakness of an otherwise exceptional season.
comments: This is the fair framing. Nobody should pretend 18-7-0 is bad management, but nobody should ignore Europe either.
Vinci a Milano e questa discussione sparisce in novanta minuti.
The hot seat is not hot. The European seat, however, is currently on fire 😂
Judge the tie after the second leg. One goal is nothing.
The concern is not one Inter loss. It is Marseille plus Bodø plus Inter. That is the whole point.

articles.label: Serie A · FT
articles.headline: Rotation Stalls in Udine — Now All Eyes Turn to Inter
articles.dek: A deliberately rotated Napoli side creates little in a goalless draw. Inter win 2–0 elsewhere, cutting the Serie A lead to five points before the Champions League showdown.
body: Napoli’s planned rotation produced exactly the kind of quiet afternoon that was always possible: a 0–0 draw away to Udinese, preserving the unbeaten Serie A record but surrendering two points in the title race.

With the Champions League knockout playoff first leg against Inter only three days away, Napoli prioritized freshness. The match never really opened up. Federico Chiesa produced the clearest Napoli opportunity of the first half, but halftime arrived scoreless.
Mikey Moore had Napoli’s best late opening, getting a chance from close range only to be denied by the Udinese goalkeeper. There was no breakthrough and the match finished 0–0.

The wider consequence arrived elsewhere. Inter won 2–0, moving to 56 points and reducing Napoli’s lead from seven points to five. Napoli remain unbeaten at 18W–7D–0L and move to 61 points from 25 league matches.

The trade-off was intentional: Napoli sacrificed some attacking sharpness in Udine to protect the core for Europe. Now that decision gets judged immediately. Inter come to the Maradona on February 15 for the first leg of the Champions League knockout playoff.
Napoli have been outstanding domestically but vulnerable in Europe after defeats to Marseille and Bodø/Glimt. The rested first-choice side now has the stage it was preserved for.
comments: Not pretty, but this was the planned rotation. The problem is Inter did their job and the gap is back to five.
Sessantuno punti, ancora imbattuti. Adesso però basta calcoli: contro l’Inter voglio il Napoli vero.
We rested everybody for Inter so those boys better come out of the tunnel breathing fire 😭
Moore nearly stole it late. Take the point, take the fresh legs, move on.
The cost is real: seven-point lead becomes five. That makes the three Inter matches even more enormous.
If Napoli eliminate Inter in Europe nobody remembers this 0-0. If not, people will absolutely revisit the rotation decision.
18-7-0. Still no league loss. Now give me the full-strength XI at the Maradona.

articles.label: Serie A · FT
articles.headline: Pio Misses, Steps Up Again, and Napoli Hold Off Fiorentina
articles.dek: Nico Paz opens the scoring, Pio Esposito produces a Goal of the Year candidate and then answers his own penalty miss as unbeaten Napoli move to 60 points.
body: Napoli preserved their unbeaten Serie A season with a dramatic 3–2 home victory over Fiorentina, moving to 60 points from 24 matches and stretching their lead over Inter to seven points after the latest round.

Nico Paz opened the scoring in the 15th minute. Scott McTominay played him in, Paz saw his first effort stopped and then followed his own rebound to make it 1–0. Albert Guðmundsson answered for Fiorentina in the 23rd minute.

The moment of the night arrived in the 58th minute. Michael Kayode delivered an extraordinary cross from around the halfway line and Pio Esposito ran onto it before striking first time. The finish put Napoli 2–1 ahead and stands as an immediate Goal of the Year candidate.

Pio then had the chance to settle the match from the penalty spot in the 70th minute but missed. When Napoli won another penalty in the 87th, he took responsibility again. This time he scored, completing his brace and reaching 21 goals in Napoli’s running season totals.
Guðmundsson converted a Fiorentina penalty one minute later to make it 3–2, but the final whistle arrived before the visitors could complete the comeback. Napoli leave the night 18W–6D–0L in Serie A.

Attention now turns to squad management. Udinese is next on February 12, with Napoli planning rotation to preserve the first-choice core for the Champions League knockout playoff first leg against Inter on February 15.
comments: Pio missing one penalty and demanding the second is striker mentality. The halfway-line delivery from Kayode was outrageous too.
VENTUNO GOL. Sbaglia il rigore e si ripresenta dal dischetto. Questo ragazzo non ha paura.
Kayode crossed that thing from another postal code and Pio hit it first time 😭
18 vittorie, 6 pareggi, ZERO sconfitte. Sessanta punti. Sempre Napoli.
Inter are now seven points back after 24 matches. The February pressure has shifted heavily onto them.
That 58th-minute goal needs to be in every end-of-season montage.
Paz keeps producing. McTominay with the pass, rebound, goal. Then Pio takes over.
Assist of the season candidate. From the centre line. Perfect weight. Perfect run.
Miss at 70. Ball back in his hands at 87. Goal. That tells you everything.
Now rotate at Udinese. Inter is three days later and that UCL tie is the priority.

articles.label: Coppa Italia · Quarterfinal
articles.headline: Juan Jesus Gets His Redemption as Napoli Reach Coppa Semifinal
articles.dek: Chiesa scores early, Beier creates both goals and Nico Paz finishes the counter after a crucial Juan Jesus tackle as Napoli beat Sassuolo 2–0.
body: Napoli are through to the Coppa Italia semifinal after a 2–0 quarterfinal victory over Sassuolo, with a heavily rotated side producing one of the season’s more unlikely redemption stories.

Federico Chiesa opened the scoring in the eighth minute, finishing a move created by Maximilian Beier. After a transfer window in which Chiesa wanted a move but ultimately stayed, his response was immediate: a goal in his first knockout assignment after the deadline.

Napoli led 1–0 at halftime. Juan Jesus, handed a rare start, survived Sassuolo pressure and then produced the defining defensive intervention of the second half. In the 70th minute he made a crucial tackle inside the Napoli box following a Sassuolo corner. Napoli broke immediately from the recovery.

At the other end, Beier supplied his second assist of the night and Nico Paz blasted home the counterattack to make it 2–0. The sequence turned a dangerous Sassuolo set piece into the goal that effectively killed the quarterfinal.
Juan Jesus, exhausted after his rare outing, was replaced by Alessandro Buongiorno in the 78th minute with the clean sheet intact. Napoli saw out the remainder without conceding.

Beier finished with two assists, Chiesa and Paz supplied the goals, and Napoli advanced to the Coppa Italia semifinal. For Juan Jesus, the night became something more: given one start in a rotated side, he delivered a match-defining tackle when Napoli needed it.
comments: Juan Jesus deserves the headline tonight. That tackle at 1–0 prevents a real chance and Napoli score on the counter seconds later. Match-defining sequence.
JUAN JESUS REDENZIONE. Gli abbiamo dato una partita e ci ha portato in semifinale 😂
Juan Jesus asked for ONE start and somehow turned it into a redemption movie 😭
Quel tackle al 70’ vale quasi come un gol. Recupero di Juan Jesus, contropiede, Paz, 2-0.
The funniest part is him coming off at 78 completely out of gas after saving the day. He emptied the tank.
I was terrified seeing Juan Jesus on the quarterfinal team sheet. Fair play. Clean sheet intact when he left and a huge tackle.
This is why squad players matter. Juan Jesus barely plays, gets called, and produces the defensive moment that settles a knockout game.
Give the man his flowers. No irony. He did exactly what was asked of him tonight.
From “one start” to Napoli cult hero for 78 minutes. Football makes absolutely no sense 😂
Al 78’ non aveva più benzina. Esce Juan Jesus, entra Buongiorno, stadio in piedi. Bellissimo.
I need the clip of that tackle framed. The Juan Jesus Game is canon now.
Beier gets the assist and Paz gets the goal, but the second goal begins with Juan Jesus reading the corner perfectly. Do not lose that detail.

articles.label: Window Closed
articles.headline: Napoli Slam the Door: Stars Stay as Deadline Window Closes
articles.dek: Endrick stays. Beier stays. Chiesa stays. Napoli reject a barrage of enormous late bids and finish the window without a senior departure, while three promoted prospects leave on development loans.
body: Napoli have closed the transfer window with the senior squad intact, refusing a remarkable series of deadline-day approaches as the club prepares for a Scudetto race and Champions League knockout campaign.

Endrick attracted three enormous bids. Juventus offered $188 million, RB Leipzig matched that $188 million figure, and Bergamo Calcio then raised the stakes to $193.4 million. Napoli rejected all three approaches.

Juventus also returned with a separate $188.9 million offer for Maximilian Beier. That proposal was rejected as well. Napoli were unwilling to strengthen a domestic rival and equally unwilling to lose a major attacking piece with the window closing.
Federico Chiesa also remains a Napoli player. Despite his desire to leave and Fiorentina’s earlier $36.2 million approach, no senior transfer was completed before the deadline.

The only outgoing business involved development loans. Goalkeeper O. Burnett left on a two-year loan, while centre-back G. Ricci and right midfielder C. Brun secured six-month loans after their academy promotions.

The final message from the window is unmistakable: Napoli chose continuity. With a five-point Serie A lead, an unbeaten domestic record and a Champions League knockout playoff against Inter ahead, the club resisted extraordinary money rather than break apart the squad for the decisive months of the season.
comments: Three bids for Endrick, another monster bid for Beier, and nobody leaves. Napoli chose the season over the balance sheet.
Mercato chiuso. Endrick resta. Beier resta. Chiesa resta. Adesso andiamo a vincere.
The important part is not just the money rejected. It is that Napoli enter February with the senior squad intact.
Napoli spent deadline day rejecting GDP-sized offers and then closed the fax machine 😭
La società ha mandato un messaggio chiarissimo: questa squadra non si smonta a febbraio.
Burnett, Ricci and Brun get development moves. Everyone we need for the run-in stays. Perfect window ending.
Endrick drew $188m from Juventus, $188m from Leipzig and $193.4m from Bergamo. Napoli declined every bid.
Juventus tried Endrick, then Beier. The answer never changed.
Chiesa staying after all that is another subplot. Now everyone has to lock in until summer.
Five points clear, Inter waiting in Europe, and the squad survives deadline day untouched. Exactly what was needed.

articles.label: Serie A
articles.headline: Beier Off the Bench to Deliver Napoli in Bologna
articles.dek: A rotated Napoli side grinds out a 1–0 league win through substitute Maximilian Beier — then sees title rival Inter drop points in a 1–1 draw with Como.
body: Napoli left Bologna with three points after a tight 1–0 victory, finding the decisive moment through the bench rather than the starting XI.

With the schedule beginning to tighten, Napoli rotated the side but kept enough senior quality on the pitch to stay in the contest. The match remained goalless through halftime before Maximilian Beier was introduced as a substitute.

The change paid off in the 53rd minute. Beier broke the deadlock to put Napoli 1–0 ahead, providing the only goal of the match and another important contribution in a season where Napoli’s attacking depth continues to matter.
There was no second goal, but there did not need to be. Napoli protected the advantage through full time and took a valuable Serie A win from a match that demanded patience rather than spectacle.

Then came another result of immediate importance to the title race: Inter were held 1–1 by Como. Napoli took all three points in Bologna while their principal Scudetto rival dropped two, increasing the value of an otherwise narrow victory.

That swing arrives with February bringing the rivalry directly onto the pitch. Napoli and Inter are scheduled to meet three times in 13 days — twice in the Champions League knockout playoff and then again in Serie A. Every point banked before that stretch matters.
Beier’s intervention was the difference in Bologna: summoned from the bench, on the scoresheet, and responsible for all three points.
comments: Rotated team, away match, clean sheet, three points — and Inter drop two. That is an excellent league day.
Comes off the bench and just solves the problem. Massive contribution.
Non bella, ma pesantissima. Noi vinciamo e l’Inter pareggia: giornata enorme.
The February schedule is brutal. Winning while rotating and seeing Inter draw is exactly what Napoli needed.
One-nil away and Inter held by Como. Take that all day.
Beier entered the chat, scored, refused to elaborate, then Como did us a favour 😭
These are the weekends that can quietly decide a title race.

articles.label: Champions League
articles.headline: Defeat in Bodø, but Napoli Secure Knockout Playoff Place
articles.dek: Evjen scores twice as Bodø/Glimt beat Napoli 2–1, but the night still ends with confirmation that Napoli have qualified for a place in the Champions League knockout playoffs.
body: Napoli left Bodø with a 2–1 defeat, but also with their European season guaranteed to continue after securing a place in the Champions League knockout playoffs.
Bodø/Glimt struck first in the 15th minute through Evjen. Napoli nearly produced an immediate response three minutes later when Pio Esposito was denied by the goalkeeper.

The equaliser arrived in the 38th minute. Maximilian Beier supplied Pio, who finished to make it 1–1 and continue his run of important contributions for Napoli. Beier then had a chance to turn the match completely before halftime, breaking through on the counter in the 44th minute only to be denied from close range.

Napoli went into the interval level and with reason to believe the match had shifted in their direction, but Evjen struck again in the 57th minute to restore Bodø/Glimt’s lead. Napoli could not find another reply and the match finished 2–1.

The performance and result will frustrate a Napoli side that created enough opportunities to take more from the night. It also follows the difficult defeat in Marseille, leaving questions about Napoli’s recent European form even as their domestic campaign remains strong.

There was, however, one significant piece of good news: Napoli have officially secured a place in the Champions League knockout playoffs. The route through Europe has become harder than the club would have wanted, but it remains open.
For Napoli, that distinction matters. This was a defeat, not an elimination. The next European assignment will carry knockout consequences.

articles.label: Academy
articles.headline: Three Get the Call: Napoli Promote Burnett, Ricci and Brun
articles.dek: With the January window entering its final seven days, Napoli have moved three 18-year-olds into the senior ranks as the club turns academy progress into the next stage of development.
body: Napoli have promoted goalkeeper O. Burnett, centre-back G. Ricci and right midfielder C. Brun from the youth academy, giving three 18-year-old prospects their first place in the senior setup during the closing week of the January transfer window.

The promotions are developmental rather than a sudden reshaping of the first team. Burnett arrives at 64 OVR with an 81–87 potential range, Ricci at 65 OVR with a 75–81 range, and Brun at 61 OVR with a 79–85 range. Napoli’s next task is to find the right senior minutes for each player, with loan moves a natural possibility while the window remains open.

Burnett joins an unusually deep young goalkeeping pipeline already containing 19-year-old Peacock and 17-year-old Lawton, who is developing on loan. His promotion gives Napoli another prospect to manage carefully behind established starter Alex Meret.

Ricci is the most senior-ready of the three by current rating, although Napoli’s elite centre-back depth means his route to immediate first-team football is narrow. A productive loan could establish whether he develops into a future squad option or a valuable academy-produced asset.

Brun represents the higher-upside attacking bet. The 18-year-old right midfielder is still some distance from Napoli’s senior attacking level, but promotion allows the club to test his development against professional opposition rather than leaving him exclusively in academy football.

The decision also underlines a broader shift in Napoli’s project. The senior side is fighting at the top of Serie A while a second layer of talent is emerging beneath it: players already developing on loan, three new graduates entering the senior system, and high-ceiling academy prospects such as E. Rossetti, S. Vitale, Y. Tran and F. Freitas still being allowed to develop without being rushed.
For Burnett, Ricci and Brun, promotion is not the finish line. It is the point at which academy promise becomes a professional development decision.
comments: This is exactly what I want to see. Do not just collect academy prospects — give them a pathway.
The important part now is minutes. Promotion followed by six months on the bench would defeat the purpose.
Burnett, Peacock and Lawton all developing at once. The goalkeeper succession battle could get very interesting.
Three academy kids getting the call while we are fighting for the title. That says a lot about how healthy the project is.
Find Brun a club that will actually play him every week and let us see what we have.
Ricci at 65 is already useful as an asset even if the first-team CB room is basically impossible to crack right now.
Burnett, Ricci e Brun promossi. Il vivaio deve avere una strada vera verso il calcio dei grandi.
Imagine getting the call and then looking at Bastoni and Buongiorno ahead of you. Welcome to senior football, Ricci 😭
Rossetti and the other high-potential kids staying in the academy is just as important. Promote when it makes sense, not because we can.

articles.label: Serie A
articles.headline: Napoli Respond in Style: Endrick and Pio Shine in 3–0 Win Over Como
articles.dek: Napoli answer the difficult night in Marseille with a controlled 3–0 league win. De Bruyne opened the scoring before Endrick and Pio Esposito each finished with a goal and an assist.
body: Napoli produced the response they needed after the Champions League defeat in Marseille, beating Como 3–0 in a composed Serie A performance.
Kevin De Bruyne opened the scoring in the 40th minute after an assist from Scott McTominay, giving Napoli a deserved 1–0 lead at halftime.
De Bruyne, still managing fatigue from the disrupted Marseille trip, was replaced by Nico Paz at the interval.
Napoli doubled the lead in the 50th minute when Pio Esposito played Endrick through and the Brazilian finished for 2–0.
The pair combined again in the 78th minute with the roles reversed: Endrick supplied the assist and Pio Esposito scored Napoli’s third.
Pio and Endrick therefore finished with one goal and one assist each, while De Bruyne scored and McTominay registered an assist.
Geertruida delivered an excellent defensive performance at left back, repeatedly cutting out Como attacks, while Bastoni also produced an important early block and Meret kept the clean sheet.
Inter’s dropped points mean Napoli finish the match three points clear of their title rivals at the top of Serie A.

articles.label: Champions League
articles.headline: Exhausted Napoli Fall 3–0 in Marseille After Brutal Night
articles.dek: Napoli held Marseille scoreless through halftime despite arriving badly depleted for energy, but the resistance broke in the second half as the hosts scored three times.
body: Napoli’s push for a Champions League top-eight place took a major hit with a 3–0 defeat away to Marseille.

The squad entered the match in extraordinary circumstances after fireworks outside the team hotel left almost the entire group badly fatigued. Kevin De Bruyne and Alphonso Davies were unavailable, while only Bastoni and Marin entered the match at full stamina.

Napoli responded by sitting deep and conserving energy. Meret made several important saves, Bastoni produced an early block and Marin helped hold the defensive line together as the visitors reached halftime at 0–0.

Marseille increased the pressure after the interval. They hit the post and forced another major save from Meret before finally opening the scoring. Højbjerg later made it 2–0 and Marseille added a third before full time.

The scoreline was heavy, but the physical condition of the squad shaped the entire match. Napoli now have to recover quickly with Como next in Serie A before Bodø/Glimt and Bologna complete a demanding run of fixtures.

articles.label: Italy
articles.headline: Italy Selection Hit by Tonali and Orsolini Injuries
articles.dek: Sandro Tonali and Riccardo Orsolini are unavailable through injury, forcing changes to Italy’s national-team selection.
body: Italy’s latest national-team selection has been hit by two injury absences, with Sandro Tonali and Riccardo Orsolini unavailable.
The losses remove two experienced options from the group and force the coaching staff to adjust the squad ahead of the upcoming international fixtures.
Tonali’s absence changes the midfield picture, while Orsolini being ruled out reduces Italy’s options in the wide attacking areas.
Attention now turns to how the squad reshuffles and which players receive larger roles during the international window.

articles.label: Serie A
articles.headline: Napoli Fight Back to Beat Juventus 2–1 and Go Top of Serie A
articles.dek: Jonathan David put Juventus ahead before Beier levelled for Napoli. Pio Esposito then drew the second-half penalty and scored it himself to complete the comeback, while Inter’s dropped points sent Napoli top on 51.
body: Napoli came from behind in Turin to beat Juventus 2–1 and reclaim first place in Serie A.
Jonathan David opened the scoring for Juventus in the 29th minute, but Napoli responded before halftime when Maximilian Beier scored the equalizer in the 37th minute.
Napoli completed the turnaround in the 57th minute after Pio Esposito drew a penalty. Pio took the spot kick himself and converted it to make it 2–1.
The match had chances at both ends. Di Gregorio denied Nico Paz, Meret saved from Kenan Yildiz, and David also struck the post before missing the rebound.
Napoli used the bench to manage the closing stages, with Endrick and Stach replacing Paz and De Bruyne, Lang coming on for Davies, and Di Lorenzo replacing Kayode.

The result became even bigger after Inter dropped points. Napoli now sit top of Serie A on 51 points, one ahead of Inter on 50. Milan are on 39 points from 20 matches, Roma 38 from 20, Lazio 37 from 20, Atalanta 36 from 20, and Juventus 34 from 21.
A comeback win away to Juventus, combined with Inter’s slip, puts Napoli back at the summit at a crucial point in the title race.

articles.label: Serie A
articles.headline: Napoli Beat Milan and Go Top as Inter Stumble
articles.dek: Beier and Esposito deliver a 2–1 win at Milan, Bologna beat Inter, and Napoli finish the round first in Serie A on 44 points.
body: Napoli are top of Serie A after a huge swing at the summit. A 2–1 away win over AC Milan, combined with Inter’s defeat to Bologna, moves Stefan Saladino’s side into first place on 44 points.

Maximilian Beier opened the scoring in the 18th minute from Pio Esposito before Esposito reacted first to a Maignan spill in the 23rd for his 10th league goal of the campaign. Milan pulled one back through Jimenez after the break, but Napoli managed the closing stages to secure all three points.

The result was particularly significant after the Supercoppa final defeat to Inter only two days earlier. With fatigue forcing careful rotation, Napoli responded immediately in the league and turned a two-point deficit to Inter into a one-point lead.
The table now reads Napoli 44, Inter 43, Milan 39, Roma 38, with Lazio and Juventus both on 34. January remains congested, but Napoli now have the position everyone else wants.

articles.label: Supercoppa Final
articles.headline: Napoli Fall Short as Inter Lift the Supercoppa
articles.dek: A heavily rotated Napoli side fought back through Nico Paz and pushed Inter to the final whistle, but a 2–1 defeat leaves the first trophy of the project just out of reach.
body: Inter are Supercoppa champions after beating Napoli 2–1 in a final shaped by fixture congestion, early pressure and a furious late Napoli response.

With the squad still carrying fatigue from the semifinal and AC Milan waiting just two days later, Stefan Saladino was forced into heavy rotation. Inter took control early and opened the scoring in the 17th minute before doubling the advantage in the 50th.

Napoli refused to fold. Nico Paz pulled one back in the 71st minute from Scott McTominay, and the closing stages became a siege. Federico Chiesa beat Dimarco and struck the post, Alphonso Davies had an effort blocked, and Paz plus Pio Esposito were both denied in a frantic final sequence.
The equalizer never came. Inter took the trophy.

articles.label: Manager of the Month
articles.headline: Saladino Named Manager of the Month After Napoli’s December Surge
articles.dek: Napoli’s December performances have earned manager Stefan Saladino the Manager of the Month award as the club carries its momentum into a Supercoppa final against Inter.
body: Stefan Saladino has been named Manager of the Month for December after a run of performances that kept Napoli firmly in the title fight and pushed the club into the Supercoppa final.
The award arrives at the start of a punishing January. Napoli’s next match is now the Supercoppa final against Inter on January 3, after the original January 2 league fixture against Monza was moved.

Monza will instead visit on January 12. The revised calendar leaves Napoli facing Inter for silverware, Milan away, Empoli away, Monza at home and Juventus at home in a 13-day stretch before two Champions League away dates later in the month.
The recognition belongs to December. The challenge now is carrying that form through the most congested stretch of the season.
comments: Manager of the Month in December, Supercoppa final in January. Keep the standards exactly where they are.
Deserved. December felt like the month this team stopped looking like a project and started looking like a contender.
The award is nice. Now the real test is managing Inter, Milan, Empoli, Monza and Juventus without running the squad into the ground.
I would like the record to show that I have temporarily suspended my agenda. Congratulations, mister.
Manager of the Month and immediately handed this January schedule. Football has a sense of humour.
The biggest improvement has been control. Napoli are finding different ways to win instead of needing the same game every week.
Recognition earned in December. Now go turn it into silverware against Inter.
This is where the full squad has to justify itself. The manager got the award; January is going to test every rotation decision.
Frame the award, then hide it until after the Supercoppa final. We have business to do.
Whatever happens next, December was excellent. The team looks confident and the manager deserves credit for it.
Imagine winning Manager of the Month and your prize is this January fixture list.
The award matters because it reflects a run, not one result. Napoli have built real momentum going into the final.

articles.label: Serie A
articles.headline: Beier Breaks Roma, Napoli’s Back Line Does the Rest
articles.dek: Maximilian Beier struck in the 50th minute from Scott McTominay’s pass, while Meret, Bastoni, Buongiorno and the Napoli defence delivered a statement clean sheet.
body: Napoli went to Roma needing the kind of performance title races eventually demand: patient when the match was uncomfortable, ruthless when the opening arrived, and disciplined enough to protect a one-goal lead.

Roma carried the early threat. They hit the crossbar from a corner in the fifth minute and forced Alex Meret into important saves, but Alessandro Bastoni and Alessandro Buongiorno repeatedly shut down the second phase. Napoli bent without breaking.
The breakthrough arrived five minutes after halftime. Scott McTominay found Maximilian Beier, and Beier supplied the finish for a 1–0 lead.

From there the match became a defensive examination. Bastoni was immense, Buongiorno blocked everything in reach, and Meret completed an exceptional clean sheet as Roma searched for an equaliser that never came.

Napoli saw out the final stages without panic. It was not a rout. It was something more useful in December: a grown-up away win in a major league fixture, with Juventus and the Supercoppa waiting next.

articles.label: AZZURRI DEBATE · Matteo Rinaldi
articles.headline: Three World Cups Missed. Italy Are Top of Their EURO Group. Can Saladino Actually Turn This Around?
articles.dek: The trauma has not disappeared, but the early evidence is finally moving in the right direction: Italy lead their EURO qualifying group and have just come through three logged internationals without conceding.
body: Italian football has earned its distrust. Three consecutive World Cups missed in this universe cannot be washed away by a promising autumn, a fashionable tactical idea or a friendly victory.
That is the burden Stefan Saladino inherited. Italy are not merely trying to qualify for another tournament. They are trying to convince a country that qualification can become normal again.
